meta.formatNotes: ISAT(International Student Admissions Test)는 ACER(호주교육연구원)가 주관하며, 호주 등 의대·보건계열에서 국제학생 선발에 사용한다. 공식 안내(isat.acer.org/preparation): 총 100문항 객관식, 시험 시간 3시간(180분), 각 문항은 4개 또는 5개의 선택지 중 정답 1개, 모든 문항 배점 동일, 오답 감점 없음. 특정 교과 지식을 요구하지 않는 범교과(cross-curricular) 시험이며, 자극 자료(지문·표·그래프)를 공유하는 문항 묶음(unit) 형태로 출제되고, 추론·논리적 연역·판단 형성 능력을 측정한다. Next/Back 버튼으로 문항 이동, 100번 이후 검토 화면 제공. 공식 연습 자료는 Candidate Information Booklet(무료, 예시 문항 포함)과 유료 Practice Test 1·2(각 시험 절반 분량). 영역: 비판적 추론(Critical Reasoning, 인문·사회과학 소재의 지문을 이해·분석하고 결론 도출·논증 평가)과 정량적 추론(Quantitative Reasoning, 수학·과학 소재의 표·그래프·도표 해석과 수학적 문제 해결)이며, 사설 안내 사이트들에 따르면 CR 약 50문항, QR 약 50문항이 별도 구획 없이 섞여 출제된다(시험 중간에 50문항 완료를 권장). 계산기는 반입 금지 물품으로 안내되며, 메모는 지울 수 있는 화이트보드 또는 A4 용지 2장으로 한다. 결과는 Statement of Results(PDF)로 발급되며 유효기간 2년, 재응시는 12개월에 1회. 본 문제은행은 4지선다로 구성했다(공식 4~5지 범위 내). 문항당 평균 시간은 180분/100문항 = 약 108초이며, timeSec은 이를 기준으로 난이도·지문 길이에 따라 조정했다. 모든 지문·수치·선택지는 공식 및 사설 문항을 참고하지 않고 새로 작성한 창작 문항이다. 출처: https://isat.acer.org/preparation , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Student_Admissions_Test , https://www.frasersmedical.com/blogs/what-is-the-isat-test , https://www.pickmyuni.com/exams/australian-admission-exams/isat , https://icon-plus.com/articles/mastering-the-isat-your-ultimate-guide-to-test-success

review.method: 출제와 별도 검수자가 정답을 가린 채 60문항 재풀이
fixes: QR-012~014 공통 지문에 최고점 시각·반감 주기 명시

review2.method: 기존 ISAT 200문항을 4묶음으로 나눠 정답을 가린 채 재풀이 → 오류·쉬운 문항·중복 정리 → 보기 길이 균형·오답 보강 → 별도 검수자가 정답을 가린 채 최종 재풀이

items.stimulus: Every volunteer who has handled compost at the Harbourside community garden has completed the garden's soil-safety workshop. The workshop has only ever been held on the first Monday of a month. Mira is a volunteer who handled compost at the garden last Saturday.
items.question: If the statements above are true, which of the following must also be true?

options.text: Mira completed the workshop last month.
Mira attended the workshop on the first Monday of some month.
Every volunteer who has completed the workshop has handled compost.
Mira handles compost at the garden every Saturday.

items.explanation_ko: 1) 퇴비를 다룬 봉사자 → 워크숍 이수. Mira는 퇴비를 다룬 봉사자이므로 워크숍을 이수했다. 2) 워크숍은 항상 '어느 달의 첫째 월요일'에만 열렸으므로 Mira는 어떤 달의 첫째 월요일에 참석했다 → B. 오답: A 지난달이라는 시점은 알 수 없음. C 조건의 역(이수자 → 퇴비 취급)으로, 성립하지 않음. D 매주 토요일인지는 근거 없음.

items.stimulus: The town council plans to reduce traffic congestion in the town centre by doubling the price of parking there. Council officials argue that higher parking prices will persuade many drivers to take the bus instead, so fewer cars will enter the centre.
items.question: The officials' argument assumes that

options.text: many drivers who currently park in the centre have a practical bus alternative for their trips.
bus fares will be reduced at the same time as parking prices rise.
most congestion in the town centre is caused by delivery vehicles.
the extra parking revenue will be spent on road repairs.

items.explanation_ko: 논증: 주차비 인상 → 운전자들이 버스로 전환 → 차량 감소. 이 연결이 성립하려면 운전자들에게 실제로 이용 가능한 버스 대안이 있어야 한다(부정하면 '버스 대안이 없다' → 전환 불가 → 논증 붕괴) → A. 오답: B 요금 인하는 도움이 될 수는 있으나 필수 전제가 아님. C 오히려 논증을 약화시키는 내용. D 수입의 용도는 혼잡 감소와 무관.

items.stimulus: A survey of a city's residents found that people who own a dog reported walking, on average, 40 minutes more per week than people who do not. A local health group concluded that encouraging residents to adopt dogs would increase the amount people walk.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most weakens the health group's conclusion?

options.text: Most dogs need to be walked at least once a day.
Some respondents who did not own a dog walked more than some who did.
Many dog owners in the survey said they chose to get a dog because they already enjoyed taking long walks.
The survey included residents from every suburb of the city.

items.explanation_ko: 결론은 '개를 키우면 → 더 걷는다'는 인과. C는 인과 방향이 반대(원래 많이 걷는 사람이 개를 키움)일 가능성을 제시하므로, 개를 입양시켜도 걷는 양이 늘지 않을 수 있다 → 가장 약화. 오답: A 오히려 강화. B 평균 비교와 양립 가능하므로 약화 효과 거의 없음. D 표본 대표성을 높여 오히려 강화.

items.stimulus: Either we ban all mobile phones from classrooms, or students will spend every lesson distracted. Since nobody wants students to be distracted, we must ban all mobile phones from classrooms.
items.question: Which of the following best describes the flaw in this reasoning?

options.text: It presents only two possible outcomes when other options exist.
It relies on the opinion of someone who is not an expert.
It draws a general conclusion from a single example.
It mistakes the effect of something for its cause.

items.explanation_ko: '전면 금지 아니면 매 수업 산만' 두 가지만 제시하는 거짓 딜레마(false dilemma). 사용 시간 제한, 보관함 등 다른 대안이 무시됨 → A. 오답: B 권위자 의견은 등장하지 않음. C 단일 사례가 제시되지 않음. D 인과 혼동이 아님.

items.stimulus: In the five years after a coastal town built a new sea wall, insurance claims for flood damage in the town fell by 30% compared with the previous five years. Researchers concluded that the sea wall was responsible for the fall.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the researchers' conclusion?

options.text: Rainfall in the region was lower in the later five-year period than in the earlier one.
The sea wall cost considerably more to build than was originally estimated.
Several insurers raised their premiums in the town during the later period.
In nearby towns without sea walls but with similar weather, flood-damage claims did not fall over the same period.

items.explanation_ko: 인과 주장을 강화하려면 다른 설명(날씨 등)을 배제해야 한다. D는 방파제가 없는 비슷한 날씨의 이웃 마을에서는 감소가 없었다는 비교군을 제시 → 방파제가 원인일 가능성 상승. 오답: A 강우 감소라는 대안 원인 → 약화. B 비용은 효과와 무관. C 보험료 인상으로 가입·청구가 줄었을 수 있어 대안 설명 → 약화.

items.stimulus: In many pre-industrial societies, written records were produced mainly by a small literate group of clerks, priests and officials. Historians who rely on such records therefore see the past largely through the concerns of those groups: taxes, property, law and religious observance. The daily lives of farmers, labourers and children appear, if at all, at the moments when they came into contact with these institutions - when they paid a fine, inherited land or were baptised. Some historians have tried to correct this imbalance by studying objects such as tools, pottery and house foundations, which were made and used by ordinary people.
items.question: Which of the following can most reasonably be inferred from the passage?

options.text: Records from pre-industrial societies are generally unreliable about taxation.
In written records, information about ordinary people tends to be tied to official or institutional events.
Farmers in pre-industrial societies were never able to read or write.
Studying physical objects gives historians a complete picture of everyday life.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 평민의 삶이 '벌금 납부, 토지 상속, 세례' 등 제도와 접촉한 순간에만 기록에 나타난다고 말한다 → B가 직접 추론됨. 오답: A 세금 기록이 부정확하다는 언급 없음(오히려 관심사였음). C '주로' 소수가 기록했다는 것이지 농민이 '절대' 문맹이었다는 뜻은 아님(과도한 일반화). D '불균형을 바로잡으려 한다'일 뿐 '완전한 그림'은 과장.

items.stimulus:
Two commentators respond to a city library's proposal to stop issuing printed library cards and require borrowers to use a phone app instead.

Commentator X: Retiring the printed card is sensible. Producing and replacing cards costs money that could be spent on books, and the app can remind borrowers when loans are due, which should cut overdue fines. Nearly nine in ten of our current borrowers already own a smartphone.

Commentator Y: The savings are real but small, and X's figure hides the real problem. The borrowers who depend on the library most - older residents, recent arrivals and people on low incomes - are disproportionately among those without smartphones. A library that makes access easier for the already-connected and harder for everyone else has misunderstood its purpose. Keep the app, by all means, but keep the cards as well.
items.question: Which of the following best expresses Commentator Y's main point?

options.text: The app should be abandoned because it will cost more than printed cards.
Most of the library's borrowers do not own a smartphone.
Printed cards should be kept alongside the app so that borrowers without smartphones are not disadvantaged.
Overdue fines are an important source of income for the library.

items.explanation_ko: Y의 마지막 문장 'Keep the app ... but keep the cards as well'이 결론이며, 근거는 도서관에 가장 의존하는 집단이 스마트폰이 없는 경우가 많다는 점 → C. 오답: A Y는 앱을 유지하라고 함. B Y는 X의 '열에 아홉 보유' 수치를 부정하지 않음. D 연체료 수입은 Y의 논점이 아님.

items.stimulus:
Two commentators respond to a city library's proposal to stop issuing printed library cards and require borrowers to use a phone app instead.

Commentator X: Retiring the printed card is sensible. Producing and replacing cards costs money that could be spent on books, and the app can remind borrowers when loans are due, which should cut overdue fines. Nearly nine in ten of our current borrowers already own a smartphone.

Commentator Y: The savings are real but small, and X's figure hides the real problem. The borrowers who depend on the library most - older residents, recent arrivals and people on low incomes - are disproportionately among those without smartphones. A library that makes access easier for the already-connected and harder for everyone else has misunderstood its purpose. Keep the app, by all means, but keep the cards as well.
items.question: Commentators X and Y disagree most clearly about whether

options.text: the smartphone-ownership figure is sufficient grounds for withdrawing printed cards.
producing and replacing printed cards costs the library money.
the app could remind borrowers when their loans are due.
the library should offer an app at all.

items.explanation_ko: X는 '열에 아홉이 스마트폰 보유'를 근거로 카드 폐지를 지지하고, Y는 그 수치가 '문제를 가린다'며 카드 유지를 주장 → 그 수치가 폐지의 충분한 근거인지가 쟁점 → A. 오답: B Y도 '절감은 실제로 있다'고 인정. C Y는 알림 기능을 반박하지 않음. D 둘 다 앱 자체에는 찬성.

items.stimulus:
Two commentators respond to a city library's proposal to stop issuing printed library cards and require borrowers to use a phone app instead.

Commentator X: Retiring the printed card is sensible. Producing and replacing cards costs money that could be spent on books, and the app can remind borrowers when loans are due, which should cut overdue fines. Nearly nine in ten of our current borrowers already own a smartphone.

Commentator Y: The savings are real but small, and X's figure hides the real problem. The borrowers who depend on the library most - older residents, recent arrivals and people on low incomes - are disproportionately among those without smartphones. A library that makes access easier for the already-connected and harder for everyone else has misunderstood its purpose. Keep the app, by all means, but keep the cards as well.
items.question: Commentator Y's argument depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.text: Most older residents dislike using new technology.
The cost of keeping printed cards is greater than X suggests.
Overdue fines will not fall if the app is introduced.
Without printed cards, borrowers who lack smartphones would not have an equally convenient way to use the library.

items.explanation_ko: Y: 스마트폰 없는 이용자가 불리해진다 → 카드도 유지해야 한다. 부정 테스트: 만약 카드 없이도 그들이 똑같이 편리하게 이용할 방법(예: 창구 신분 조회)이 있다면 '카드를 유지해야 한다'는 결론이 무너짐 → D가 필수 가정. 오답: A Y의 논거는 '보유 여부'이지 기술에 대한 '선호'가 아님. B Y는 절감이 실제로 있다고 인정했으므로 반대 방향. C 연체료 감소 여부는 Y의 결론과 무관.

items.stimulus: If a bridge is rated for heavy vehicles, it has passed a load test. The Fenwick Bridge has not passed a load test. Therefore, the Fenwick Bridge is not rated for heavy vehicles.
items.question: Which of the following arguments is most similar in its pattern of reasoning to the argument above?

options.text: If a plant is a cactus, it stores water in its stem. This plant stores water in its stem, so it is a cactus.
If it rains, the match is cancelled. It did not rain, so the match was not cancelled.
If a student is on the honour roll, her average mark is above 85. Lena's average mark is not above 85, so Lena is not on the honour roll.
All licensed pilots have passed a medical examination. Kim has passed a medical examination, so Kim is a licensed pilot.

items.explanation_ko: 원 논증 구조: P이면 Q / Q가 아님 / 따라서 P가 아님(후건 부정, 타당). C도 '우등생이면 85 초과 / 85 초과 아님 / 우등생 아님'으로 동일 구조 → C. 오답: A·D 'Q이다 → P이다'(후건 긍정 오류). B 'P가 아님 → Q가 아님'(전건 부정 오류).

items.stimulus: Most of the town's bakers belong to the local trade association, and most members of the trade association support the new opening-hours rule. So most of the town's bakers support the new rule.
items.question: Which of the following contains the same flaw in reasoning as the argument above?

options.text: All members of the choir can read music, and Sam is a member of the choir. So Sam can read music.
Most residents of the valley own a car, and most car owners in the valley drive to work. So most residents of the valley drive to work.
Most visitors to the museum arrive by train, so the train station should display signs to the museum.
No reptile is warm-blooded, and every snake is a reptile. So no snake is warm-blooded.

items.explanation_ko: '대부분 A는 B, 대부분 B는 C → 대부분 A는 C'는 오류다(예: 60%×60%=36%로 절반 미만이 될 수 있음). 또 협회 회원 중 찬성자가 제빵사가 아닐 수도 있다. B도 '대부분 주민은 차 소유, 대부분 차 소유자는 차로 출근 → 대부분 주민이 차로 출근'으로 같은 '대부분' 연쇄 오류 → B. 오답: A·D는 '모두/어떤 것도'를 쓴 타당한 삼단논법. C는 연쇄 구조가 아닌 정책 제안.

items.stimulus: A company that sells a memory-training app reports that users who completed its 30-day programme scored 25% higher on the app's own memory quiz at the end of the programme than at the start. The company advertises that its app 'improves memory'.
items.question: Which of the following is the most serious problem with using this evidence to support the company's advertising claim?

options.text: The higher quiz scores may reflect practice with that particular quiz rather than an improvement in memory generally.
Thirty days may be too short a period for some users to finish the programme.
Some users may not have enjoyed using the app.
A 25% increase is too small to be noticed in daily life.

items.explanation_ko: 증거는 '앱 자체 퀴즈' 점수 상승인데, 주장은 '기억력 전반의 향상'이다. 같은 형식의 퀴즈를 반복하면 연습 효과만으로 점수가 오를 수 있어 증거와 주장 사이에 간극이 있다 → A. 오답: B 완료자만 분석했으므로 기간은 핵심 문제 아님. C 선호도는 효과와 무관. D 25%가 작다는 것은 근거 없는 판단이며 가장 심각한 문제도 아님.

items.stimulus: When a centuries-old painting is cleaned, conservators face a choice that is as much philosophical as technical. Varnish applied by earlier owners yellows over time, dulling colours the artist may have intended to be bright, and removing it can reveal a startling brilliance. Some critics object that a painting's history is part of the painting: the yellowed surface is what generations of viewers actually saw, and stripping it away replaces a real, inherited object with a modern guess about the artist's intentions. Conservators reply that most old varnish was never the artist's choice, and that leaving it in place preserves not history but neglect. The disagreement is sharpened by the fact that cleaning is irreversible. A layer that has been removed cannot be put back, whereas a decision to wait can always be revisited when techniques improve.
items.question: Which of the following best describes the main purpose of the passage?

options.text: To argue that all old paintings should be cleaned as soon as possible
To explain the chemical process that causes varnish to turn yellow
To criticise conservators for working too slowly
To outline a debate about removing aged varnish from old paintings and the considerations on each side

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 비판자(변색된 표면도 작품의 역사)와 복원가(오래된 바니시는 작가의 선택이 아님) 양측 입장과 비가역성이라는 고려 사항을 소개한다 → D. 오답: A 한쪽 결론을 주장하지 않음. B 화학적 원리는 설명하지 않음. C 복원가를 비판하는 글이 아님.

items.stimulus: When a centuries-old painting is cleaned, conservators face a choice that is as much philosophical as technical. Varnish applied by earlier owners yellows over time, dulling colours the artist may have intended to be bright, and removing it can reveal a startling brilliance. Some critics object that a painting's history is part of the painting: the yellowed surface is what generations of viewers actually saw, and stripping it away replaces a real, inherited object with a modern guess about the artist's intentions. Conservators reply that most old varnish was never the artist's choice, and that leaving it in place preserves not history but neglect. The disagreement is sharpened by the fact that cleaning is irreversible. A layer that has been removed cannot be put back, whereas a decision to wait can always be revisited when techniques improve.
items.question: The last two sentences of the passage most strongly support which of the following?

options.text: When there is real doubt about whether to clean a painting, the irreversibility of cleaning is a reason to favour waiting.
Modern cleaning techniques can no longer be improved.
Critics believe that artists always intended their paintings to look yellow.
Conservators should never clean old paintings.

items.explanation_ko: 마지막 두 문장: 제거한 층은 되돌릴 수 없지만, 기다리기로 한 결정은 기술이 발전하면 다시 검토할 수 있다 → 불확실할 때는 기다리는 쪽에 유리한 비대칭 → A. 오답: B '기술이 발전하면'이라는 표현과 모순. C 비판자는 '작가 의도'가 아니라 '관람의 역사'를 근거로 함. D '절대 하지 말라'는 과도한 결론.

items.stimulus: When a centuries-old painting is cleaned, conservators face a choice that is as much philosophical as technical. Varnish applied by earlier owners yellows over time, dulling colours the artist may have intended to be bright, and removing it can reveal a startling brilliance. Some critics object that a painting's history is part of the painting: the yellowed surface is what generations of viewers actually saw, and stripping it away replaces a real, inherited object with a modern guess about the artist's intentions. Conservators reply that most old varnish was never the artist's choice, and that leaving it in place preserves not history but neglect. The disagreement is sharpened by the fact that cleaning is irreversible. A layer that has been removed cannot be put back, whereas a decision to wait can always be revisited when techniques improve.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the conservators' reply to the critics?

options.text: Surveys show that many museum visitors prefer the warm tone of yellowed paintings.
Some cleaning carried out in the past damaged the paint beneath the varnish.
Artists' letters and workshop records show that many painters expected owners to strip and renew varnish periodically and did not intend any particular layer to be permanent.
Some artists deliberately tinted their varnish to soften the colours of their paintings.

items.explanation_ko: 복원가의 반론 핵심: '오래된 바니시 대부분은 작가의 선택이 아니었다'. C는 작가들 스스로 바니시가 주기적으로 교체될 것으로 여겼다는 기록 증거로 이를 직접 뒷받침 → C. 오답: A 관람객 선호는 비판자 쪽에 유리. B 세척 위험을 보여 비판자 쪽에 유리. D 바니시가 작가의 의도였던 경우를 보여 복원가 주장을 약화.

items.stimulus: Since a hospital introduced an online appointment-booking system, the proportion of missed appointments has fallen from 12% to 7%. The hospital's administrator concludes that the system should be introduced at all of the region's outpatient clinics, because it will reduce missed appointments there as well.
items.question: The administrator's conclusion relies on the assumption that

options.text: missed appointments cost the region's clinics a significant amount of money.
patients at the other outpatient clinics are similar enough to the hospital's patients, in their access to and use of online services, for the effect to carry over.
the online system was cheaper to set up than the hospital's previous booking method.
missed appointments at the hospital had been rising before the system was introduced.

items.explanation_ko: 한 병원에서의 효과를 다른 모든 외래 클리닉으로 일반화하므로, 두 집단의 환자가 온라인 이용 면에서 비슷하다는 전제가 필요하다(부정하면 효과가 이전되지 않을 수 있음) → B. 오답: A 비용 문제는 '줄어들 것'이라는 예측과 무관. C 도입 비용은 결론의 근거가 아님. D 이전 추세는 필수 전제가 아님.

items.stimulus: Dr Alvarez argues that the city should add fluoride to its water supply. However, Dr Alvarez once owned shares in a company that sold dental products. Her argument should therefore be rejected.
items.question: The reasoning above is flawed because it

options.text: assumes that what is true of a group must be true of each of its members.
treats a correlation between two things as proof that one causes the other.
uses a key term in two different senses.
rejects an argument because of a fact about the person making it rather than on the argument's merits.

items.explanation_ko: Alvarez 박사의 주장 내용을 검토하지 않고, 과거 주식 보유라는 개인적 사실만으로 주장을 기각한다 → 인신공격(ad hominem) 오류 → D. 오답: A 집단-개인 오류 아님. B 상관-인과 혼동 아님. C 용어의 이중 의미가 사용되지 않음.

items.stimulus: The following rules apply to the crew at a polar research station. Anyone who drives the snow vehicle holds a cold-weather first-aid certificate. Nobody who holds a cold-weather first-aid certificate is assigned to night kitchen duty. Priya is assigned to night kitchen duty. Tomas drives the snow vehicle.
items.question: If all of the statements above are true, which of the following could be true?

options.text: Tomas is assigned to night kitchen duty.
Priya holds a cold-weather first-aid certificate.
Priya drives the snow vehicle.
A crew member who holds a cold-weather first-aid certificate does not drive the snow vehicle.

items.explanation_ko: 규칙: 운전 → 자격증, 자격증 → 야간 주방 아님. Tomas: 운전 → 자격증 → 주방 아님(A 불가능). Priya: 주방 → (대우) 자격증 없음(B 불가능) → (대우) 운전 안 함(C 불가능). D는 '자격증 소지 → 운전'이라는 규칙이 없으므로(역은 성립하지 않음) 가능 → D. '반드시 참'이 아니라 '참일 수 있는 것'을 묻는다는 점에 주의.

items.stimulus: Over the past ten years, the number of reported cases of a certain skin condition in Country Q has tripled. Over the same period, sales of a popular brand of sunscreen in Country Q have also tripled. A consumer group argues that the sunscreen is causing the skin condition and should be withdrawn from sale.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most weakens the consumer group's argument?

options.text: The sunscreen is also sold in several neighbouring countries.
During the decade, a national campaign trained doctors to recognise and report the condition, which had previously often gone undiagnosed.
Some people who have the skin condition have never used that brand of sunscreen.
The sunscreen contains ingredients that are also found in other skin products.

items.explanation_ko: 두 수치가 함께 늘었다는 상관관계만으로 인과를 주장한다. B는 '보고 건수' 증가가 실제 발생 증가가 아니라 진단·보고 체계 변화 때문일 수 있음을 보여줌 → 가장 강하게 약화. 오답: A 이웃 국가 자료가 없으면 판단 불가. C 다른 원인도 있을 수 있다는 것일 뿐, 이 선크림이 원인 중 하나일 가능성은 남음(흔한 함정). D 다른 제품과 성분 공유는 판단에 도움이 안 됨.

items.stimulus: A newspaper columnist writes: Districts that moved to a four-day school week to save money have, on average, seen little change in pupils' test scores. Opponents warned that pupils would fall behind, but the data have proved them wrong. Every school district facing budget pressure should therefore adopt the four-day week. The savings on transport, heating and staff time are substantial, and since achievement is unaffected, there is no downside.
items.question: The columnist's claim that there is 'no downside' is most vulnerable to which criticism?

options.text: It relies on data from school districts rather than from whole countries.
It assumes that saving money is undesirable for school districts.
It treats unchanged average test scores as if they captured every relevant effect, overlooking possible effects on particular groups of pupils or on families.
It concludes that the opponents were wrong without offering any evidence.

items.explanation_ko: 칼럼니스트는 '평균 점수 불변 → 손해 없음'으로 비약한다. 평균은 일부 학생 집단의 하락을 가릴 수 있고, 시험 점수 외의 영향(맞벌이 가정의 돌봄 부담 등)도 고려하지 않았다 → C. 오답: A 지역 단위 자료 자체는 문제가 아님. B 칼럼니스트는 절약을 바람직하게 봄(정반대). D 평균 점수 자료를 근거로 제시했음.

items.stimulus: A newspaper columnist writes: Districts that moved to a four-day school week to save money have, on average, seen little change in pupils' test scores. Opponents warned that pupils would fall behind, but the data have proved them wrong. Every school district facing budget pressure should therefore adopt the four-day week. The savings on transport, heating and staff time are substantial, and since achievement is unaffected, there is no downside.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the columnist's recommendation to districts facing budget pressure?

options.text: Many parents in districts with a four-day week say they prefer the new schedule.
In some four-day districts, test scores were slightly higher than had been predicted.
Several of the districts that adopted a four-day week are in rural areas.
In districts that adopted the four-day week, the savings amounted to less than 2% of their budgets, because the largest costs, such as teachers' salaries, did not change.

items.explanation_ko: 권고의 근거 중 하나는 '절감액이 상당하다'는 것. D는 실제 절감이 예산의 2% 미만으로 미미했다고 하여 예산 압박 해소라는 목적 자체를 약화 → D. 오답: A·B 오히려 정책을 지지. C 농촌 지역이라는 사실만으로는 효과를 판단할 수 없음.

items.stimulus: A town compared two adult reading programmes, each of which enrolled 200 participants. Programme M used volunteer tutors and Programme N used paid tutors. The town's report concluded that Programme M was more effective, because a higher percentage of its participants passed the final reading assessment. The report's figures are shown in the table.
items.question: Which of the following is the best evaluation of the report's conclusion?

options.text: It is well supported, because 80% of Programme M's completers passed, compared with 70% of Programme N's.
It is doubtful, because 56% of Programme N's enrolled participants passed compared with 32% of Programme M's, and M's pass rate counts only the minority who completed.
It is doubtful, because Programme N enrolled more participants than Programme M.
It is well supported, because volunteer tutors are usually more motivated than paid tutors.

items.explanation_ko: 완료자 기준 합격률: M 64/80=80%, N 112/160=70%. 등록자 기준: M 64/200=32%, N 112/200=56%. M은 등록자의 60%가 중도 탈락했으므로 완료자 기준 비율만으로 '더 효과적'이라 할 수 없다 → B. 오답: A 탈락을 무시한 함정. C 두 프로그램 모두 200명 등록(사실 오류). D 지문 밖 일반론으로 증거가 아님.

items.stimulus: The Merrow River ferry operates only when the river level is between 1.2 metres and 3.5 metres. On Tuesday morning, the ferry was operating.
items.question: Which of the following must be true?

options.text: The river level was exactly 3.5 metres on Tuesday morning.
The ferry operates every Tuesday morning.
Whenever the river level is between 1.2 and 3.5 metres, the ferry operates.
On Tuesday morning, the river level was between 1.2 metres and 3.5 metres.

items.explanation_ko: '오직 ~일 때만 운항' = 운항 → 수위 1.2~3.5 m. 화요일 아침 운항했으므로 수위는 그 범위 안 → D. 오답: A 정확한 값은 알 수 없음. B 매주 운항한다는 근거 없음. C 조건의 역(수위가 맞으면 반드시 운항)으로, 'only when'에서는 도출되지 않음.

items.stimulus: An ecologist argues: The decline in native bee numbers in the Kerrin Valley cannot be due to the new pesticide, because bee numbers in the valley began falling two years before that pesticide first went on sale.
items.question: The ecologist's argument assumes that

options.text: the decline in bee numbers has been driven by the same cause throughout the period in which numbers have fallen.
the new pesticide is harmful to some insects other than bees.
bee numbers in neighbouring valleys have remained stable.
the pesticide's manufacturer tested its effect on bees before selling it.

items.explanation_ko: 감소가 농약 출시 전부터 시작됐다는 사실은 '감소의 시작 원인'이 농약이 아님을 보여줄 뿐이다. 출시 이후 농약이 감소를 가속했을 가능성을 배제하려면 '감소 전체가 하나의 같은 원인 때문'이라는 전제가 필요(부정하면 농약이 추가 원인일 수 있어 결론 붕괴) → A. 오답: B 다른 곤충 피해는 무관. C 이웃 계곡 상황은 전제로 필요 없음. D 제조사 시험 여부는 논증 구조와 무관.

items.stimulus: Linguists estimate that a large share of the world's languages are each spoken by fewer than ten thousand people, and that many of these are no longer being learned by children. When a language stops being passed on, it does not usually vanish at once; it lingers for a generation or two among older speakers. This interval matters. Recordings, dictionaries and grammars made while fluent speakers remain can later support revival, as several communities have shown by teaching an ancestral language to children who grew up speaking only a majority language. Documentation alone, however, does not keep a language alive. A language survives as a means of everyday communication only if families and communities choose to use it, and that choice is shaped by schooling, employment and the prestige the language carries.
items.question: Which of the following is best supported by the passage?

options.text: Recording a language guarantees that it will survive.
The period after children stop learning a language offers an opportunity that may be lost if it is not used.
Most of the world's languages are spoken by more than ten thousand people each.
Attempts to revive languages have never succeeded.

items.explanation_ko: 지문: 아이들이 배우지 않게 된 후에도 한두 세대 동안 노년 화자가 남는다 → 'This interval matters' → 그 기간에 기록을 남겨야 나중에 부흥이 가능 → B. 오답: A 'Documentation alone ... does not keep a language alive'와 모순. C '상당 부분'이 1만 명 미만이라는 정보만으로 과반 여부를 알 수 없음. D 여러 공동체의 성공 사례가 언급됨.

items.stimulus: Linguists estimate that a large share of the world's languages are each spoken by fewer than ten thousand people, and that many of these are no longer being learned by children. When a language stops being passed on, it does not usually vanish at once; it lingers for a generation or two among older speakers. This interval matters. Recordings, dictionaries and grammars made while fluent speakers remain can later support revival, as several communities have shown by teaching an ancestral language to children who grew up speaking only a majority language. Documentation alone, however, does not keep a language alive. A language survives as a means of everyday communication only if families and communities choose to use it, and that choice is shaped by schooling, employment and the prestige the language carries.
items.question: The author would most likely agree that a government wishing to support an endangered language should

options.text: fund documentation projects only, since recordings make later revival possible.
require every citizen to learn the language.
combine documentation with measures that make the language useful and valued in schooling and employment.
concentrate its support on the languages with the most speakers.

items.explanation_ko: 저자는 기록의 가치를 인정하면서도 '기록만으로는 부족하며, 사용 여부는 학교·고용·위상에 좌우된다'고 말한다 → 두 가지를 병행하는 C. 오답: A '기록만'은 저자 입장과 모순. B 전 국민 의무 학습은 지문에 없는 극단적 주장. D 화자 수가 많은 언어 우선은 근거 없음.

items.stimulus: A cafe owner believes that playing slower music in her cafe makes customers stay longer and spend more.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the owner's belief?

options.text: The cafe's staff prefer working while fast music is playing.
Licences for slow music cost less than licences for fast music.
On days when slow music was played, customers stayed longer and spent more per visit than on otherwise comparable days when fast music was played.
Some of the cafe's customers buy only takeaway coffee.

items.explanation_ko: 음악 템포 외의 조건이 비슷한 날끼리 비교해 느린 음악일 때 체류 시간과 지출이 더 컸다는 자료는 주장을 직접 뒷받침 → C. 오답: A·B 직원 선호와 비용은 고객 행동과 무관. D 테이크아웃 고객 존재는 주장을 강화하지 않음(오히려 효과가 제한적일 수 있음).

items.stimulus: Last year, 60% of the cyclists injured in road accidents in our city were not wearing a helmet. This shows that cyclists who do not wear helmets are more likely to be injured than cyclists who do.
items.question: Which of the following identifies the most serious flaw in this argument?

options.text: It assumes that helmets prevent all injuries.
It fails to consider what proportion of all cyclists in the city do not wear helmets.
It confuses how serious injuries are with how often they occur.
It assumes that cyclists cause all road accidents.

items.explanation_ko: '부상자 중 60%가 미착용'이라는 수치만으로는 위험도를 비교할 수 없다. 예컨대 시 전체 자전거 이용자의 80%가 미착용이라면 미착용자의 부상 위험은 오히려 더 낮을 수 있다(기저율 무시) → B. 오답: A 모든 부상을 막는다는 가정은 없음. C 심각도는 언급되지 않음. D 사고 책임 주체는 논증과 무관.

items.stimulus: In a regional orchestra, all of the string players also sing in the orchestra's choir. Some of the brass players also sing in the choir. No one who sings in the choir plays in the jazz band.
items.question: If these statements are true, which of the following must also be true?

options.text: Some of the brass players play in the jazz band.
Everyone who sings in the choir is a string player.
No brass player plays in the jazz band.
No string player plays in the jazz band.

items.explanation_ko: 현악 → 합창단 → 재즈밴드 아님. 따라서 모든 현악 연주자는 재즈밴드에 속하지 않는다 → D. 오답: A 합창단에 없는 금관 연주자가 재즈밴드에 있을 '수는' 있지만 반드시 그런 것은 아님. B 역(합창단 → 현악)은 성립하지 않으며 금관 연주자도 합창단에 있음. C '일부' 금관만 합창단이므로 나머지는 재즈밴드일 수도 있음.

items.stimulus: When cars were banned from the main street of the village of Larrow (population 900), the street became busier with shoppers and sales at local shops increased. The capital city (population 2 million) should therefore ban cars from its main shopping avenue to achieve the same result.
items.question: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it

options.text: assumes that a policy's effect in a small village will be the same in a very large city, despite relevant differences such as how shoppers travel there.
provides no evidence that sales at Larrow's shops increased.
relies only on the testimony of shop owners.
confuses the cause of increased sales with its effect.

items.explanation_ko: 인구 900명 마을과 200만 도시를 유비해 같은 결과를 기대한다. 쇼핑객의 이동 방식, 교통량, 상권 규모 등 결과에 영향을 줄 수 있는 차이를 무시하므로 유비가 약하다 → A. 오답: B 매출 증가는 전제로 제시됨. C 상점 주인 증언은 언급되지 않음. D 인과 방향 혼동이 아님.

items.question: A jacket priced at $80 is reduced by 25% in a sale. After the sale, the reduced price is increased by 25%. What is the new price of the jacket?
items.explanation_ko: 할인 후: 80 × 0.75 = 60달러. 인상 후: 60 × 1.25 = 75달러 → B. 25% 인상의 기준이 원래 가격(80)이 아니라 할인된 가격(60)이므로 원래대로 돌아오지 않는다. 오답: D 80은 '−25%+25%=0'이라는 흔한 착각. A 70, C 76은 계산 실수.

items.question: A cyclist rides 18 km in 45 minutes at a steady speed. What is her speed in kilometres per hour?

options.text: 24 km/h
40 km/h

items.question: A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue and 4 green counters. One counter is taken at random. What is the probability that it is NOT blue?
items.explanation_ko: 전체 5+3+4 = 12개, 파란색이 아닌 것 9개 → 9/12 = 3/4 → D. 오답: A 1/4은 파란색일 확률. B 1/3, C 2/3은 개수 대신 색깔 수(3가지)로 계산하는 등의 실수.

items.question: What is the next number in the sequence 3, 7, 15, 31, ... ?
items.explanation_ko: 규칙: 앞 항 × 2 + 1 (3→7→15→31). 31 × 2 + 1 = 63 → D. 차이가 4, 8, 16으로 두 배씩 늘어나므로 다음 차이는 32 → 31 + 32 = 63으로도 확인 가능. 오답: A 47 = 차이 16을 반복. B 55 = 차이를 등차(+8)로 착각. C 62 = 31 × 2(+1 누락).

items.question: A medicine is prescribed at 15 mg per kilogram of body mass per day, given in 3 equal doses. How many milligrams should each dose be for a child of mass 24 kg?

options.text: 5 mg
40 mg
360 mg
120 mg

items.explanation_ko: 하루 총량: 15 × 24 = 360 mg. 3회로 나누면 360 ÷ 3 = 120 mg → D. 오답: A 5 = 15 ÷ 3(체중 무시). B 40 = 120을 한 번 더 3으로 나눔. C 360은 하루 총량(1회분 아님).

items.stimulus: The table shows the number of visitors (in thousands) to four national parks in each season of one year.
items.question: Which park had the greatest difference between its number of visitors in its busiest season and in its quietest season?

options.text: Dunmore
Brook
Alder
Cinder

items.explanation_ko: 각 공원의 (최대 − 최소): Alder 48−12 = 36, Brook 42−18 = 24, Cinder 60−8 = 52, Dunmore 25−25 = 0 → Cinder → D. 오답: Brook은 최대 계절이 봄(42)이라 여름만 보면 오판하기 쉬움. Dunmore는 차이가 0.

items.stimulus: The table shows the number of visitors (in thousands) to four national parks in each season of one year.
items.question: In spring, the number of visitors to Brook was what percentage greater than the number of visitors to Alder?

options.text: About 29%

items.explanation_ko: 봄: Brook 42, Alder 30. 증가율 = (42 − 30) ÷ 30 × 100 = 12/30 = 40% → A. 기준은 '비교 대상'인 Alder(30). 오답: B 약 29% = 12 ÷ 42(기준을 Brook으로 잘못 잡음). C 12%는 차이(천 명)를 퍼센트로 착각. D 140%는 42/30 비율 자체.

items.stimulus: The table shows the number of visitors (in thousands) to four national parks in each season of one year.
items.question: Next year, Cinder expects its summer visitors to fall by 25% and its winter visitors to double, with autumn and spring unchanged. Dunmore expects its visitors in every season to rise by 10%. If these expectations are correct, which statement about next year's annual totals is true?

options.text: Dunmore will have 3 thousand more visitors than Cinder.
The two parks will have the same number of visitors.
Cinder will have 3 thousand more visitors than Dunmore.
Cinder will have 10 thousand more visitors than Dunmore.

items.explanation_ko: Cinder: 여름 60 × 0.75 = 45, 가을 20, 겨울 8 × 2 = 16, 봄 32 → 45+20+16+32 = 113(천 명). Dunmore: 올해 100 × 1.1 = 110. 차이 113 − 110 = 3 → Cinder가 3천 명 많음 → C. 오답: A 방향을 반대로 읽음. B 변화를 상쇄된다고 착각. D 10 = 올해 Cinder 120과 Dunmore 110을 비교한 실수.

items.question: A community theatre sold 40 tickets for one performance. Adult tickets cost $12 and child tickets cost $7. Total ticket sales were $395. How many adult tickets were sold?
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the product of the two numbers shown is even?
items.explanation_ko: 곱이 홀수가 되려면 두 주사위가 모두 홀수여야 함: (1/2) × (1/2) = 1/4. 따라서 곱이 짝수일 확률 = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4 → D. 오답: A 1/4은 곱이 홀수일 확률. B 1/2은 '짝수/홀수 반반'이라는 직관적 착각. C 2/3은 근거 없는 값.

items.question: A city of about 4.8 million people produces about 1.95 million tonnes of household waste per year. Approximately how much household waste is this per person per day? (1 tonne = 1000 kg)

options.text: 1.1 kg
11 kg
400 kg

items.stimulus: A patient is given a single dose of a drug at time 0. A graph of the drug's concentration in the patient's blood rises to a peak and then falls smoothly. The values read from the graph are given in the table. The peak concentration of 12 mg/L occurs 2 hours after the dose; after that, the concentration halves every 2 hours.

table.title: Blood concentration of drug after a single dose (graph values)

items.question: Between 2 hours and 6 hours after the dose, by how much does the concentration fall, on average, per hour?

options.text: 1.5 mg/L per hour
2.25 mg/L per hour
3.0 mg/L per hour
4.5 mg/L per hour

items.explanation_ko: 2시간: 12 mg/L, 6시간: 3 mg/L. 감소량 9 mg/L ÷ 경과 시간 4시간 = 2.25 mg/L/h → B. 오답: A 1.5 = 9 ÷ 6(시각 6을 경과시간으로 착각). C 3.0 = 9 ÷ 3. D 4.5 = 9 ÷ 2.

items.stimulus: A patient is given a single dose of a drug at time 0. A graph of the drug's concentration in the patient's blood rises to a peak and then falls smoothly. The values read from the graph are given in the table. The peak concentration of 12 mg/L occurs 2 hours after the dose; after that, the concentration halves every 2 hours.

table.title: Blood concentration of drug after a single dose (graph values)

items.question: If the pattern after the peak continues, what will the concentration be 14 hours after the dose, to two decimal places?

options.text: 0 mg/L

items.explanation_ko: 정점(2시간, 12) 이후 2시간마다 절반: 4h 6 → 6h 3 → 8h 1.5 → 10h 0.75 → 12h 0.375 → 14h 0.1875 ≈ 0.19 mg/L → C. 반감기가 일정하면 농도는 0이 되지 않는다(지수 감소). 오답: A 0.38은 12시간 값. B 0은 직선 감소로 착각. D 0.09는 16시간 값.

items.stimulus: A patient is given a single dose of a drug at time 0. A graph of the drug's concentration in the patient's blood rises to a peak and then falls smoothly. The values read from the graph are given in the table. The peak concentration of 12 mg/L occurs 2 hours after the dose; after that, the concentration halves every 2 hours.

table.title: Blood concentration of drug after a single dose (graph values)

items.question: A second, identical dose is given 6 hours after the first. Assume the second dose produces exactly the same concentration pattern as the first (starting from its own time 0) and that concentrations from the two doses add together. What is the total concentration 8 hours after the FIRST dose?

options.text: 12 mg/L
15 mg/L

items.explanation_ko: 첫 투여 후 8시간 시점: 첫 번째 용량 기여 = 8h 값 1.5 mg/L. 두 번째 용량은 6시간에 투여했으므로 이 시점은 그 투여 후 2시간 → 12 mg/L. 합 = 1.5 + 12 = 13.5 mg/L → D. 오답: A 12는 두 번째 용량만 계산. B 15 = 12 + 3(첫 용량의 6h 값을 잘못 사용). C 10.5 = 9 + 1.5(두 번째 용량의 1h 값을 사용).

items.question: A laboratory solution contains reagent P and water in the ratio 2 : 7 by volume. A technician has 450 mL of this solution and wants to change the ratio to 1 : 2 by adding only reagent P. How much reagent P must be added?

options.text: 25 mL
50 mL
75 mL
175 mL

items.explanation_ko: 현재: P = 450 × 2/9 = 100 mL, 물 = 350 mL. 물은 그대로이므로 목표 P = 350 ÷ 2 = 175 mL. 추가량 = 175 − 100 = 75 mL → C. 검산: 175 : 350 = 1 : 2. 오답: D 175는 최종 P의 양(추가량이 아님). B 50은 1 : 2를 기존 전체 450 mL에 적용해 목표 P를 150 mL로 잡은 실수. A 25는 계산 실수.

items.question: An empty tank can be filled by pipe X alone in 3 hours or by pipe Y alone in 6 hours. A drain Z, working alone, can empty a full tank in 4 hours. If X, Y and Z are all opened at the same time when the tank is empty, how long will it take to fill the tank?

options.text: 4 hours
2 hours
1 hour 20 minutes
12 hours

items.question: A bacterial culture contains 500 cells at 9:00 am, and the number of cells doubles every 20 minutes. The culture is counted every 20 minutes, starting at 9:00 am. At which count will the number of cells first be greater than 30,000?
The mean mass of 8 laboratory mice is 24 g. One mouse is removed, and the mean mass of the remaining 7 mice is 23 g. What is the mass of the mouse that was removed?
items.explanation_ko: 총합: 8 × 24 = 192 g, 남은 7마리 7 × 23 = 161 g. 제거된 쥐 = 192 − 161 = 31 g → A. 오답: B 25는 평균이 1 g 줄었으니 24 + 1이라고 착각한 값. C 24·D 23은 평균값을 그대로 고른 함정.

items.stimulus: The speed of sound in air depends on the air temperature. The table gives measured values. Over this range, the speed increases by the same amount for each degree Celsius.
items.question: During a storm, the air temperature is 30 °C. A person hears thunder 4.0 seconds after seeing a lightning flash. Treating the light as arriving instantly, approximately how far away was the lightning?

items.stimulus: The speed of sound in air depends on the air temperature. The table gives measured values. Over this range, the speed increases by the same amount for each degree Celsius.
items.question: A researcher shouts towards a cliff and hears the echo 4.0 seconds later. The air temperature is actually 10 °C, but she mistakenly uses the speed of sound at 30 °C to calculate her distance from the cliff. By how many metres will her calculated distance differ from the true distance?

options.text: 6 m

items.explanation_ko: 메아리는 왕복이므로 거리 = 음속 × 4.0 ÷ 2 = 음속 × 2. 실제(10 °C): 337 × 2 = 674 m. 잘못된 계산(30 °C): 349 × 2 = 698 m. 차이 = 24 m → C. (음속 차 12 m/s × 2 s = 24 m로도 계산 가능.) 오답: A 48 m는 왕복을 반으로 나누지 않음. B 12 m는 음속 차이 자체. D 6 m는 1초 기준 절반 계산 실수.

items.question: A screening test is used for a condition that is present in 2% of the people tested. The test gives a positive result for 90% of people who have the condition, and also gives a positive result for 10% of people who do not have the condition. A randomly chosen person who was tested receives a positive result. Approximately what is the probability that this person has the condition?

options.text: About 2%
About 16%
About 50%
About 90%

items.explanation_ko: 1,000명으로 가정: 질환 있음 20명 → 양성 18명. 질환 없음 980명 → 위양성 98명. 양성 총 116명 중 실제 질환자 18명 → 18/116 ≈ 0.155 ≈ 16% → B. 오답: D 90%는 민감도(질환자 중 양성 비율)를 양성자 중 질환자 비율로 혼동하는 대표적 오류. A 2%는 사전 유병률 그대로. C 50%는 근거 없는 추측.

items.question: In a clinic, the ratio of nurses to doctors is 5 : 2. After 6 more doctors join the clinic (and no nurses join or leave), the ratio of nurses to doctors becomes 5 : 3. How many nurses work at the clinic?
items.explanation_ko: 간호사 5k, 의사 2k. 5k : (2k + 6) = 5 : 3 → 15k = 10k + 30 → k = 6. 간호사 = 30명 → A. 검산: 의사 12 → 18, 30 : 18 = 5 : 3. 오답: B 18은 바뀐 뒤 의사 수. C 15는 k를 3으로 잘못 구한 경우. D 36은 계산 실수.

items.question: Of 200 applicants for a training course, 45% are men. 30% of the men and 40% of the women passed the entrance test. What percentage of all 200 applicants passed?
items.explanation_ko: 남성 200 × 0.45 = 90명 → 합격 27명. 여성 110명 → 합격 44명. 전체 합격 71명 ÷ 200 = 35.5% → B. 오답: A 35%는 30%와 40%의 단순 평균(인원 가중치 무시). C 34.5%는 남녀 인원을 거꾸로 적용(남 110명 × 30% = 33, 여 90명 × 40% = 36 → 69/200). D 70%는 두 비율을 더한 값.

items.stimulus: A delivery van leaves its depot at 8:00 and returns at 12:00. The table gives values read from a graph of the van's distance from the depot. Between the times shown, the van moves at a constant speed or is stationary.

table.title: Distance of a delivery van from its depot (values read from a distance-time graph)

items.question: What was the van's average speed over the whole period from 8:00 to 12:00, based on the total distance it travelled?

options.text: 25 km/h
0 km/h

items.explanation_ko: 총 이동거리: 8:00–9:00 30 km, 9:30–10:00 20 km, 10:30–11:00 30 km, 11:00–12:00 20 km → 100 km(갔다가 돌아온 거리 50 + 50). 총 시간 4시간 → 100 ÷ 4 = 25 km/h → A. 오답: B 12.5 = 50 ÷ 4(편도만 계산). C 33.3 = 100 ÷ 3(정지 시간 제외, 문제는 전체 시간을 요구). D 0은 출발점과 도착점이 같아 변위를 사용한 경우.

items.question: A cylindrical water tank has an internal diameter of 2 m and a height of 3 m. Water flows into the empty tank at 50 litres per minute. Using π ≈ 3, approximately how long will it take to fill the tank? (1 m³ = 1000 litres; volume of a cylinder = πr²h)

options.text: 1.5 hours
3 hours
6 hours
12 hours

items.explanation_ko: 반지름 r = 1 m. 부피 ≈ 3 × 1² × 3 = 9 m³ = 9,000 L. 9,000 ÷ 50 = 180분 = 3시간 → B. 오답: D 12시간은 지름 2 m를 반지름으로 사용(36 m³). C 6시간은 r² 대신 2r 사용(18 m³). A 1.5시간은 부피를 절반으로 잘못 계산.

items.question: The cost of hiring a hall is a fixed booking fee plus a charge for each hour. Hiring the hall for 3 hours costs $190, and hiring it for 7 hours costs $350. Community groups receive a 20% discount on the total cost. How much does a community group pay to hire the hall for 5 hours?
items.explanation_ko: 4시간 차이로 160달러 차이 → 시간당 40달러. 고정료 = 190 − 3 × 40 = 70달러. 5시간 = 70 + 200 = 270달러. 20% 할인 → 270 × 0.8 = 216달러 → A. 오답: C 270은 할인 미적용. B 230은 시간당 요금에만 할인 적용(70 + 160). D 250은 20%를 20달러로 착각.

items.question: A box contains 6 batteries, of which 2 are faulty. Two batteries are taken from the box at random, one after the other, without replacement. What is the probability that at least one of the two batteries is faulty?
items.explanation_ko: 여사건 이용: 둘 다 정상일 확률 = 4/6 × 3/5 = 12/30 = 2/5. 적어도 하나 불량 = 1 − 2/5 = 3/5 → C. 오답: A 5/9는 복원 추출로 계산(1 − (2/3)²). B 2/5는 둘 다 정상일 확률. D 1/3은 한 개만 뽑았을 때 불량일 확률.

items.question: In a sequence of numbers, each term after the second is the sum of the two terms before it. The 3rd term is 11 and the 6th term is 47. What is the 1st term?

Train A leaves a station at 9:00 and travels at a constant 60 km/h. Train B leaves the same station at 9:40, travelling in the same direction on a parallel track at a constant 90 km/h. At what time does Train B catch up with Train A?
items.explanation_ko: 9:40에 A는 이미 60 × (40/60) = 40 km 앞서 있음. 상대 속도 90 − 60 = 30 km/h → 40 ÷ 30 = 4/3시간 = 1시간 20분 → 9:40 + 1:20 = 11:00 → C. 검산: 11:00에 A 120 km(2시간), B 90 × 4/3 = 120 km. 오답: A 10:20은 9:40에 40분(앞선 40 km를 시속 60 km로 잘못 나눈 시간)을 더한 값. B 10:40은 9:40에 1시간만 더한 어림 실수. D 11:20은 출발 지연 40분을 한 번 더 더한 값.

items.question: A stock solution has a concentration of 2.5 mol/L. What volume of the stock solution is needed to make 400 mL of a solution with a concentration of 0.15 mol/L by adding water?

options.text: 2.4 mL
6 mL
60 mL
24 mL

items.explanation_ko: 용질의 양은 희석 전후 같음: C1V1 = C2V2 → 2.5 × V1 = 0.15 × 400 = 60 → V1 = 60 ÷ 2.5 = 24 mL → D. 오답: C 60은 2.5로 나누는 단계 누락. A 2.4는 자릿수 실수. B 6은 0.15 × 400 ÷ 10 등 잘못된 나눗셈.

items.stimulus: A recent study of 2,400 Australian adults aged 18-35 examined the relationship between social media use and life satisfaction. Initial analysis revealed that participants using social media more than three hours daily reported life satisfaction scores 0.4 standard deviations below light users—a substantial difference. However, when researchers separated 'active engagement' (creating content, direct messaging, video calls) from 'passive consumption' (scrolling without interaction), the picture changed. The negative association held only for passive consumption. Heavy active users showed satisfaction scores statistically indistinguishable from light users, despite spending equivalent total hours on the platforms. A subgroup who reported using social media primarily to maintain contact with close friends and family showed satisfaction scores slightly above non-users.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reliably inferred from the passage?

options.text: Reducing total social media use to under three hours daily would substantially improve wellbeing for most heavy users.
How people use social media seems to matter more for wellbeing than how long, and some uses show no negative link at all.
Researchers have demonstrated that creating social media content directly causes higher life satisfaction in young adults.
Most Australian adults aged 18-35 use social media for more than three hours daily, and most of that time is spent on passive scrolling.

items.explanation_ko: 부정적 연관은 수동적 소비에서만 나타났고, 같은 시간을 쓰는 능동 사용자는 가벼운 사용자와 차이가 없었으며, 가까운 사람과 연락하는 용도의 사용자는 비사용자보다 약간 높았다. 따라서 사용 시간보다 사용 방식이 더 중요해 보이고 일부 사용 방식에는 부정적 연관이 없다는 B가 가장 확실한 추론이다. 오답: A는 시간을 줄이면 개선된다는 인과 주장으로, 같은 시간을 써도 차이가 없던 능동 사용자 결과와 맞지 않는다. C는 관찰 연구를 직접 인과가 증명된 것으로 과장했다. D는 헤비 유저의 비율도, 사용 시간 중 수동 스크롤의 비중도 지문에 나오지 않는다.

items.stimulus: Urban tree planting programmes are typically evaluated on a single metric: tonnes of CO₂ sequestered per year. Officials measure success by carbon absorption, and species selection follows—favouring fast-growing varieties optimised for that metric. While quantifiable, this approach systematically undervalues other benefits that urban trees provide. Stormwater interception by canopy and root systems reduces flood damage and water treatment costs. Shade lowers urban temperatures during heatwaves, with documented effects on heat-related mortality among elderly residents. Habitat for urban wildlife, mental health benefits for nearby residents, and even local property values all flow from tree presence regardless of carbon performance. A neighbourhood maple grove may sequester less carbon per hectare than a eucalyptus plantation, yet deliver greater overall value when these factors are weighed. The pattern is not unique to forestry: any complex programme evaluated by a single quantitative metric risks optimising that metric while degrading the actual outcomes the programme was meant to achieve.
items.question: Which of the following best captures the author's central argument?

options.text: Because maple groves can outperform eucalyptus plantations on overall value, urban programmes should favour maples over fast-growing species.
Carbon sequestration is a misleading measure of urban tree value and should be removed from programme evaluation altogether.
Judging a complex programme by a single metric can improve that metric while undermining the outcomes the programme was meant to achieve.
Urban trees deliver stormwater, cooling, habitat, mental-health and property-value benefits whose combined value exceeds their carbon value.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 탄소 흡수량이라는 단일 지표 평가가 빗물 차단, 그늘, 서식지 등 다른 가치를 놓치게 한다고 설명한 뒤, 마지막 문장에서 이것이 임업만의 문제가 아니라 단일 지표로 평가되는 모든 복잡한 프로그램의 위험이라고 일반화한다. 이 일반 결론을 담은 C가 정답이다. 오답: A는 단풍나무와 유칼립투스 비교를 예시가 아닌 수종 권고로 오해했다. B는 탄소 지표를 아예 빼라는 주장으로, 저자는 그것 하나만 쓰는 것을 문제 삼을 뿐이다. D는 근거로 나열된 세부 정보이며, 합산 가치가 탄소 가치를 넘는다는 단정도 지문에 없다.

items.stimulus: Critics of standardised university admissions testing argue that such tests should be eliminated. They cite a recent longitudinal study tracking 5,000 graduates from a major Australian university, which found that students' admissions test scores correlated only weakly (r = 0.18) with workplace performance ratings five years after graduation. The critics conclude that admissions tests fail to identify candidates who will succeed in their careers, and that universities should drop them in favour of holistic assessments based on personal essays, recommendations, and structured interviews.
items.question: The critics' argument depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.text: Workplace ratings five years on are a valid measure of career success, and the proposed holistic assessments would predict those ratings better.
All Australian universities currently rely heavily on standardised admissions tests, giving them decisive weight in their selection decisions.
Personal essays and structured interviews are inherently more accurate than standardised tests at predicting any outcome universities care about.
Students who score well on admissions tests tend to be less motivated in their later careers than students who perform well in interviews.

items.explanation_ko: 비판자들은 시험 점수와 5년 후 직장 평가의 약한 상관(r = 0.18)을 근거로 시험을 폐지하고 총체적 평가로 대체하자고 한다. 이 결론이 성립하려면 직장 평가가 경력 성공의 타당한 척도여야 하고, 대체할 평가가 그 척도를 더 잘 예측해야 한다. 둘 다 담은 A가 정답이다. 오답: B는 호주의 모든 대학이 시험에 결정적 비중을 둘 필요가 없어 불필요하다. C는 대학이 중시하는 '모든' 결과를 본질적으로 더 잘 예측한다는 필요 이상으로 강한 가정이다. D는 경력상 동기 비교로 논증의 근거와 무관하다.

items.stimulus: Dr. Patel proposes that requiring all Australian medical students to complete a six-month rural placement during their training would substantially improve healthcare access in underserved regional areas. She bases her proposal on overseas data: in one European country, a similar mandatory rural rotation programme was followed by a sustained increase in the proportion of medical graduates choosing rural practice, from 15% before the programme to 38% in subsequent cohorts—a difference maintained over fifteen years of follow-up. Critics object that the European country's geographic, cultural, and healthcare-system context differs from Australia's in ways that may limit how well its results would transfer to Australia.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strongly support Dr. Patel's proposal against the critics' objection?

options.text: The overseas programme has been favourably reviewed in international medical journals and adopted by two neighbouring countries with similar health systems.
Two Australian medical schools that made rural placements compulsory for whole cohorts saw a similar, lasting rise in graduates entering regional practice.
Both countries have publicly funded universal healthcare systems and broadly comparable medical school curricula and accreditation standards.
Rural communities in the overseas country offer large financial incentives to retain doctors after training, incentives that are uncommon in Australian regional areas.

items.explanation_ko: 비판자의 반론은 해외 결과가 지리·문화·의료 체계가 다른 호주에 그대로 옮겨지지 않을 수 있다는 것이다. 이를 가장 직접적으로 막는 것은 호주 안에서 같은 개입(전원 의무 농촌 실습)이 비슷한 효과를 지속적으로 냈다는 증거이므로 B가 정답이다. 오답: A는 비슷한 이웃 나라들에서의 재현이라 호주로의 이전 가능성은 여전히 보여주지 못한다. C는 제도의 일반적 유사성만 보여줄 뿐 호주에서 실제로 효과가 나는지는 말해주지 못한다. D는 해외 효과가 의무 실습이 아니라 재정 인센티브 때문일 수 있음을 시사해 오히려 제안을 약화한다.

items.stimulus: An economic commentator argues: 'The minimum wage increase enacted in our state two years ago has clearly hurt employment. State unemployment in entry-level retail and fast-food positions rose from 6.2% to 7.4% over those two years—a substantial increase. The wage increase priced low-skilled workers out of jobs, just as economic theory predicted. Other states should learn from our experience and reject similar proposals.'
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the commentator's argument?

options.text: Some prominent economists have published papers disputing the view that minimum wage increases reduce employment, citing evidence from other regions.
Neighbouring states with no wage increase saw entry-level unemployment rise even more, from 5.8% to 8.5%, during a regional downturn that hit all states.
The minimum wage increase improved the financial circumstances of low-wage workers who retained their jobs, helping many escape poverty-level incomes.
Most large national retail chains absorbed the wage increase without reducing employment levels, while small local businesses cut staff hours rather than fire workers.

items.explanation_ko: 논평자는 최저임금 인상 뒤 실업률이 6.2%에서 7.4%로 1.2%p 오른 것을 인상 탓으로 돌린다. B에 따르면 인상이 없던 이웃 주는 같은 기간 5.8%에서 8.5%로 2.7%p나 올랐고 원인은 모든 주에 닥친 지역 경기 침체였으므로, 실업 증가는 최저임금이 아닌 공통 요인으로 설명된다. 오답: A는 다른 지역 근거를 든 학자들의 반대 의견일 뿐 이 주의 데이터를 반박하지 않는다. C는 다른 이익을 말할 뿐 실업 증가 자체를 부정하지 않는다. D는 일부 기업의 대응 방식을 보여줄 뿐 전체 실업률 상승의 원인을 바꾸지 못한다.

items.stimulus: Coral reefs face severe threats from rising ocean temperatures and acidification, which together cause coral bleaching events that have killed substantial portions of major reef systems worldwide. However, scientists studying reefs in unusually warm pockets of the Pacific have identified coral colonies that survive at temperatures lethal to most reef corals. Genetic analysis reveals these heat-resistant colonies carry distinct symbiotic algae and stress-response gene variants. Conservation researchers are now exploring whether these resilient colonies could be propagated and introduced to vulnerable reefs to enhance survival rates. Critics caution that introducing organisms beyond their natural range, even within the same species, can produce unintended ecological consequences and that the long-term performance of relocated colonies in different environments remains poorly understood.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: Propagating heat-resistant colonies is likely to reverse reef decline, because their genetic advantages should carry over to any reef.
Since some corals already tolerate lethal temperatures, warming poses a smaller long-term threat to the world's reefs than was previously thought.
Heat resistance is likely to spread through most reef populations naturally, making human relocation of colonies unnecessary.
Heat-resistant colonies may offer a useful conservation tool, though relocating them to other reefs carries real ecological uncertainty.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 고온에서 살아남는 산호 군체가 발견되어 이식이 검토되고 있지만, 비판자들이 자연 분포 밖 도입의 예기치 못한 결과와 장기 성과의 불확실성을 경고한다고 전한다. 유용한 보전 수단일 수 있지만 다른 산호초로 옮기는 데에는 실제 생태적 불확실성이 있다는 D가 지문과 일치한다. 오답: A는 어느 산호초에서나 효과가 이어진다고 단정해 비판자의 우려를 무시한다. B는 위협이 줄었다고 하지만 지문은 심각한 위협을 전제한다. C는 내성이 자연적으로 퍼진다고 예측하는데 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.stimulus: Historians often present major technological innovations as the work of singular geniuses—Edison and the light bulb, Watt and the steam engine, the Wright brothers and powered flight. This narrative is appealing but historically misleading. Each of these breakthroughs depended on decades of preceding work by less famous engineers, scientists, and tinkerers whose contributions were essential to the eventual breakthrough. Edison's light bulb followed dozens of earlier prototypes that established the engineering principles he refined. Watt improved on Newcomen's existing engine rather than inventing the concept. The Wright brothers built on aerodynamic research published widely in their era. Recognising the collaborative and incremental nature of innovation does not diminish the achievements of the famous figures, but it does change how we should think about scientific and technological progress: less as the work of isolated heroes and more as the visible peak of a much larger underlying community.
items.question: What is the author's central argument?

options.text: Famous innovators refined work built by many predecessors, so progress is better seen as collective and incremental than as solitary genius.
Edison, Watt and the Wright brothers have been overrated, since their breakthroughs were largely the work of earlier and less famous engineers.
Historians should stop crediting individuals for inventions and instead attribute each breakthrough to the community that preceded it.
The singular-genius narrative persists mainly because it is more appealing to readers than detailed accounts of incremental engineering.

items.explanation_ko: 저자는 단독 천재 서사가 오해를 부른다고 비판하며 에디슨, 와트, 라이트 형제 모두 앞선 수많은 작업 위에서 성과를 냈다고 설명한다. 동시에 이것이 그들의 업적을 깎아내리는 것은 아니며, 진보를 더 큰 공동체의 보이는 봉우리로 보아야 한다고 결론짓는다. 이를 담은 A가 정답이다. 오답: B는 저자가 명시적으로 부정한 업적 폄하이고, 성과가 '대부분 다른 사람의 작업'이었다는 것도 과장이다. C는 개인에게 공을 돌리지 말라는 주장으로 업적을 인정하는 저자의 입장과 어긋난다. D는 서사가 지속되는 이유에 대한 주장으로 지문이 다루지 않는다.

items.stimulus: An education commentator argues: 'Recent test data prove that private schools provide superior education to public schools. The latest national assessment shows private school students scoring 18 percentage points higher on standardised mathematics tests than public school students. The gap has been remarkably stable over the past five years. Parents who can afford private education are giving their children a clear academic advantage—a finding that should inform government policy on school choice.'
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the commentator's argument?

options.text: Tuition fees at many private schools have risen faster than inflation over the same five-year period.
Standardised mathematics tests capture only one dimension of educational achievement and omit many others.
Public schools enrol a larger share of students with learning disabilities and of students still learning English.
After adjusting for family income, parental education and achievement at age 5, the gap falls to under 2 points.

items.explanation_ko: 논평자는 18점 격차를 사립학교 교육의 우월성으로 해석한다. D처럼 가정 소득, 부모 학력, 5세 시점 학업 성취를 통제하자 격차가 2점 미만으로 줄면, 격차는 학교의 질이 아니라 입학 전부터 있던 학생 차이(선발 효과)에서 온 것이 된다. 오답: A는 학비 문제로 교육 효과와 무관하다. B는 시험의 한계를 말할 뿐 수학 성적 차이 자체를 부정하지 않는다. C는 격차 일부를 설명할 수 있으나 얼마나 설명하는지 알 수 없어 격차 대부분을 지우는 D보다 약하다.

items.stimulus: A philosopher of mind argues: 'Recent large language models have demonstrated the capacity to solve novel mathematical problems they were never explicitly trained on—including problems whose solutions require combining concepts from multiple domains in ways no human author had previously documented. If sophisticated pattern matching alone could produce these results, we would expect such models to fail when problem structures are sufficiently distant from their training data, since matching has nothing to extrapolate from. Yet the models succeed even on highly novel structures. This success cannot be explained by pattern matching, and therefore the models must possess a form of genuine understanding distinct from mere statistical association.'
items.question: The philosopher's argument depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.text: Mathematical problem-solving is the most rigorous test of cognitive ability currently available to researchers studying minds.
Pattern matching, however sophisticated or large its training data, cannot in principle generalise to problem structures far from those it has seen.
Human mathematicians achieve their results through processes fundamentally different from statistical learning.
The novel problems the models solved are representative of the full range of problems that a system with genuine understanding should be able to handle.

items.explanation_ko: 철학자는 패턴 매칭이라면 학습 데이터에서 멀리 떨어진 문제에서 실패해야 하는데 모델은 성공하므로 진정한 이해가 있다고 결론짓는다. 이 논증은 아무리 정교하고 데이터가 많은 패턴 매칭도 원리적으로 그런 일반화를 할 수 없다는 전제에 의존하며, 이를 부정하면 결론이 무너진다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. 오답: A는 수학이 가장 엄격한 시험일 필요가 없어 불필요하다. C는 인간의 방식에 관한 주장으로 모델에 대한 논증과 무관하다. D는 진정한 이해가 다룰 모든 문제를 대표할 필요까지는 없으며, 부정해도 '패턴 매칭으로는 설명 불가'라는 핵심 추론은 남는다.

items.stimulus: Public health researchers have long debated optimal vaccination campaign design. Mass campaigns distribute vaccines broadly across short windows, achieving high overall coverage but consuming enormous logistical resources. Targeted campaigns focus on high-risk subgroups (elderly, immunocompromised, healthcare workers), achieving lower total coverage but at far lower cost per quality-adjusted life year saved. A 2024 modelling study compared both approaches across twelve disease scenarios. Targeted campaigns were superior in nine scenarios when measured by lives saved per dollar spent. However, in the three scenarios involving highly contagious airborne pathogens with reproduction numbers above 5, mass campaigns substantially outperformed targeted approaches—not merely on lives saved, but also on cost-effectiveness, because the rapid transmission dynamics meant that uncovered subgroups would soon expose the vaccinated, undermining the protection that targeted coverage was designed to deliver.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: Targeted vaccination campaigns are always less appropriate than mass campaigns for diseases with reproduction numbers above 5, whatever their cost.
Mass vaccination campaigns are inappropriate for any disease that does not transmit through airborne pathways.
The best vaccination strategy depends on how the pathogen spreads, so the approach that is usually more cost-effective may not be in every case.
Cost-effectiveness, measured as lives saved per dollar, should be the primary criterion for choosing between vaccination strategies in all decisions.

items.explanation_ko: 12개 시나리오 중 9개에서는 표적 접종이 비용 대비 더 효과적이었지만, 재생산수 5 이상의 공기 전파 병원체 3개에서는 대량 접종이 생명과 비용 효과 모두에서 앞섰다. 따라서 최적 전략은 병원체의 전파 방식에 달려 있고 평소 더 비용 효과적인 방식이 모든 경우에 그렇지는 않다는 C가 정답이다. 오답: A는 3개 시나리오 결과를 비용과 상관없이 '항상'으로 일반화했다. B는 비공기 전파 질환에서 대량 접종이 부적절하다는 근거가 지문에 없다. D는 비용 효과를 모든 결정의 일차 기준으로 삼으라는 규범적 주장으로, 지문은 그런 결론을 내리지 않는다.

items.stimulus: Dr. Patel claims that early childhood reading aloud by parents substantially improves children's later academic performance. She bases her hypothesis on observational data showing that children whose parents reported reading to them daily before age 5 scored 20% higher on standardised tests at age 10 compared to children read to less frequently. Critics suggest the apparent effect may reflect parental factors—educated, attentive parents read more AND prepare children for academic success in many other ways—rather than reading itself.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strongly support Dr. Patel's hypothesis?

options.text: Parents who read daily to their children usually report enjoying the activity and continue it well beyond age 5.
Children who were read to daily before age 5 also tend to own more books and visit libraries more often at age 10 than children read to less often.
In a survey, teachers rated children who had been read to daily as more attentive and better prepared in class at age 10.
In a randomised trial, children of families assigned a reading program outperformed matched controls academically five years later.

items.explanation_ko: 비판자는 관찰된 차이가 독서 자체가 아니라 교육 수준과 관심이 높은 부모의 다른 영향 때문일 수 있다고 본다. D는 가정을 무작위로 배정해 부모 특성을 통제한 뒤에도 독서 프로그램 집단의 학업 성과가 높았음을 보여주므로 가설을 가장 강하게 지지한다. 오답: A는 부모가 즐긴다는 정보로 효과와 무관하다. B는 책 보유와 도서관 이용이 함께 나타난다는 관찰로, 부모 특성 설명과도 그대로 양립한다. C도 교사 평가라는 관찰 자료라 교란 요인을 배제하지 못한다.

items.stimulus: An environmental advocate argues: 'Mandatory recycling programs significantly reduce landfill waste. Cities that have introduced mandatory household recycling have seen landfill volumes drop by 30% on average. Therefore, every city should implement mandatory recycling to address waste problems.'
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the advocate's conclusion?

options.text: Residents in several cities have resisted mandatory recycling, citing the inconvenience and the time needed to sort and rinse household waste each week.
Some recycled materials, such as mixed plastics, cannot currently be processed economically and are eventually landfilled.
Cities with mandatory recycling report higher resident satisfaction with waste services than cities without it.
Cities that mandated recycling also added composting and commercial-waste rules; cities that mandated recycling alone cut landfill by only 5%.

items.explanation_ko: 옹호자는 의무 재활용 도시의 매립량 30% 감소를 재활용 정책의 효과로 보고 모든 도시에 권한다. D에 따르면 이 도시들은 퇴비화와 상업 폐기물 규제를 함께 도입했고 재활용만 도입한 도시는 5% 감소에 그쳤으므로, 효과의 대부분은 다른 정책에서 나온 것이다. 오답: A는 실행상의 불편과 저항일 뿐 효과를 반박하지 않는다. B는 일부 재료의 처리 문제로, 이미 측정된 매립량 감소를 부정하지 않는다. C는 주민 만족도로 매립량 감소 결론과 무관하다.

items.stimulus: Discussions of poverty often focus on individual choices and behaviours—savings habits, education decisions, work ethic, financial planning. Yet a growing body of research suggests this framing has the causal arrow pointing in the wrong direction. People struggling to pay rent or feed their families show measurably reduced performance on cognitive tasks involving attention, planning, and self-control—not because they are inherently less capable, but because their cognitive resources are constantly consumed by immediate survival concerns. The same individuals, when temporarily relieved of financial pressure, score significantly higher on the same tests. This finding inverts conventional thinking: rather than poor decisions causing poverty, the cognitive conditions of poverty often produce the very 'poor decisions' that observers later cite as evidence of personal failing. The implications for policy are substantial: addressing the cognitive burden of scarcity may be more effective than programmes that demand additional cognitive effort from already-burdened people.
items.question: Which of the following best captures the author's central argument?

options.text: People in poverty make poorer financial decisions mainly because they have less underlying cognitive capacity than wealthier people do.
Cognitive test scores shift with circumstances, so they are unreliable measures of ability and should not guide policy.
Poverty itself impairs decision-making, so easing financial pressure may beat demanding more effort from the poor.
Teaching financial planning skills is the most effective way to break the link between poverty and poor decisions.

items.explanation_ko: 저자는 재정 압박이 주의, 계획, 자기통제에 쓰일 인지 자원을 소모하며, 같은 사람도 압박이 풀리면 점수가 올라간다고 제시한다. 그래서 나쁜 결정이 빈곤을 낳는다기보다 빈곤이 나쁜 결정을 낳으며, 압박을 덜어주는 정책이 더 효과적일 수 있다고 결론짓는다. 이것이 C다. 오답: A는 저자가 명시적으로 부정한 '본래 인지 능력 부족' 설명이다. B는 검사의 신뢰성을 문제 삼지만 저자는 같은 검사로 변화를 보여줄 뿐 검사를 버리자고 하지 않는다. D는 재무 계획 교육을 권하는데, 이는 저자가 비판한 '추가 인지 노력 요구' 방식이다.

items.stimulus: A pharmaceutical company tested a new antidepressant in two randomised controlled trials with identical protocols, dosages, inclusion criteria, and primary outcome measures. Trial A, conducted at six urban academic medical centres, found the drug outperformed placebo by 14.5 percentage points (p < 0.001). Trial B, conducted at twelve community clinics in rural and small-city settings, found the drug outperformed placebo by 2.8 percentage points (p = 0.41, not statistically significant). The company submitted Trial A to the regulatory authority for approval and presented it at scientific conferences. Trial B was disclosed only in supplementary documentation, where the company described 'methodological concerns about Trial B implementation' without providing further specifics. No other trials of the drug have been conducted.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: The drug is ineffective at treating depression, since Trial A's result was most likely a fluke, and it should not be approved.
The company's selective reporting may give regulators and doctors a distorted view of the drug's effectiveness, whether or not its concerns are valid.
Patients in rural and small-city settings respond differently to antidepressants than patients in academic medical centres.
Trial B's failure to show a significant effect demonstrates that academic medical centres employ research practices superior to those of community clinics.

items.explanation_ko: 동일한 설계의 두 시험이 크게 다른 결과(14.5%p 대 2.8%p)를 냈는데, 회사는 유리한 Trial A만 적극 제출·발표하고 Trial B는 구체적 근거 없이 보조 자료에만 넣었다. 따라서 방법론 우려가 타당하든 아니든 선택적 보고가 규제기관과 의사의 판단을 왜곡할 수 있다는 B가 정답이다. 오답: A는 Trial A를 우연으로 단정하고 효과 없음을 결론짓는데 지문에 근거가 없다. C는 결과 차이의 원인을 환자 반응 차이로 단정하는데 다른 설명도 가능하다. D는 연구 기관의 우열을 단정하는데 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.stimulus: An ethicist argues for a strict utilitarian programming standard for autonomous medical triage systems: 'When such a system must allocate scarce critical-care resources—say, between two patients with comparable medical need—it should be programmed to select whichever choice maximises total expected life-years saved across the population, including all downstream effects on other patients waiting for resources. Any other criterion, such as first-come-first-served or random selection, sacrifices lives without justification. Since every life carries equal moral weight, and since arithmetic dictates that saving more aggregate life-years is preferable to saving fewer, the utilitarian standard is the only morally defensible programming choice.'
items.question: The ethicist's argument depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.text: Autonomous triage systems can, in practice, reliably estimate expected life-years across the downstream effects of each allocation.
Most shortages of critical-care resources arise between patients whose medical need is genuinely comparable.
Only consequences, measured in aggregate life-years, matter in judging an allocation; procedural fairness has no independent weight.
First-come-first-served allocation is morally indistinguishable from random selection between patients.

items.explanation_ko: 윤리학자는 모든 생명이 동등하고 더 많은 생명연수를 살리는 것이 낫다는 점에서 공리주의 기준만이 도덕적으로 정당하다고 결론짓는다. 다른 기준이 '정당한 이유 없이' 생명을 희생한다고 보려면 절차적 공정성 같은 비결과적 요소가 독립적 무게를 갖지 않아야 하므로 C가 핵심 가정이다. 오답: A는 실행 가능성 문제로, 원칙의 도덕적 정당성에 관한 논증에는 필요하지 않다. B는 부족 상황의 빈도에 관한 것으로 결론과 무관하다. D는 두 대안이 도덕적으로 같을 필요가 없으며 둘 다 비공리주의 기준으로 거부될 뿐이다.

items.stimulus: Vaccination policies often focus on achieving high coverage in the general population, but recent epidemiological research highlights the importance of equity. A vaccination program that reaches 95% of high-income neighborhoods but only 60% of low-income neighborhoods may produce a population-wide coverage of 80%, yet leave entire communities vulnerable to outbreaks. These pockets of low coverage can sustain disease transmission and eventually spread back to highly vaccinated areas. True public health success requires not just high average coverage but uniform distribution across all communities.
items.question: What is the main argument of the passage?

options.text: Vaccination programmes should aim for complete coverage in every neighbourhood before pursuing other health goals.
High average coverage is not enough; vaccination coverage must be evenly distributed across all communities.
Low-income neighbourhoods are the main source of the outbreaks that later spread to high-income areas.
Population-wide coverage of 80% is too low to prevent outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 고소득 지역 95%, 저소득 지역 60%로 전체 80%를 달성해도 낮은 지역이 전파를 유지해 다시 퍼질 수 있다고 하고, 진정한 성공은 높은 평균이 아니라 균일한 분포라고 결론짓는다. 이것이 B다. 오답: A는 모든 지역의 완전 접종을 최우선 목표로 제시하지만 지문의 주장은 분포의 균일성이다. C는 저소득 지역을 '주된' 발병원으로 단정해 지문을 넘어선다. D는 80%라는 수준 자체가 낮다고 하지만 지문은 평균이 아닌 격차를 문제 삼는다.

items.stimulus: Traditional histories of ancient Egypt focus on pharaohs and monumental architecture, but recent archaeological discoveries are reshaping our understanding. Excavations at workers' villages, such as those near the Giza pyramids and at Deir el-Medina, reveal complex social organization, evidence of paid labor (not slavery, as long believed), specialized craft guilds, medical care, and even labor disputes documented on papyri. These findings suggest that ancient Egyptian society was far more sophisticated and bureaucratically organized at the everyday level than monument-focused histories conveyed.
items.question: What is the author's primary point?

options.text: New excavations show that everyday Egyptian society was more complex and organised than monument-focused histories implied.
Evidence of paid labour proves that the pyramids were built without any forced or conscripted workers.
Monument-focused histories of Egypt are unreliable and should be replaced by the study of workers' villages alone.
Egyptian craft guilds and medical care were more advanced than those of other ancient civilisations.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 파라오와 기념물 중심의 전통적 역사와 달리, 노동자 마을 발굴에서 임금 노동, 장인 조합, 의료, 노동 분쟁 기록이 드러났다고 소개한 뒤 일상 수준에서도 정교하게 조직된 사회였다고 결론짓는다. 이것이 A다. 오답: B는 강제나 징발 노동이 전혀 없었다고 단정해 근거를 넘어선다. C는 기념물 중심 역사를 노동자 마을 연구로만 대체하자고 하지만 저자는 이해를 넓히자는 것일 뿐이다. D는 다른 고대 문명과의 비교로 지문에 없다.

items.stimulus: Recent economic data show that countries with high levels of investment in vocational training—programs that teach specific job skills like welding, plumbing, or healthcare assisting—tend to have lower youth unemployment rates than countries focusing exclusively on traditional academic education. The pattern holds even after controlling for overall economic conditions.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: Vocational training investment goes with lower youth unemployment, even allowing for overall economic conditions.
Countries focused on academic education have higher youth unemployment because academic degrees have little labour-market value.
Shifting young people from academic to vocational programs would lower youth unemployment in any country that tried it.
Vocational training reduces youth unemployment mainly by steering young people into trades such as welding and plumbing.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 직업훈련 투자가 많은 나라의 청년 실업률이 낮고, 이 패턴이 전반적 경제 상황을 통제해도 유지된다고 한다. 이 연관을 그대로 진술한 A가 가장 합리적인 추론이다. 오답: B는 학위의 노동시장 가치가 낮다는 원인을 지어냈다. C는 국가 간 연관을 '어느 나라에서나' 성립하는 인과로 확대했다. D는 특정 직종으로의 유도라는 메커니즘을 지어냈다.

items.stimulus: Climate scientist Dr. Rodriguez argues that solar activity is NOT the primary cause of recent global temperature rise. Her evidence: solar output has actually decreased slightly over the past 40 years, while global temperatures have risen substantially. Critics counter that complex climate systems may respond to solar changes with delays, and that even small variations in solar energy could amplify through atmospheric mechanisms.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strongly support Dr. Rodriguez's argument?

options.text: Over 40 years the lower atmosphere warmed while higher layers cooled, a pattern expected from greenhouse gases but not from solar forcing.
Solar output varies over an 11-year cycle, and global temperatures show small fluctuations that roughly track that cycle.
Earlier periods of high solar activity in the twentieth century coincided with periods of noticeable global warming.
Some atmospheric amplification mechanisms are known to respond to changes in solar ultraviolet output only after a delay of several years or more.

items.explanation_ko: Rodriguez 박사는 태양이 최근 온난화의 주원인이 아니라고 주장한다. A에서 하층 대기는 데워지고 상층은 냉각되었는데, 태양이 원인이라면 상층도 데워져야 하므로 이 패턴은 온실가스와는 맞고 태양 원인과는 맞지 않는다. 지연이나 증폭이라는 비판자 반론도 이 패턴은 설명하지 못한다. 오답: B와 C는 태양 활동과 기온이 함께 움직였다는 정보로 오히려 태양 원인설에 가깝다. D는 수년 이상의 지연 반응을 보여 비판자의 지연·증폭 주장을 지지한다.

items.stimulus: A financial analyst argues: 'Mutual funds operated by women managers significantly outperform funds managed by men. A recent study examined 200 mutual funds and found that women-managed funds had average annual returns 1.2 percentage points higher than those managed by men over a five-year period. This proves that women bring superior judgement to investment decisions, and investors should preferentially select female fund managers.'
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the analyst's conclusion?

options.text: Women-managed funds were concentrated in sectors that beat the market; compared within the same sectors, returns did not differ.
Several women-managed funds in the sample underperformed the market average during the five-year study period.
Women-managed funds in the sample attracted less new investor money than men-managed funds did over the period.
Returns for both groups of funds varied considerably from year to year as overall market conditions changed.
