items.stimulus: An environmental advocate argues: 'Carbon-offset programs allow individuals to compensate for their carbon emissions by funding projects that reduce emissions elsewhere. People who fly frequently can purchase offsets that fund forest preservation or renewable energy, neutralising their environmental impact. Therefore, frequent flyers who purchase certified offsets bear no genuine environmental responsibility for their flights.'
items.question: The advocate's argument depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.text: People who fly frequently generally have enough income to pay for certified offsets.
Offset projects are usually funded by a mix of individual buyers and large companies.
Certified offsets deliver real, lasting cuts that would not have happened anyway, fully balancing the flights.
Flying produces more greenhouse emissions per passenger-kilometre than any other common form of long-distance transport.

items.explanation_ko: 옹호자는 인증 상쇄를 구매하면 비행의 환경 영향이 '중화'되므로 책임이 전혀 없다고 결론짓는다. 이 결론은 상쇄 사업이 원래 일어나지 않았을 실질적·지속적 감축을 만들어 비행 배출을 완전히 상쇄한다는 C가 참일 때만 성립한다. 오답: A(구매 능력)는 구매한 사람에 대한 결론이므로 필요 없고, B(자금 출처)는 상쇄의 실효성과 무관하며, D(교통수단별 배출 비교)는 비행이 가장 배출이 많은지와 상관없이 상쇄가 완전한지만 문제되므로 필요 없다.

items.stimulus: Government statistics frequently report 'the unemployment rate'—typically the percentage of the labour force currently seeking work but unable to find it. This standard measure, while widely cited, captures only part of the employment landscape. It excludes people who have stopped actively looking for work because they are discouraged about prospects (often called 'discouraged workers'), part-time workers who would prefer full-time employment but cannot find it, and recent graduates who have not yet entered the labour force. During economic downturns, the gap between the official unemployment rate and broader measures of labour underutilisation typically widens substantially. A jurisdiction reporting 'unemployment fell from 6% to 5%' may simultaneously have seen its broader labour underutilisation rate rise from 12% to 14% if more workers became discouraged faster than unemployed workers found jobs.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: The official unemployment rate is misleading and should be replaced by broader measures.
Discouraged workers stop looking for jobs mainly because they lack the motivation to keep trying.
A falling official unemployment rate does not necessarily mean labour market conditions are improving.
During downturns, the official rate rises faster than broader measures of labour underutilisation.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 공식 실업률이 구직 단념자·불완전 취업자 등을 빠뜨리며, 경기 침체기에는 공식 실업률이 떨어져도 더 넓은 노동 저활용률은 오를 수 있다고 예시한다. 따라서 C처럼 공식 실업률 하락이 곧 노동시장 개선을 뜻하지는 않는다고 추론할 수 있다. 오답: A는 '일부만 포착한다'를 '폐지하고 대체하라'로 비약한 처방이고, B는 구직 단념의 원인을 의욕 부족으로 돌렸는데 지문은 전망에 대한 낙담이라고 했으며, D는 침체기에 넓은 지표와의 격차가 커진다는 지문과 반대 방향이다.

items.stimulus: A real estate firm's marketing materials advertise: 'Houses in our region appreciate by an average of 8% per year, making them an excellent long-term investment. Over the past decade, our region has consistently outperformed the national average. Buy now to take advantage of this proven, sustained growth pattern.'
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the firm's claim?

options.text: Real estate firms have sometimes been criticised for exaggerating returns in their advertising.
Several other regions also outperformed the national average for house prices over the past decade.
The region's population grew steadily over the decade as new employers arrived, increasing local demand for housing.
The 8% average is driven by a few luxury homes; the median home rose 1.2% a year, and prices are now falling.

items.explanation_ko: 회사는 연평균 8% 상승과 지난 10년의 실적을 근거로 '입증된 지속 성장'이니 지금 사라고 광고한다. D는 8%가 소수 고급 주택에 끌어올려진 평균일 뿐 중위 주택은 연 1.2% 올랐고, 최근에는 가격이 하락하기 시작했다고 하므로 대표성과 지속성을 동시에 무너뜨려 가장 크게 약화한다. 오답: A는 업계 전반에 대한 평판 문제로 이 자료의 진위를 다루지 않고, B는 다른 지역도 평균을 웃돌았다는 것으로 이 지역 주장과 무관하며, C는 인구 증가로 수요가 늘었다는 것이어서 오히려 광고를 지지한다.

items.stimulus: Informed consent for medical procedures requires that patients understand the nature, risks, benefits, and alternatives of the proposed intervention. However, recent research suggests this standard is rarely met in practice. In one study of 250 surgical consent encounters, only 38% of patients could correctly recall any of the named risks five minutes after the discussion. Patient comprehension was significantly lower among those who were anxious, in pain, or under time pressure—precisely the conditions in which most consent discussions occur. Yet ethics committees and courts continue to treat signed consent forms as evidence of valid informed consent, often treating the legal document as if the underlying epistemic state had actually been achieved. The gap between the procedural requirement and the cognitive reality remains largely unaddressed in current medical practice.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: Courts and ethics committees treat signed forms as proof of an understanding that patients often lack.
Signed consent forms have no legal value and should no longer be required before surgery.
Most surgical patients would prefer not to hear detailed information about the risks of their procedures.
Holding consent discussions when patients are calm would let most of them recall the named risks.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 환자가 설명 직후에도 위험을 거의 기억하지 못해 실제 이해가 부족한데도, 윤리위원회와 법원은 서명된 동의서를 유효한 동의의 증거로 취급한다고 지적한다. A가 이 '형식과 실제 이해의 괴리'를 그대로 담는다. 오답: B는 동의서를 폐지하라는 극단적 처방으로 지문에 없고, C는 환자들이 정보를 원하지 않는다는 선호 주장으로 근거가 없으며, D는 불안·통증이 이해를 낮춘다는 자료에서 차분한 상황이면 '대부분' 기억할 것이라는 결과를 끌어내 범위를 넘어섰다.

items.stimulus: A psychologist proposes that brief mindfulness meditation practice (10 minutes daily) reduces work-related anxiety in office workers. Her hypothesis is based on a study where 200 office workers who self-selected into a mindfulness program reported 30% lower anxiety scores after eight weeks compared to baseline. Critics argue that the apparent effect could reflect (a) people who chose to start meditation were already motivated to address their anxiety through other means, (b) self-reported anxiety could decline simply due to expectation of improvement, and (c) the eight-week period coincided with seasonal changes that affect mood independently.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strongly support the psychologist's hypothesis against the critics' objections?

options.text: A randomised trial with an equally credible control activity found larger cortisol drops with mindfulness.
The 30% drop in anxiety scores in the original study was statistically significant at p < 0.001.
Participants in the original study said beforehand that they expected meditation to ease their anxiety.
Office workers who start any new self-care routine often report feeling less anxious for a while.

items.explanation_ko: 비판자들은 (a) 자기 선택, (b) 기대 효과, (c) 계절 변화를 대안 설명으로 제시했다. A의 무작위 대조시험은 무작위 배정으로 (a)를, 기대 수준이 비슷한 대조 활동과 코르티솔 같은 생리 지표로 (b)를, 같은 기간 동시 비교로 (c)를 막으므로 가설을 가장 강하게 지지한다. 오답: B는 통계적 유의성만 말할 뿐 교란 요인을 배제하지 못하고, C는 참여자들이 효과를 기대했다는 것으로 기대 효과 비판을 오히려 뒷받침하며, D는 어떤 자기관리든 불안이 줄어든다는 것이어서 명상 고유의 효과를 의심하게 만든다.

items.stimulus: Public debates about social policy often present an apparent dilemma: either we treat people as fully responsible agents whose outcomes reflect their choices, or we treat them as products of circumstances beyond their control. Each framing alone produces incomplete analysis. The 'pure responsibility' view ignores genuine constraints—someone born into severe poverty, with poor schooling and unstable family circumstances, faces choices radically different from someone born into stable middle-class circumstances. The 'pure circumstances' view denies the reality that even within constrained situations, choices made matter and are properly attributable to the people who make them. Mature policy thinking holds both views simultaneously: people make real choices that genuinely shape their outcomes, and those choices are made within circumstances that powerfully shape what options exist and what choices feel possible. Effective policy must address both layers—creating circumstances that expand the meaningful options available to people, while still treating people as agents whose choices have weight and whose dignity requires recognition of their agency.
items.question: What is the author's central argument?

options.text: People should be held fully responsible for their choices, whatever circumstances they were born into.
Since circumstances shape which options seem possible, they largely determine how people's lives turn out.
Most policy disagreements about poverty could be settled by gathering better data on people's circumstances.
Good social policy must both widen people's real options and respect their choices as genuine agents.

items.explanation_ko: 저자는 '완전한 책임'과 '완전한 환경 결정' 두 관점이 각각 불완전하다며, 사람은 실제 선택을 하지만 그 선택은 환경의 제약 속에서 이루어지므로 정책은 선택지를 넓히는 동시에 개인의 주체성을 존중해야 한다고 주장한다. D가 이 두 층위를 함께 담는다. 오답: A는 '완전한 책임' 관점만, B는 '환경 결정' 관점만 택해 저자가 불완전하다고 한 한쪽으로 치우쳤고, C는 더 나은 자료로 논쟁이 해결된다는 주장으로 지문에서 다루지 않는다.

items.stimulus: Predictions about technology's effect on employment have a poor historical track record. In the early 1900s, economists predicted that mechanisation of agriculture would create permanent mass unemployment as farm workers were displaced. By the 1960s, similar predictions targeted factory automation. In the 1980s, computers were expected to render office workers obsolete. In each case, the predictions proved partly right (specific job categories did contract or disappear) and partly wrong (total employment did not collapse, as new categories of work emerged—often in ways no forecaster anticipated). Current debates about AI and employment echo these earlier patterns. However, several economists argue this time may be different: previous waves of automation primarily affected manual or routine cognitive tasks, while current AI systems can perform many non-routine cognitive tasks—a much broader range. Whether this difference produces a fundamentally different outcome, or merely shifts the categories of jobs affected while preserving the broader pattern of disruption-and-adaptation, remains genuinely uncertain.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: Because AI performs non-routine cognitive tasks, it will cause lasting mass unemployment unlike past technologies.
Past patterns of disruption and adaptation may or may not hold for AI, and history alone cannot settle which.
Past forecasts of technological unemployment were wrong in every respect, so current fears about AI are unfounded.
Workers in manual jobs face greater risk from AI than workers in non-routine cognitive jobs.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 과거 기술 변화가 일부 직종을 줄였지만 새 일자리가 생겨 '부분적 혼란 후 적응'의 패턴을 보였으며, AI가 비정형 인지 업무까지 수행해 이번에는 다를 수 있는지는 '진정으로 불확실하다'고 말한다. B가 이를 정확히 담는다. 오답: A는 영구적 대량 실업을 단정해 불확실하다는 지문과 어긋나고, C는 과거 예측이 '부분적으로 옳았다'는 지문과 달리 모두 틀렸다고 하며 AI 우려까지 부정했고, D는 과거 자동화가 육체·정형 업무에 영향을 주었고 AI는 비정형 인지 업무까지 한다는 지문과 반대 방향의 위험 비교다.

items.stimulus: A policy advocate argues: 'Raising the minimum wage to $25 per hour would reduce poverty without significant economic costs. Economists from leading research universities have published studies showing that recent moderate minimum wage increases (from $7 to $15) produced no measurable employment losses in affected regions. Therefore, a further increase to $25 would similarly help low-wage workers without harming employment.'
items.question: The advocate's argument depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.text: Researchers at leading universities produce more reliable minimum wage studies than other economists.
The lack of job losses seen between $7 and $15 would continue at a much higher level such as $25.
Every low-wage worker would gain by the same amount from a $25 minimum wage.
The current minimum wage is too low for a full-time worker to stay above the poverty line.

items.explanation_ko: 옹호자는 7달러에서 15달러로의 인상에서 고용 손실이 없었다는 연구를 근거로 25달러 인상도 마찬가지일 것이라고 결론짓는다. 이는 그 범위에서 관찰된 관계가 훨씬 높은 수준에서도 유지된다는 B를 전제해야만 성립한다. 오답: A는 연구 기관의 상대적 신뢰도에 관한 것으로 결론에 필요 없고, C는 모든 노동자가 '똑같이' 이득을 본다는 것인데 빈곤 감소에는 균등한 이득이 필요하지 않으며, D는 현행 최저임금으로 전일제 노동자가 빈곤선을 넘지 못한다는 것으로 인상이 빈곤을 줄인다는 주장에 반드시 필요한 전제는 아니다.

items.stimulus: A sociologist argues: 'There is now overwhelming evidence that smartphone use causes adolescent depression. Surveys show that teenagers who use smartphones more than three hours daily report depression symptoms at twice the rate of teenagers who use them less than one hour daily. The trend is global, with similar patterns documented in Australia, the U.S., the U.K., and South Korea. Public health authorities should treat smartphones as a primary risk factor for adolescent mental illness and recommend strict use limits.'
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the sociologist's argument?

options.text: Some teenagers use smartphones mostly for schoolwork, which may have neutral or even positive effects.
Some studies of smartphone use and adolescent mood were funded by technology companies.
The same link between heavy phone use and depression has been found in surveys from several other countries.
Studies tracking the same teenagers over time find depression usually comes before heavier phone use.

items.explanation_ko: 사회학자는 휴대전화 사용과 우울의 상관을 근거로 휴대전화가 우울을 '일으킨다'고 단정한다. D는 같은 청소년을 추적한 연구에서 우울이 휴대전화 사용 증가보다 먼저 나타난다고 하므로, 인과 방향이 반대일 수 있음을 보여 주장을 가장 크게 약화한다. 오답: A는 일부 청소년의 사용 목적에 관한 것으로 평균적 연관을 반박하지 못하고, B는 연구 자금 출처를 말하지만 어떤 연구인지, 결과가 어떻게 달라지는지 알 수 없어 논증과 연결되지 않으며, C는 다른 나라에서도 같은 연관이 나왔다는 것이어서 오히려 주장을 지지한다.

items.stimulus: The history of medicine reveals a striking pattern: groundbreaking treatments often face resistance not just from the public but from the medical establishment itself. When Ignaz Semmelweis demonstrated in 1847 that physicians washing their hands between patients dramatically reduced maternal mortality, his colleagues mocked him; his career was destroyed and he died in an asylum. When Barry Marshall proposed in the 1980s that bacteria—not stress, as universally believed—caused stomach ulcers, he was dismissed for years; he even infected himself with H. pylori and developed gastritis to demonstrate his point, and wide acceptance came only after later treatment trials. Both men were ultimately vindicated and their findings transformed medicine, but only after enormous personal cost and decades of preventable suffering by patients. Yet drawing the wrong lesson from these cases is also dangerous: most heterodox medical claims are rejected because they are wrong, not because expert consensus is unreliable. The challenge is recognising that legitimate expert consensus can sometimes be a barrier to genuine advances, while preserving the appropriate scepticism toward most novel claims that medical knowledge requires.
items.question: What is the author's central argument?

options.text: Expert consensus rightly filters most new claims but can sometimes block real advances; both must be kept in view.
Because experts wrongly rejected Semmelweis and Marshall, new treatments should be adopted without waiting for consensus.
Most medical innovations are rejected at first, which shows that expert consensus is generally unreliable.
Self-experimentation, as in Marshall's case, is the surest way to overcome resistance to new medical ideas.

items.explanation_ko: 저자는 제멜바이스와 마셜 사례처럼 전문가 합의가 진정한 진보를 막은 적이 있지만, 비주류 주장 대부분은 틀렸기 때문에 거부되므로 합의의 걸러내기 기능과 드문 패러다임 전환에 대한 개방성을 함께 유지해야 한다고 주장한다. A가 이 균형을 담는다. 오답: B는 합의를 기다리지 말자는 결론으로 저자가 경고한 '잘못된 교훈'에 해당하고, C는 대부분의 혁신이 처음 거부되며 합의가 신뢰할 수 없다고 해 지문과 반대이며, D는 자기 실험을 가장 확실한 방법으로 일반화했는데 지문은 마셜의 사례를 소개했을 뿐이다.

items.stimulus: Cancer mortality statistics are commonly reported as five-year survival rates: the percentage of patients diagnosed with a particular cancer who are alive five years later. By this measure, treatments and screening programmes appear to have made dramatic progress. Five-year survival for some cancers has risen from 20% in 1980 to 60% today. However, statisticians have raised an unsettling concern: this increase is partly a product of how survival is measured rather than how long patients actually live. When screening detects cancers earlier in their natural course, patients formally 'survive' longer from the moment of diagnosis even if the date of death is unchanged. This is called 'lead-time bias'. A related effect, 'length-time bias', means that screening tends to detect slower-growing cancers (which take more time in the screenable phase), inflating survival statistics for screened populations relative to unscreened ones, regardless of whether treatment actually helped.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: Cancer screening does not actually extend lives and should therefore be discontinued.
Rising five-year survival rates alone do not show that screening or treatment is extending lives.
All of the rise in five-year survival since 1980 is explained by lead-time and length-time bias.
Slower-growing cancers are more likely to be fatal than faster-growing cancers.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 조기 발견에 따른 리드타임 편향과 느리게 자라는 암을 더 많이 잡는 길이 편향 때문에, 실제 사망 시점이 같아도 5년 생존율이 오를 수 있다고 설명한다. 따라서 B처럼 5년 생존율 상승만으로는 수명 연장을 입증할 수 없다고 추론할 수 있다. 오답: A는 검진이 수명을 늘리지 않는다고 단정하고 중단까지 주장해 지문의 범위를 넘고, C는 상승이 '부분적으로' 측정 방식 때문이라는 지문을 '전부'로 확대했으며, D는 느리게 자라는 암이 더 치명적이라는 것으로 지문에서 근거를 찾을 수 없다.

items.stimulus: An economist proposes that a city-wide universal preschool program (offering free preschool to all 3-4 year-olds) would substantially reduce long-term inequality and yield economic returns far exceeding its costs. She bases the argument on research showing that early childhood education improves school readiness, later academic outcomes, and adult earnings. Critics object that (1) the cited research mostly comes from small, intensively funded pilot programs that may not scale to a city-wide implementation, (2) middle-class and wealthy families would benefit from a free service they could afford on their own, reducing the policy's progressive impact, and (3) the long-term economic returns assume current labour market conditions will persist for decades.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strongly support the economist's proposal against the critics' objections?

options.text: Universal preschool has been adopted in several countries and enjoys broad public approval there.
Many middle-income parents already pay for private preschool for their children out of their own pockets, often at high cost.
City-wide programs matched pilot results, helped low-income children most, and paid off under several job-market scenarios.
Some critics of the proposal have personal or financial links to private childcare providers.

items.explanation_ko: 비판자들은 (1) 소규모 시범 결과가 도시 규모로 재현되지 않을 수 있고, (2) 중산층까지 혜택을 받아 재분배 효과가 약해지며, (3) 장기 수익이 현재 노동시장 조건에 의존한다고 지적했다. C는 도시 단위 프로그램이 시범 결과를 재현했고, 저소득층 아동에게 가장 큰 이득이 돌아갔으며, 여러 노동시장 시나리오에서 수익을 냈다고 하므로 세 비판에 하나씩 대응해 가장 강하게 지지한다. 오답: A는 여론 지지일 뿐 효과 증거가 아니고, B는 중산층이 이미 비용을 낼 수 있다는 것이라 비판 (2)를 뒷받침하며, D는 비판자의 이해관계를 공격할 뿐 제안의 근거를 제공하지 않는다.

items.stimulus: A legal commentator argues against medical malpractice reform that would cap damages: 'High malpractice payouts are necessary to incentivise doctor competence. Countries with limited damages have higher rates of medical errors than those with unlimited damages. Therefore, capping damages would worsen patient safety. Reform proponents claim caps reduce healthcare costs by lowering insurance premiums, but this is a false economy: the cost of additional medical errors caused by reduced doctor care would exceed any savings on premiums.'
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the commentator's argument?

options.text: Several legal scholars have published papers arguing in favour of capping malpractice damages.
Countries with damage limits also have stronger licensing and accreditation; controlling for these removes the link.
Premium savings in countries with caps have been smaller than reform proponents usually claim.
Doctors in countries with unlimited damages pay noticeably higher malpractice insurance premiums on average.

items.explanation_ko: 평론가의 핵심 근거는 배상 제한 국가가 무제한 국가보다 의료 과오율이 높다는 비교이고, 이를 배상 제한이 의사의 주의를 떨어뜨린 결과로 해석한다. B는 제한 국가들이 면허·보수교육·인증 제도에서도 다르고 이를 통제하면 제한과 과오율의 관계가 사라진다고 하므로 인과 근거 자체를 무너뜨려 가장 크게 약화한다. 오답: A는 학자들의 의견일 뿐 실증 반박이 아니고, C는 상한제의 보험료 절감 효과가 작다는 것이어서 오히려 평론가의 '잘못된 절약' 주장을 거든다. D는 무제한 국가의 보험료가 높다는 것으로 상한제가 비용을 줄인다는 개혁 측 주장과 맞을 뿐, 과오율에 대한 평론가의 인과 주장을 건드리지 못한다.

items.stimulus: An education researcher argues: 'Students who use generative AI tools during their studies will become dependent on them and lose the ability to think critically. Studies show that students who frequently use spell-checkers have weaker spelling skills than those who do not, and students who use calculators heavily perform worse on mental arithmetic. The pattern is consistent: external cognitive tools weaken the corresponding internal capacities. Therefore, schools should ban generative AI tools during all coursework to preserve students' independent thinking abilities.'
items.question: The researcher's argument depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.text: What holds for narrow skills such as spelling and arithmetic also holds for the broader skill of critical thinking.
Generative AI tools have been widely available to secondary school and university students for several years already.
Students who rely heavily on calculators also tend to rely heavily on spell-checkers.
Critical thinking is more important than any other skill that schools aim to develop in students.

items.explanation_ko: 연구자는 맞춤법 검사기와 계산기처럼 좁고 명확한 기술에서 관찰된 '도구 사용이 내적 능력을 약화한다'는 패턴을 생성형 AI와 비판적 사고에 그대로 적용한다. 이 유비가 성립하려면 좁은 기술에서의 관계가 훨씬 넓고 복잡한 비판적 사고에도 일반화된다는 A가 참이어야 한다. 오답: B(AI 보급 기간)와 C(계산기와 맞춤법 검사기 사용자의 겹침)는 결론과 무관하고, D는 비판적 사고가 '가장' 중요한 능력이라는 것인데 금지 주장은 비판적 사고를 보존할 가치가 있다는 것만으로 충분하므로 필요 없다.

items.stimulus: Social science research has long faced a credibility problem known as the 'file drawer effect'. When researchers conduct studies, those that find statistically significant results tend to be submitted to journals and published, while those that find null results often remain unpublished in the researcher's file drawer. Over time, this selective publication distorts the apparent state of evidence: the published literature appears to confirm hypotheses far more strongly than the underlying research actually supports. The effect is particularly severe in fields with many small studies and flexible analytical choices. Recent reforms—pre-registration of hypotheses before data collection, registered reports that commit journals to publishing based on methodology rather than results, and meta-analyses that include unpublished studies—aim to address the problem but have been adopted unevenly across disciplines. In some fields, perhaps half of all studies remain unaccounted for in published evidence summaries.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: Published research in some social science fields probably overstates how well tested hypotheses are supported.
Most published findings in fields with a strong file drawer effect are probably false.
Pre-registration and registered reports have now largely solved the file drawer problem across disciplines.
Meta-analyses that include unpublished studies are less reliable than those limited to published work.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 유의미한 결과만 주로 출판되는 '서랍 효과' 때문에 출판된 문헌이 실제 증거보다 가설을 더 강하게 지지하는 것처럼 보이고, 개혁이 고르게 채택되지 않아 일부 분야에서는 연구의 절반가량이 증거 요약에서 빠져 있다고 말한다. 따라서 A처럼 일부 분야의 출판 문헌이 증거의 강도를 과대평가하고 있을 가능성이 높다고 추론할 수 있다. 오답: B는 과대평가를 '대부분 거짓'으로 비약했고, C는 개혁이 고르지 않게 채택됐다는 지문과 반대로 문제가 해결됐다고 하며, D는 미출판 연구를 포함한 메타분석이 문제를 줄이려는 개혁이라는 지문과 반대 방향이다.

items.stimulus: Dr. Reyes proposes that public health authorities should subsidise community-based exercise programmes for older adults rather than focusing exclusively on medical treatments for age-related chronic diseases. Her argument: while medical treatments address diseases after they develop, regular exercise can prevent or substantially delay the onset of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, and certain cancers. She estimates that a $50 million annual investment in community exercise infrastructure would save more in long-term healthcare costs than equivalent spending on additional medical treatment for the same conditions. Critics argue that older adults are unlikely to maintain consistent exercise programmes, that the cost-benefit projections are speculative, and that the savings are too long-term to justify the upfront investment.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strongly support Dr. Reyes's proposal against the critics' objections?

options.text: Several countries have introduced exercise subsidy programmes for older adults, with participation levels varying widely between regions.
Health authorities have recommended regular exercise for older adults for many decades.
Ten-year pilot data show most older participants still exercising, fewer heart disease cases, and net savings by year four.
Some critics of the proposal have ties to companies that sell treatments for chronic disease.

items.explanation_ko: 비판자들은 (1) 노인이 운동을 꾸준히 유지하지 못하고, (2) 비용 편익 추정이 추측에 불과하며, (3) 절감이 너무 장기적이라고 지적했다. C는 10년 시범 자료로 참여 유지, 심혈관 질환 감소, 4년 차까지의 순절감을 보여 세 비판에 하나씩 대응하므로 제안을 가장 강하게 지지한다. 오답: A는 여러 나라가 도입했다는 사실일 뿐 효과 자료가 없고, B는 운동을 오래 권장해 왔다는 일반론으로 비판에 답하지 못하며, D는 비판자의 이해관계를 공격할 뿐 제안의 근거를 제공하지 않는다.

items.stimulus: Public concern about misinformation tends to focus on its most visible forms—deliberately fabricated news stories, conspiracy theories, viral hoaxes. These are real problems, but research suggests they may not be the most consequential. A more pervasive challenge is what researchers call 'context collapse': true information stripped of the qualifications, caveats, and contextual signals that gave it meaning in its original setting, then circulated to audiences for whom that context is invisible. A scientific finding presented to specialist colleagues with all its uncertainties properly framed can become, after repeated reposting, a confident-sounding viral claim that misrepresents the underlying evidence even though no individual statement is technically false. Combating outright falsehoods is straightforward in principle. Combating context collapse is harder because the problem is not what is said but what surrounds saying—and the architecture of modern platforms systematically strips away exactly those surrounding signals.
items.question: What is the author's central argument?

options.text: Fabricated news stories are no longer a significant problem in today's media environment.
Since true claims can also mislead, all viral content should be treated as misinformation by default.
True information stripped of context is a harder problem than outright falsehood, and platforms worsen it.
Scientific findings should be shared only among specialists so that they cannot be misrepresented.

items.explanation_ko: 저자는 조작된 뉴스도 실제 문제이지만, 더 광범위하고 해결이 어려운 문제는 참인 정보가 맥락을 잃고 퍼지는 '맥락 붕괴'이며 플랫폼 구조가 그 맥락 신호를 체계적으로 제거한다고 주장한다. C가 이를 정확히 담는다. 오답: A는 조작 뉴스를 '실제 문제'라고 한 지문과 어긋나고, B는 참인 주장도 오도할 수 있다는 점을 '모든 바이럴 콘텐츠를 허위정보로 보라'로 비약했으며, D는 과학적 발견의 공유 범위를 제한하자는 처방으로 지문에 없다.

items.stimulus: A philosopher of mathematics argues: 'Mathematical objects exist independently of human minds. Two thousand years ago, mathematicians proved theorems about prime numbers that remain true today—not because mathematicians today agree with the ancient ones, but because the theorems describe properties of objects that exist in some genuine, mind-independent way. If mathematical objects were merely human inventions, we would expect different cultures developing mathematics independently to produce different mathematical truths. Yet mathematicians from completely different traditions discover the same theorems, the same patterns, the same constants. This convergence cannot be explained by anything other than the existence of an external mathematical reality that all mathematicians are exploring.'
items.question: The philosopher's argument depends on which of the following assumptions?

options.text: Mathematicians in every era and culture have agreed on all mathematical theorems.
Ancient mathematicians understood the properties of prime numbers as thoroughly as mathematicians do today.
Mathematical truths are more certain than truths discovered in the natural sciences.
The shared results of separate traditions cannot be explained by common human cognition or common problems.

items.explanation_ko: 철학자는 서로 독립적인 수학 전통들이 같은 정리와 상수에 도달한다는 수렴을 '외부의 수학적 실재 외에는 설명할 수 없다'고 결론짓는다. 이 결론은 그 수렴이 인간에게 공통된 인지 구조나 비슷한 실용적 문제 같은 다른 요인으로 설명될 수 없다는 D가 참이어야만 성립한다. 오답: A는 모든 수학자가 모든 정리에 동의한다는 것으로 논증은 그런 완전한 합의를 요구하지 않고, B는 고대 수학자의 이해 수준에 관한 것이라 정리가 여전히 참이라는 논점과 무관하며, C는 수학적 진리와 자연과학적 진리의 확실성 비교로 결론에 쓰이지 않는다.

items.stimulus: An automotive industry advocate argues: 'Self-driving cars should be approved for unrestricted public road use immediately. Recent industry statistics show that human-driven vehicles cause 1.3 fatalities per 100 million miles driven, while autonomous vehicles in current testing cause only 0.8 fatalities per 100 million miles. Self-driving technology is already safer than human drivers. Continuing to require additional testing or restrictions delays the deployment of life-saving technology and effectively kills people.'
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the advocate's argument?

options.text: Some executives who support approval have financial stakes in autonomous vehicle companies.
The autonomous figure covers only simple test conditions, where human drivers have just 0.4 deaths per 100 million miles.
Self-driving cars need costly sensors and computers that make them dearer than ordinary cars.
Some opponents of self-driving cars object to automation on broadly ideological grounds and would oppose approval under any safety data.

items.explanation_ko: 옹호자는 자율주행차의 사망률(1억 마일당 0.8)이 사람 운전(1.3)보다 낮다는 비교로 즉시 무제한 승인을 주장한다. B는 자율주행 수치가 단순한 시험 조건에서만 산출되었고, 같은 조건의 사람 운전 사망률은 0.4에 불과하다고 하므로 비교 자체가 불공정하며 오히려 사람이 더 안전할 수 있음을 보여 가장 크게 약화한다. 오답: A와 D는 찬반 양측 인물의 이해관계나 성향을 공격할 뿐 안전성 자료를 다루지 않고, C는 차량 비용 문제로 '더 안전하다'는 핵심 주장과 무관하다.

items.stimulus: Political scientists studying democratic backsliding—the gradual erosion of democratic institutions in countries that were previously considered consolidated democracies—have identified a paradoxical pattern. Backsliding rarely begins with overt assaults on democratic institutions. Instead, it typically proceeds through legal channels: elected leaders use their authority to weaken courts, alter electoral rules, restrict press freedoms, and concentrate power, all while maintaining the appearance of democratic legitimacy. Critics in such systems are often dismissed as 'alarmist' precisely because each individual change appears modest in isolation, even as their cumulative effect transforms the political system. By the time the pattern becomes obvious enough to galvanise broad opposition, the institutional means to reverse it have often been compromised. Recovery, when it occurs, typically requires extraordinary mobilisation rather than routine democratic processes.
items.question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the passage?

options.text: Strong executive leadership is incompatible with maintaining a democratic political system.
Countries that experience democratic backsliding can recover only with sustained pressure from foreign governments.
Because each step seems minor, backsliding can erode the means of reversing it before opposition forms.
Citizens who warn early about democratic erosion are usually proved right in the end.

items.explanation_ko: 지문은 민주주의 후퇴가 합법적 경로로 조금씩 진행되어 각 단계가 사소해 보이고, 패턴이 분명해질 무렵에는 이를 되돌릴 제도적 수단이 이미 훼손되어 있다고 설명한다. C가 이 '점진성 때문에 정상적 절차로 대응하기 어렵다'는 구조를 담는다. 오답: A는 강한 행정부 리더십과 민주주의가 양립할 수 없다는 일반화로 지문에 없고, B는 회복에 외국 정부의 압력이 필요하다고 했는데 지문은 회복에 '비상한 동원'이 필요하다고만 했으며, D는 초기 경고자가 대체로 옳다는 평가로 지문은 그들이 '과장된다고 무시된다'고만 했다.

items.stimulus: Ethical decision-making in professional life rarely matches the clean structure of philosophical thought experiments. Real situations involve incomplete information, time pressure, emotional stakes, conflicting obligations, and consequences that ripple through multiple lives in ways that cannot be fully foreseen. A clinician deciding how to allocate scarce resources, a journalist deciding what private information to publish, a manager deciding whom to lay off—each faces choices where every available option imposes serious harm on someone, where the relevant facts are partly unknown, and where reasonable people examining the same situation reach different conclusions. The philosophical literature offers important conceptual tools, but these tools illuminate ethical structure rather than dictate ethical answers. The actual work of ethical practice involves judgement under uncertainty, maintained while bearing the weight of consequences that cannot be undone. This is not a deficiency of ethical reasoning but its proper character—an honest engagement with the genuine difficulty of doing right in conditions where the right answer is rarely fully visible.
items.question: What is the author's central argument?

options.text: Ethical reasoning cannot be relied on when real professional decisions involve uncertainty.
Professionals facing hard dilemmas should look to the philosophical literature for clear and definitive answers to them.
Real ethical practice means judgement under uncertainty, and this difficulty is its proper character, not a flaw.
Every professional ethical decision involves choosing between two or more conflicting obligations.

items.explanation_ko: 저자는 실제 직업 윤리의 결정이 불완전한 정보, 시간 압박, 상충하는 의무 속에서 이루어지며, 철학적 도구는 답을 정해 주지 않고 구조를 비추어 줄 뿐이라고 하면서, 불확실성 속의 판단이라는 어려움은 결함이 아니라 윤리적 실천의 본래 성격이라고 주장한다. C가 이를 담는다. 오답: A는 저자가 '결함이 아니다'라고 한 것과 반대로 윤리적 추론을 믿을 수 없다고 하고, B는 철학 문헌이 답을 정해 주지 않는다는 지문과 반대이며, D는 '모든' 결정이 상충하는 의무를 포함한다고 확대한 세부 일반화로 중심 주장이 아니다.

items.stimulus:
A clinic recorded patient consultation times (minutes) by department over five days:

| Department  | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri |
|-------------|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|
| General     | 12  | 15  | 14  | 13  | 16  |
| Pediatric   | 18  | 22  | 20  | 19  | 21  |
| Cardiology  | 25  | 28  | 30  | 26  | 31  |
| Dermatology | 10  | 12  | 11  | 9   | 13  |
items.question: Which department's average consultation time across the five days is closest to twice the average of the department with the shortest mean consultation time?

options.text: General
Pediatric
Cardiology
No department's mean is close to twice the shortest mean.

items.explanation_ko: 각 과 평균은 General 14분, Pediatric 20분, Cardiology 28분, Dermatology 11분이다. 가장 짧은 평균은 Dermatology 11분이고 그 두 배는 22분이다. 22분과의 차이는 Pediatric 2분, Cardiology 6분, General 8분이므로 Pediatric이 가장 가깝다. 오답: A는 8분 차이로 가장 멀다. C는 가장 긴 평균이지만 22분보다 6분 많다. D는 2분 차이로 충분히 가까운 과가 있으므로 틀리다.

items.stimulus: A regional medical school enrolled 800 students in 2020. By 2024, total enrollment had increased to 1,000 students. In 2020, the gender split was 55% female and 45% male. In 2024, the proportion of female students had decreased by 5 percentage points compared to 2020.
items.question: How many more male students were enrolled in 2024 compared to 2020?
items.explanation_ko: 2020년 남학생은 800 × 45% = 360명이다. 2024년 여학생 비율은 55%에서 5%p 내려간 50%이므로 남학생도 50%, 즉 1,000 × 50% = 500명이다. 증가분은 500 − 360 = 140명이다. 오답: A는 전체 증가 200명을 반으로 나눈 값이다. C와 D는 남학생 비율 변화를 잘못 적용한 값이다.

items.stimulus:
A clinic recorded daily new patient registrations over four weeks (Mon-Fri only):

Week 1: Mon 12, Tue 18, Wed 14, Thu 16, Fri 25 (total 85)
Week 2: Mon 14, Tue 20, Wed 15, Thu 18, Fri 28 (total 95)
Week 3: Mon 16, Tue 22, Wed 16, Thu 20, Fri 31 (total 105)
Week 4: Mon 18, Tue 24, Wed 17, Thu 22, Fri 34 (total 115)
items.question: Which of the following statements is best supported by the data?

options.text: Wednesday and Friday registrations are growing at the same percentage rate from week to week.
Friday registrations consistently account for more than 25% of total weekly registrations.
Total weekly registrations grew by approximately 15% from Week 1 to Week 4.
Each weekday's registrations grew by an equal absolute number from week to week.

items.explanation_ko: 금요일 비중은 25/85 = 29.4%, 28/95 = 29.5%, 31/105 = 29.5%, 34/115 = 29.6%로 매주 25%를 넘으므로 B가 옳다. 오답: A는 수요일이 주당 +1, 금요일이 +3씩 늘어 증가율이 다르다. C는 85에서 115로 약 35.3% 증가했으므로 15%가 아니다. D는 월·화·목은 +2, 수는 +1, 금은 +3으로 요일마다 증가량이 다르다.

items.stimulus:
A medical screening test for a particular disease has the following characteristics:
- Sensitivity: 95% (correctly identifies 95% of people who have the disease)
- Specificity: 90% (correctly identifies 90% of people who do NOT have the disease)

In a population of 10,000 people, 200 actually have the disease.
items.question: Of all people who test positive in this population, approximately what proportion actually has the disease?

options.text: About 16%
About 50%
About 86%
About 95%

items.explanation_ko: 질병자 200명 중 양성은 200 × 95% = 190명(진양성)이다. 비질병자 9,800명 중 양성은 9,800 × 10% = 980명(위양성)이다. 양성 판정자 1,170명 중 실제 환자는 190명이므로 190 / 1,170 ≈ 16%이다. 오답: B는 진양성과 위양성이 비슷하다고 가정한 값이다. C는 근거 없는 수치이다. D는 민감도 95%를 양성 예측도로 착각한 값이다.

items.stimulus:
A research lab uses four reagents to run a single experiment, with the following requirements and bulk-pack pricing:

| Reagent | Per Experiment | Sold In         | Price per Pack |
|---------|---------------|-----------------|----------------|
| A       | 3 units       | 10-unit packs   | $80            |
| B       | 2 units       | 5-unit packs    | $50            |
| C       | 5 units       | 20-unit packs   | $90            |
| D       | 1 unit        | 4-unit packs    | $48            |

Reagents must be purchased in whole packs (no partial packs). Unused reagent cannot be returned but can be used for future experiments.
items.question: What is the minimum total cost to run exactly 6 experiments, assuming the lab starts with no reagent inventory?
items.explanation_ko: 6회 실험에 A는 18단위로 10단위 팩 2개($160), B는 12단위로 5단위 팩 3개($150), C는 30단위로 20단위 팩 2개($180), D는 6단위로 4단위 팩 2개($96)가 필요하다. 합계는 160 + 150 + 180 + 96 = $586이다. 오답: A($566)는 한 시약의 팩 수를 적게 잡는 등 올림 처리를 빠뜨린 값이다. C($610)와 D($640)는 팩을 필요 이상으로 계산한 값이다.

items.stimulus: A clinical research team measured patient recovery times (in days) for 9 patients undergoing a particular procedure: 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 45.
items.question: What can we conclude by comparing the mean and median of this data set?

options.text: The mean is lower than the median, indicating that the data are skewed to the left.
The mean (about 10.6 days) is the better summary of a typical patient because it uses every value.
The mean (about 10.6 days) is well above the median (6 days) because of one extreme value, so the median better represents a typical patient.
Removing the 45-day value would lower the median by more than it lowers the mean.

items.explanation_ko: 합계는 95이므로 평균은 95 / 9 ≈ 10.6일이고, 9개 값의 다섯 번째인 중앙값은 6일이다. 45일 한 명이 평균을 크게 끌어올려 평균이 중앙값보다 훨씬 크므로, 전형적인 환자를 나타내는 데는 중앙값이 더 적절하다. 오답: A는 평균이 중앙값보다 크므로 왼쪽 치우침이 아니다. B는 극단값에 끌려간 평균이 전형적 환자를 대표하지 못한다. D는 45를 빼면 중앙값은 6에서 5.5로 0.5 줄지만 평균은 10.6에서 6.25로 크게 줄어 반대이다.

items.stimulus: An ambulance travels from a rural clinic to a city hospital at 60 km/h, then returns along the same route at 40 km/h (slower due to traffic). The two distances (clinic to hospital and hospital to clinic) are identical.
items.question: What is the ambulance's average speed for the entire round trip?

options.text: 45 km/h
50 km/h
48 km/h
52 km/h

items.explanation_ko: 편도 거리를 120 km로 두면 가는 데 120 / 60 = 2시간, 오는 데 120 / 40 = 3시간이 걸린다. 왕복 240 km를 5시간에 갔으므로 평균 속력은 240 / 5 = 48 km/h이다. 오답: B(50)는 두 속력을 단순 평균한 함정이다. 느린 구간에 더 오래 머물기 때문에 평균은 50보다 작다. A(45)와 D(52)는 계산 근거가 없다.

items.stimulus:
Emergency department patients are categorised by triage level. In a particular ED:
- 60% of patients are Triage 1 (lower acuity); of these, 30% are admitted to the hospital
- 40% of patients are Triage 2 (higher acuity); of these, 80% are admitted to the hospital
items.question: If a randomly selected patient is admitted, what is the probability they were Triage 2?

options.text: About 40%
About 50%
About 80%
About 64%

items.explanation_ko: 환자 100명 기준으로 Triage 1은 60명 중 30%인 18명, Triage 2는 40명 중 80%인 32명이 입원한다. 입원자 50명 중 Triage 2는 32명이므로 32 / 50 = 64%이다. 오답: A(40%)는 전체 환자 중 Triage 2 비율이다. B(50%)는 입원자 수 50과 혼동한 값이다. C(80%)는 Triage 2의 입원율로, 조건의 방향을 뒤집은 것이다.

items.stimulus: A pilot trial of a new blood pressure medication showed a 5 mmHg reduction compared to placebo, with 80% statistical power requiring 800 patients per group. The research team is now planning a follow-up trial designed to detect a smaller but clinically still meaningful 3 mmHg reduction, using the same statistical assumptions (80% power, α = 0.05, same outcome variability). Under these assumptions, the required sample size per group is inversely proportional to the square of the effect size to be detected.
items.question: Approximately how many patients per group will be required in the follow-up trial?

options.text: About 480
About 800
About 2,222
About 1,333

items.explanation_ko: 표본 크기는 검출할 효과 크기의 제곱에 반비례한다. 효과가 5에서 3 mmHg로 줄면 필요 표본은 (5/3)² ≈ 2.78배가 되므로 800 × 2.78 ≈ 2,222명이다. 오답: A(480)는 효과 크기에 비례해 표본이 준다고 본 값(800 × 3/5)이다. B(800)는 효과 크기의 영향을 무시했다. D(1,333)는 제곱 없이 단순 반비례(800 × 5/3)만 적용한 값이다.

items.stimulus: A medical claims processing centre has measured productivity. With 6 staff working 8 hours each, they process 200 insurance claims per day. The work rate per person-hour is constant. The centre is considering staffing 5 staff for 10 hours each instead.
items.question: Approximately how many claims per day will the centre process under the new staffing plan?

options.text: About 167 claims
About 200 claims
About 240 claims
About 208 claims

items.explanation_ko: 현재 6명 × 8시간 = 48인시로 200건을 처리하므로 인시당 200 / 48 ≈ 4.17건이다. 새 계획은 5명 × 10시간 = 50인시이므로 200 × 50 / 48 ≈ 208건이다. 오답: A(167)는 인원 감소만 반영하고 근무 시간 증가를 무시했다. B(200)는 인시 변화를 반영하지 않았다. C(240)는 근거 없는 값이다.

items.stimulus:
A health survey of 1,000 adults reported the following:

- 60% reported regular exercise (≥3 sessions/week)
- 40% reported regular exercise + healthy diet
- 25% reported regular exercise + healthy diet + adequate sleep (≥7 hours nightly)
- 30% reported NEITHER regular exercise NOR healthy diet
- 'Healthy diet' was self-reported following recommended guidelines
items.question: How many adults reported a healthy diet (regardless of exercise status)?

options.text: About 250
About 500
About 400
About 600

items.explanation_ko: 운동하지 않는 사람은 100% − 60% = 40%이고, 그중 운동도 식단도 하지 않는 사람이 30%이므로 운동은 안 하고 식단만 지키는 사람은 10%이다. 식단을 지키는 사람은 운동+식단 40%와 식단만 10%를 더한 50%, 즉 500명이다. 수면 25% 정보는 풀이에 필요 없는 정보이다. 오답: A(250)는 세 조건을 모두 만족하는 인원이다. C(400)는 운동과 식단을 함께 하는 인원만 센 값이다. D(600)는 운동하는 인원과 혼동한 값이다.

items.stimulus:
A medical researcher must choose between two treatment plans for a patient with a serious condition:

Plan A: 70% chance of full recovery (utility = 100), 30% chance of partial recovery with mild ongoing symptoms (utility = 60).

Plan B: 50% chance of full recovery (utility = 100), 30% chance of partial recovery (utility = 60), 20% chance of no improvement (utility = 0).
items.question: Which plan has the higher expected utility, and by how much?

options.text: The two plans have equal expected utility
Plan A by 8 utility points (88 vs 80)
Plan B by 8 utility points (88 vs 96)
Plan A by 20 utility points (88 vs 68)

items.explanation_ko: Plan A의 기대 효용은 0.7 × 100 + 0.3 × 60 = 70 + 18 = 88이다. Plan B는 0.5 × 100 + 0.3 × 60 + 0.2 × 0 = 50 + 18 + 0 = 68이다. 따라서 Plan A가 20점 높다. 오답: A는 두 값이 다르므로 틀리다. B는 Plan B를 80으로 잘못 계산했다. C는 방향과 수치가 모두 틀렸다.

items.stimulus: A clinic schedules patient appointments in 20-minute slots. The clinic operates from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM with a 1-hour lunch break starting at noon.
items.question: How many patient appointment slots are available in a single day?
items.explanation_ko: 오전 8시부터 오후 5시까지는 9시간이고 점심 1시간을 빼면 8시간, 즉 480분이다. 20분 단위로 나누면 480 / 20 = 24개이다. 오답: A(18)와 B(21)는 운영 시간을 짧게 잡은 값이다. D(27)는 점심시간을 빼지 않은 값(540 / 20)이다.

items.stimulus: A medical textbook originally costs $180. The bookstore offers a 25% student discount, and additionally, paying with the school's prepaid card provides an extra 10% off the discounted price.
items.question: What is the final price of the textbook with both discounts applied?
items.explanation_ko: 학생 할인 후 가격은 $180 × 0.75 = $135이고, 추가 10% 할인은 이 할인된 가격에 적용되므로 $135 × 0.9 = $121.50이다. 오답: B($117)는 25%와 10%를 더해 35%를 한 번에 할인한 값이다. D($135)는 두 번째 할인을 빼먹은 값이다. C($126)는 계산 근거가 없다.

items.stimulus:
A pharmacist must prepare 100 mL of a 30% antiseptic solution by mixing two existing solutions:
- Solution X: 60% antiseptic concentration
- Solution Y: 20% antiseptic concentration
items.question: How many mL of each solution should the pharmacist mix?

options.text: 20 mL X + 80 mL Y
30 mL X + 70 mL Y
25 mL X + 75 mL Y
40 mL X + 60 mL Y

items.stimulus: A clinical trial has two phases. Phase 1 has a 70% probability of success. If Phase 1 succeeds, Phase 2 has a 50% probability of success. If Phase 1 fails, the trial ends immediately and Phase 2 is not conducted. Phase 2 success requires Phase 1 success first.
items.question: What is the probability that the trial completes both phases successfully?
items.explanation_ko: 두 단계가 모두 성공하려면 1단계 성공(0.7) 뒤 2단계 성공(0.5)이 이어져야 하므로 0.7 × 0.5 = 0.35, 즉 35%이다. 오답: A(30%)는 1단계 실패 확률이다. B(85%)는 둘 중 하나라도 성공할 확률 공식을 잘못 쓴 값이다. C(60%)는 두 확률을 평균한 값이다.

items.stimulus:
Two clinical trials measured the same outcome (improvement scores from 0-100):

- Trial A: mean = 75, standard deviation = 5
- Trial B: mean = 75, standard deviation = 18

Both trials had similar sample sizes.
items.question: Which statement most accurately compares the two trials?

options.text: The two trials show equivalent results because their means are identical.
Trial B is more reliable because its wider spread captures more of the variation among patients.
Patients in Trial A responded more consistently, whereas Trial B suggests that responses varied considerably between patients.
Trial B must have included patients who showed no improvement at all.

items.explanation_ko: 두 시험의 평균은 같지만 표준편차는 A가 5, B가 18이다. 표준편차가 작은 A는 환자들이 75 근처에 모여 반응이 일관적이고, B는 점수가 넓게 퍼져 환자마다 반응 차이가 크다. 오답: A는 평균만 같을 뿐 분포가 달라 동등하다고 할 수 없다. B는 퍼짐이 크다고 신뢰도가 높아지지 않는다. D는 표준편차만으로 개선이 전혀 없었던 환자가 있었는지 단정할 수 없다.

items.stimulus: A medical student deposits $5,000 into a savings account that earns 6% interest compounded annually (the interest is added to the principal each year, and the next year's interest is calculated on the new total).
items.question: Approximately how much will the account contain after 5 years?

options.text: About $5,500
About $6,700
About $6,500
About $6,000

items.explanation_ko: 복리 공식으로 $5,000 × 1.06⁵ ≈ $5,000 × 1.3382 ≈ $6,691이므로 약 $6,700이다. 오답: C($6,500)는 매년 $300씩 단리로 더한 값이다. A($5,500)와 D($6,000)는 기간이나 이자를 지나치게 작게 잡은 값이다.

items.stimulus:
In a population of 1,000 patients screened in a clinic:
- 8% have a particular disease
- 75% of patients with the disease present a specific symptom
- 10% of patients without the disease also present that symptom (likely due to other causes)
items.question: How many patients in this population would be expected to present this specific symptom?
items.explanation_ko: 질병자는 1,000 × 8% = 80명이고 그중 75%인 60명이 증상을 보인다. 비질병자 920명 중 10%인 92명도 증상을 보인다. 증상자는 60 + 92 = 152명이다. 오답: A(60)는 질병자 중 증상자만, B(92)는 비질병자 중 증상자만 센 값이다. C(180)는 근거 없는 합이다.

items.stimulus: A medical equipment store offers a 25% discount on a particular model of stethoscope. The discounted price is $90.
items.question: What was the original price (before discount)?
items.explanation_ko: 할인가 $90은 원가의 75%이므로 원가는 90 / 0.75 = $120이다. 확인하면 $120의 25%는 $30이고 $120 − $30 = $90이다. 오답: B($112.50)는 할인가에 25%를 더한 함정으로, 할인율의 기준이 원가임을 놓쳤다. C와 D는 근거 없는 값이다.

items.stimulus: A clinical trial reports its primary result: 'The new treatment reduced symptom severity by an average of 18% compared to placebo, with a p-value of 0.003 (the prespecified threshold for significance was p < 0.01).' The trial enrolled 240 patients with prespecified inclusion criteria and used the same outcome measure that the trial protocol named in advance.
items.question: Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of the p-value of 0.003?

options.text: If the treatment had no real effect (the null hypothesis were true), there would be only a 0.3% probability of observing a result this strong (or stronger) by chance alone.
The new treatment reduces symptoms by 0.3% on average; the 18% figure is not credible.
There is a 99.7% probability that the new treatment is genuinely effective.
The treatment will produce symptom reduction in 99.7% of patients who receive it.

items.explanation_ko: p값은 귀무가설(효과 없음)이 참이라고 가정할 때 관찰된 결과만큼 또는 그보다 극단적인 결과가 우연히 나올 확률이다. 따라서 p = 0.003은 효과가 없다면 이런 결과가 나올 확률이 0.3%라는 뜻이다. 오답: B는 p값을 효과 크기로 착각했다. C는 p값을 가설이 참일 확률로 뒤집어 해석했다. D는 p값을 효과를 보는 환자 비율로 오해했다.

items.stimulus:
A medical screening protocol uses two independent diagnostic tests in sequence. Test A is administered first; only if Test A is positive does the patient receive Test B. A patient is treated only if BOTH tests come back positive.

- Test A: sensitivity 90%, specificity 80%
- Test B: sensitivity 85%, specificity 95%

The two tests' results are statistically independent given the patient's true disease status.
items.question: For a patient who actually has the disease, what is the probability they will be correctly identified for treatment (i.e., both tests return positive)?
items.explanation_ko: 실제 환자가 치료를 받으려면 두 검사가 모두 양성이어야 한다. 환자에게 양성이 나올 확률은 각 검사의 민감도이고 두 검사가 독립이므로 0.90 × 0.85 = 0.765, 즉 76.5%이다. 특이도는 비질병자에 대한 값이라 이 계산에 쓰이지 않는다. 오답: D(87.5%)는 두 민감도를 평균 낸 값이다. B(72.5%)와 C(82.5%)는 계산 근거가 없다.

items.stimulus:
A medical school admissions committee evaluates candidates using three weighted components:

- GPA (Grade Point Average): 40% of total composite score
- ISAT (entrance exam): 35% of total composite score
- Interview performance: 25% of total composite score

A candidate's component scores (each on a 0-100 scale): GPA = 85, ISAT = 72, Interview = 90.
items.question: What is the candidate's total weighted composite score?

items.stimulus:
Two hospitals reported their performance metrics for similar patient populations:

| Metric                            | Hospital A | Hospital B |
|-----------------------------------|------------|------------|
| Annual surgical procedures        | 8,000      | 4,500      |
| Surgical mortality rate           | 2.0%       | 1.5%       |
| Average length of stay (days)     | 5.5        | 6.8        |
| Postoperative infection rate      | 4.5%       | 2.8%       |
| Cost per procedure                | $18,500    | $24,000    |
| Patient satisfaction (% favourable)| 78         | 88         |
items.question: Which of the following statements is best supported by the data?

options.text: Hospital A performs better overall, because it carries out about 78% more procedures at a lower cost per procedure.
Hospital B performs better on every measure in the table, so it is clearly the superior hospital.
The data show that lower infection rates cause higher patient satisfaction.
Hospital A is stronger on volume and cost, while Hospital B is stronger on mortality, infection and satisfaction, so the better choice depends on priorities.

items.explanation_ko: A병원은 수술 건수가 많고 건당 비용이 낮다. B병원은 사망률(1.5%), 감염률(2.8%), 만족도(88%)가 더 좋다. 한 병원이 모든 지표에서 앞서지 않으므로 우선순위에 따라 판단이 달라진다는 D가 가장 잘 뒷받침된다. 오답: A는 건수와 비용만 보고 임상 결과의 열세를 무시했다. B는 B병원이 건수와 비용에서 뒤지므로 '모든 지표'가 틀렸다. C는 병원 두 곳의 자료로 인과관계를 주장할 수 없다.

items.stimulus:
Researchers studying a new analgesic drug found that its effectiveness E (measured as % reduction in pain scores) follows a dose-response relationship described by:

E = -0.5D² + 8D

where D is the dose in milligrams. The formula is empirically valid for doses between 0 and 16 mg. Beyond a certain dose, increasing D further actually reduces effectiveness due to receptor saturation and adverse effects.
items.question: What dose D maximises the drug's effectiveness, and what is that maximum effectiveness?

options.text: D = 4 mg, maximum effectiveness = 24
D = 8 mg, maximum effectiveness = 32
D = 6 mg, maximum effectiveness = 30
D = 16 mg, maximum effectiveness = 0

items.explanation_ko: E = −0.5D² + 8D는 위로 볼록한 이차함수이므로 꼭짓점 D = −8 / (2 × −0.5) = 8에서 최대이다. 이때 E = −0.5 × 64 + 64 = 32이다. 오답: A(D = 4, E = 24)와 C(D = 6, E = 30)는 값 자체는 맞지만 최대가 아니다. D(D = 16, E = 0)는 범위 끝으로 효과가 0이 되는 지점이다.

items.stimulus:
A study recorded the number of doctor visits per year for 100 adults:
- 0 visits: 15 people
- 1 visit: 25 people
- 2 visits: 30 people
- 3 visits: 18 people
- 4 or more visits: 12 people
items.question: What percentage of adults visited a doctor at least twice in the year?
items.explanation_ko: '최소 2회'는 2회, 3회, 4회 이상을 모두 포함하므로 30 + 18 + 12 = 60명, 즉 60%이다. 오답: C(48%)는 4회 이상 방문자를 빠뜨린 값(30 + 18)이다. B(55%)와 D(70%)는 근거 없는 값이다. '2회 초과'로 잘못 읽으면 30%가 된다.

items.stimulus: A team of 6 nurses can complete patient rounds in 2 hours.
items.question: How long would it take 4 nurses to complete the same rounds, assuming all nurses work at the same rate?

options.text: 2.5 hours
3.5 hours
3 hours
4 hours

items.explanation_ko: 전체 작업량은 6명 × 2시간 = 12인시이므로 4명이면 12 / 4 = 3시간이 걸린다. 오답: A(2.5시간)는 인원 감소 효과를 작게 본 값이다. B(3.5시간)와 D(4시간)는 근거 없는 값이다.

items.stimulus:
Average daily sleep hours by age group (survey of adults):

| Age Group | Average Sleep (hours) |
|-----------|----------------------|
| 18-25     | 7.8                  |
| 26-40     | 7.0                  |
| 41-55     | 6.5                  |
| 56-70     | 6.8                  |
| 71+       | 7.2                  |
items.question: Which statement is best supported by the data?

options.text: Sleep duration decreases continuously with age.
Young adults sleep less than the elderly.
Sleep duration is shortest in middle-aged adults (41-55) and increases again in older adults.
All age groups average more than 7 hours of sleep.

items.explanation_ko: 수면 시간은 18–25세 7.8시간에서 41–55세 6.5시간까지 줄었다가 56–70세 6.8시간, 71세 이상 7.2시간으로 다시 늘어난다. 따라서 중년층이 가장 짧고 노년층에서 다시 늘어난다는 C가 옳다. 오답: A는 56–70세에서 다시 늘어나므로 계속 줄지 않는다. B는 청년층(7.8)이 노년층(7.2)보다 더 오래 잔다. D는 41–55세와 56–70세가 7시간 미만이다.

items.stimulus:
Two independent diagnostic tests are used in sequence to screen for a particular condition. For a healthy individual (no disease):
- Test A correctly returns negative 95% of the time (specificity 95%)
- Test B correctly returns negative 92% of the time (specificity 92%)

The two test results are statistically independent.
items.question: If a healthy person takes both tests, what is the probability that at least one test will incorrectly return positive (false positive on at least one test)?
items.explanation_ko: 건강한 사람이 두 검사 모두 음성일 확률은 0.95 × 0.92 = 0.874이다. 적어도 하나가 위양성일 확률은 1 − 0.874 = 0.126, 즉 12.6%이다. 오답: A(5%)와 C(8%)는 각 검사 하나의 위양성률이다. D는 두 위양성률을 단순히 더한 13%와도 다른 근거 없는 값이며, 단순 합은 둘 다 위양성인 경우를 두 번 세게 된다.

items.stimulus: A medical conference had 240 registered attendees. Members paid $100 each, and non-members paid $150 each. The total registration revenue was $30,000.
items.question: How many members and how many non-members attended?

options.text: 120 members and 120 non-members
100 members and 140 non-members
150 members and 90 non-members
180 members and 60 non-members

items.explanation_ko: 회원을 x명이라 하면 100x + 150(240 − x) = 30,000이므로 36,000 − 50x = 30,000, x = 120이다. 따라서 회원 120명, 비회원 120명이다. 평균 등록비 $125가 $100과 $150의 중간이라는 점으로도 바로 알 수 있다. 오답: B는 $31,000, C는 $28,500, D는 $27,000이 된다.

items.stimulus: Five medical students take their first ISAT mock exam. Their scores average 78. A sixth student then takes the same exam, and the new average for all six students rises to 80.
items.question: What was the sixth student's score on the exam?
items.explanation_ko: 5명 합계는 5 × 78 = 390, 6명 합계는 6 × 80 = 480이므로 여섯 번째 학생은 480 − 390 = 90점이다. 오답: B(88)이면 평균이 약 79.7, C(85)이면 약 79.2, D(92)이면 약 80.3이 된다.

items.stimulus: In a particular metropolitan region, two hospitals treat all stroke patients. Hospital A treats 40% of regional stroke cases; Hospital B treats the remaining 60%. Of patients treated at Hospital A, 90% achieve full recovery within six months. Of patients treated at Hospital B, 75% achieve full recovery within six months.
items.question: Of all stroke patients in the region who achieved full recovery, approximately what percentage were treated at Hospital A?

options.text: About 44%
About 40%
About 36%
About 50%

items.explanation_ko: 환자 100명 기준으로 A병원 40명 중 90%인 36명, B병원 60명 중 75%인 45명이 완전 회복한다. 회복자 81명 중 A병원 환자는 36명이므로 36 / 81 ≈ 44%이다. 오답: B(40%)는 A병원의 전체 환자 점유율로, 회복률 차이를 무시했다. C(36%)는 A병원 회복자 수 36을 비율로 착각한 값이다. D(50%)는 근거 없는 값이다.

items.stimulus: A bacterial culture in a clinical laboratory doubles in size every 30 minutes under optimal growth conditions. The culture starts with 1,000 bacteria at 9:00 AM. Assume growth continues at this rate.
items.question: At what time will the bacterial population reach 64,000?
items.explanation_ko: 64,000 / 1,000 = 64 = 2⁶이므로 6번 배가해야 한다. 30분마다 한 번씩이므로 6 × 30분 = 3시간이 걸리고, 오전 9시에서 3시간 뒤인 낮 12시이다. 오답: B(11:30)는 5번 배가로 32,000이다. C(11:00)는 4번 배가로 16,000이다. D(12:30)는 7번 배가로 128,000이다.

items.stimulus: A patient requires intravenous administration of a medication. The prescription specifies 250 mg total dose to be infused steadily over 4 hours. The medication is supplied as a solution at 5 mg/mL concentration.
items.question: What is the required infusion rate in millilitres per hour?

options.text: 12.5 mL/hr
10.0 mL/hr
15.0 mL/hr
20.0 mL/hr

items.explanation_ko: 필요한 총 용액은 250 mg / 5 mg/mL = 50 mL이고, 이를 4시간에 나누어 주입하므로 50 / 4 = 12.5 mL/h이다. 오답: B(10.0)는 5시간으로 나눈 값이다. C(15.0)와 D(20.0)는 주입 시간을 짧게 잡은 값이다.

items.stimulus:
A five-year cardiovascular outcomes trial compared a new statin to placebo. The rate of major cardiovascular events (heart attack, stroke, or cardiovascular death) was 8% in the placebo group and 5% in the treatment group over the five-year period. The drug was well-tolerated with no serious safety signals.

The Number Needed to Treat (NNT) is calculated as 1 divided by the absolute risk reduction (the difference between the two event rates, expressed as a proportion).
items.question: Approximately how many patients need to be treated for five years to prevent one cardiovascular event (Number Needed to Treat)?

options.text: About 16
About 25
About 33
About 60

items.explanation_ko: 절대위험감소는 8% − 5% = 3%p(0.03)이고 NNT = 1 / 0.03 ≈ 33이다. 즉 5년간 약 33명을 치료하면 사건 1건을 예방한다. 오답: A(16)는 차이를 6%로 잘못 잡은 값이다. B(25)와 D(60)는 근거 없는 값이다. 상대위험감소 37.5%를 쓰면 약 3이 나오는데, 이는 NNT 정의와 맞지 않는다.

items.stimulus:
A specialty medical clinic is evaluating its monthly financial sustainability. Costs are structured as follows:

- Fixed costs (rent, salaried staff, equipment leases, utilities): $400,000 per month
- Variable costs (per-patient consumables, hourly staff time, lab fees): $200 per patient

The clinic charges $350 per patient consultation. Patient billing is the clinic's only revenue source; insurance reimbursements at this rate cover all consultations regardless of complexity.
items.question: What is the minimum number of patients per month required for the clinic to break even (revenue equals total costs)?

options.text: About 1,150
About 2,667
About 1,800
About 3,200

items.explanation_ko: 손익분기에서는 350x = 400,000 + 200x이므로 150x = 400,000, x ≈ 2,667명이다. 환자 1명당 공헌이익 $150으로 고정비 $400,000을 회수하는 구조이다. 오답: A(약 1,150)는 변동비를 무시하고 400,000 / 350으로 나눈 값이다. C(약 1,800)와 D(약 3,200)는 근거 없는 값이다.

items.stimulus: A clinic with 5 medical assistants can process 200 patient files in a 10-hour day. The work rate per assistant-hour is constant. The clinic plans to hire additional assistants for a similar 10-hour day.
items.question: If the clinic increases to 8 assistants, approximately how many patient files can they process in the same 10-hour day?
items.explanation_ko: 처리량은 인원에 비례하므로 200 × 8/5 = 320건이다. 오답: A(240)는 일부만 비례시킨 값, B(280)는 늘어난 3명분을 20건씩으로 잘못 계산한 값, C(400)는 인원을 두 배로 본 값이다.

items.stimulus: A clinic's monthly patient count increased from 240 to 312 over six months.
items.question: What is the percentage increase?
items.explanation_ko: 증가분은 312 − 240 = 72이고, 72 ÷ 240 = 0.30이므로 30% 증가이다. 오답: 25%는 72를 312 근처 값으로 나눈 경우(72 ÷ 312 ≈ 23%)와 혼동한 값이고, 20%와 35%는 계산 오류이다.

items.stimulus:
Patient counts at a clinic by age group:
- 0-17: 120
- 18-34: 180
- 35-54: 240
- 55-74: 200
- 75+: 80
items.question: What proportion of patients are aged 35 or older?

options.text: About 50%
About 55%
About 70%
About 63%

items.stimulus:
A diagnostic test for a rare disease has the following operating characteristics:
- Sensitivity: 99% (correctly identifies 99% of patients with the disease)
- Specificity: 95% (correctly identifies 95% of healthy people as negative)
- Disease prevalence in population: 0.1% (1 in 1,000 people has the disease)
items.question: If a randomly selected person tests positive, what is the approximate probability they actually have the disease?

options.text: About 50%
About 2%
About 95%
About 99%

items.explanation_ko: 100,000명 중 환자 100명, 비환자 99,900명이다. 진양성은 100 × 0.99 = 99명, 위양성은 99,900 × 0.05 = 4,995명이므로 양성 중 환자 비율은 99 ÷ 5,094 ≈ 1.9%, 약 2%이다. 오답: D(99%)는 민감도, C(95%)는 특이도를 그대로 답으로 쓴 것이고, A(50%)는 근거 없는 값이다.

items.stimulus: A clinical trial of a blood pressure medication reports: 'The average reduction in systolic blood pressure with the new drug was 12 mmHg, with a 95% confidence interval of 8 to 16 mmHg.'
items.question: Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of this 95% confidence interval?

options.text: If the study were repeated many times, about 95% of intervals constructed this way would contain the true average reduction; this study's interval is 8 to 16 mmHg.
95% of patients in the trial had a reduction in systolic blood pressure of between 8 and 16 mmHg.
There is a 95% chance that any individual patient who takes the drug will have a reduction of at least 8 mmHg.
There is a 95% probability that the average reduction observed in this trial's sample lies between 8 and 16 mmHg.

items.explanation_ko: 95% 신뢰구간은 같은 방식으로 표본을 반복 추출해 구간을 만들면 그 중 약 95%가 모집단의 참 평균을 포함한다는 뜻이며, 이 연구에서 그 구간이 8–16 mmHg이다. 오답: B는 개별 환자 분포로 오해한 것, C는 신뢰구간을 개별 환자의 확률로 해석한 것, D는 표본 평균(12)은 이미 알려진 값인데 표본 평균을 확률적으로 표현한 오류이다.

items.stimulus: A nurse adds 250 mL of distilled water to 500 mL of 0.9% saline solution. The two are thoroughly mixed.
items.question: What is the new concentration of the diluted solution?
items.explanation_ko: 용질 양은 500 × 0.9% = 4.5 g으로 변하지 않고, 부피는 750 mL가 된다. 4.5 ÷ 750 = 0.60%이다. 오답: B(0.45%)는 부피가 두 배가 된 것으로 본 값, C(0.30%)는 세 배로 본 값, D(0.75%)는 계산 오류이다.

items.stimulus:
A linear graph shows the relationship between hours of physical therapy received and patient improvement scores. Two reference points on the line are:
- (5 hours, 200 points)
- (15 hours, 800 points)
items.question: What is the slope of the line (improvement score per additional hour of therapy)?

options.text: 40 points/hour
50 points/hour
60 points/hour
100 points/hour

items.explanation_ko: 기울기 = (800 − 200) ÷ (15 − 5) = 600 ÷ 10 = 60점/시간이다. 오답: A(40)는 200 ÷ 5, D(100)는 x 값 차이를 6으로 잘못 계산한 값 등 계산 오류이며, B(50)는 800 ÷ 15를 반올림한 것과 혼동한 값이다.

items.stimulus: A particular surgical procedure has a 12% complication rate (independent of patient characteristics in this idealised scenario). Two patients who do not know each other are randomly selected from the same procedure on the same day, in different operating rooms with different surgical teams. The two surgeries' complication outcomes can be considered statistically independent.
items.question: What is the probability that BOTH patients will experience a complication?
items.explanation_ko: 두 사건이 독립이므로 0.12 × 0.12 = 0.0144, 즉 1.44%이다. 오답: B(12%)는 한 명의 확률, C(24%)는 두 확률을 더한 값, D(44%)는 숫자를 잘못 조합한 값이다.

items.stimulus: A medication decreases its plasma concentration by 8% each hour through metabolism. The patient's initial plasma concentration is 100 mg/L. The decline is independent and compound (each hour, 8% of the current concentration is removed, not 8% of the original).
items.question: Approximately what is the concentration after 5 hours?

options.text: About 60 mg/L
About 66 mg/L
About 72 mg/L
About 78 mg/L

items.explanation_ko: 매시간 현재 농도의 92%가 남으므로 100 × 0.92^5 ≈ 65.9 mg/L, 약 66 mg/L이다. 오답: A(60)는 8%씩 5번을 단순히 뺀 값(40% 감소)이고, C(72)는 4시간 후 값(71.6), D(78)은 3시간 후 값(77.9)이다.

items.stimulus: A clinic has determined that 3 doctors working 8 hours each can see exactly 24 patients in a day. The work rate per doctor-hour is constant. The clinic is considering a different staffing plan: 5 doctors working 6 hours each.
items.question: Approximately how many patients can the clinic see in a day under the new staffing plan?

options.text: 30 patients
24 patients
20 patients
36 patients

items.explanation_ko: 3명 × 8시간 = 24 의사-시간에 24명이므로 의사-시간당 1명이다. 새 계획은 5 × 6 = 30 의사-시간이므로 30명이다. 오답: B(24)는 변화가 없다고 본 값, C(20)와 D(36)는 인원과 시간 중 하나만 반영한 계산 오류이다.

items.stimulus:
Two cholesterol medications were tracked over six months:

| Month | Drug A (mg/dL reduction) | Drug B (mg/dL reduction) |
|-------|-------------------------|-------------------------|
| 1     | 15                       | 10                       |
| 2     | 25                       | 18                       |
| 3     | 35                       | 28                       |
| 4     | 42                       | 38                       |
| 5     | 47                       | 47                       |
| 6     | 50                       | 55                       |
items.question: Which statement is most accurately supported by the data?

options.text: Drug A produced a larger reduction than Drug B in every month.
Drug A produced the larger reduction in months 1 to 4, the two were equal in month 5, and Drug B produced the larger reduction in month 6.
Drug B's reduction increased by a smaller amount than Drug A's from each month to the next.
The difference between the two drugs' reductions was greatest in month 6.

items.explanation_ko: 1–4개월에는 A의 감소폭이 B보다 크고(15>10, 25>18, 35>28, 42>38), 5개월에 47로 같으며, 6개월에는 B(55)가 A(50)보다 크다. 오답: A는 6개월에 B가 더 크므로 틀리고, C는 B의 월별 증가폭(8, 10, 10, 9, 8)이 4–6개월 A의 증가폭(7, 5, 3)보다 크므로 틀리며, D는 두 약의 차이가 2·3개월(7)에 가장 크고 6개월(5)은 아니므로 틀리다.

items.stimulus: A medication is supplied at a concentration of 5 g/L (5 grams per litre). The doctor needs to express this concentration in milligrams per millilitre (mg/mL) for the patient's chart.
items.question: What is the concentration in mg/mL?

options.text: 0.5 mg/mL
500 mg/mL
50 mg/mL
5 mg/mL

items.explanation_ko: 5 g/L = 5,000 mg ÷ 1,000 mL = 5 mg/mL이다. g→mg(×1,000)과 L→mL(×1,000)이 서로 상쇄된다. 오답: A·B·C는 두 환산 중 하나만 적용하거나 자릿수를 잘못 옮긴 값이다.

items.stimulus: A nurse recorded patient wait times (in minutes) at an urgent care clinic over a single shift: 5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 18, 22, 95.
items.question: What does the difference between the mean and median wait times reveal about the data?

options.text: The mean (about 23.1 min) is well above the median (13.5 min) because one extreme wait pulls the mean up, so the median better reflects a typical wait.
The mean and median are close to each other, so the wait times are roughly symmetrically distributed.
The median is greater than the mean, which shows the wait times are skewed towards shorter waits.
The mean is greater than the median because most patients waited longer than 23 minutes.

items.explanation_ko: 평균은 185 ÷ 8 ≈ 23.1분, 중앙값은 (12 + 15) ÷ 2 = 13.5분이다. 95분이라는 극단값 하나가 평균을 끌어올려 오른쪽으로 치우친 분포이며, 전형적인 대기 시간은 중앙값이 더 잘 나타낸다. 오답: B는 두 값이 10분 가까이 차이 나므로 틀리고, C는 중앙값이 평균보다 작으므로 틀리며, D는 8명 중 7명이 22분 이하로 기다렸으므로 틀리다.

items.stimulus:
An adult dose of a particular medication is 500 mg. For pediatric patients, the dose is calculated using Clark's rule, which assumes a standard adult body weight of 70 kg:

Pediatric dose = (Child's weight in kg / 70 kg) × Adult dose
items.question: What is the appropriate dose for a 28 kg child?

options.text: 150 mg
200 mg
250 mg
300 mg

items.stimulus: A medical school admissions committee has 5 applicants in their final pool: 3 are graduate-entry applicants (with a prior degree) and 2 are school-leavers. Two applicants are randomly selected (without replacement) for in-depth review.
items.question: What is the probability that BOTH selected applicants are graduate-entry applicants?
items.explanation_ko: 첫 번째가 해당 지원자일 확률 3/5, 두 번째도 해당 지원자일 확률 2/4이므로 3/5 × 2/4 = 6/20 = 30%이다. 조합으로도 C(3,2) ÷ C(5,2) = 3 ÷ 10 = 30%이다. 오답: D(60%)는 첫 번째 선택 확률만 계산한 값, C(36%)는 복원 추출로 본 값(0.6²), A(20%)는 계산 오류이다.

items.stimulus:
Two cancer treatment options have been studied:
- Treatment A: Increases survival by 20 percentage points, costs $5,000 per patient
- Treatment B: Increases survival by 30 percentage points, costs $9,000 per patient

A hospital must choose between the treatments based on cost-effectiveness (cost per survival benefit unit).
items.question: Which treatment is more cost-effective per percentage point of survival benefit, and by approximately how much?

options.text: Treatment B is more cost-effective by about $50/percentage point.
Treatment A is more cost-effective by about $300/percentage point.
Treatment A is more cost-effective by about $50/percentage point.
The two treatments are equally cost-effective.

items.explanation_ko: A는 $5,000 ÷ 20 = $250/%p, B는 $9,000 ÷ 30 = $300/%p이므로 A가 %p당 약 $50 저렴해 더 비용 효과적이다. 오답: A는 방향이 반대이고, B($300)는 B의 단가를 차이로 착각한 값이며, D는 두 단가가 다르므로 틀리다.

items.stimulus:
A metropolitan area has 1,500,000 residents. According to public health surveys:
- 18% of residents are aged 65 or older
- Of those aged 65 or older, 65% have at least one chronic condition (diabetes, heart disease, hypertension, etc.)
items.question: Approximately how many residents in this metropolitan area are aged 65 or older AND have at least one chronic condition?

options.text: About 195,000
About 270,000
About 175,500
About 415,500

items.stimulus: A study plotted weekly exercise hours (x-axis) against blood cholesterol levels (y-axis) for 100 adults. The resulting scatter plot showed a downward-sloping pattern: people with more weekly exercise hours generally had lower cholesterol levels, though there was substantial variation around the trend (the points formed a cloud rather than a tight line).
items.question: Which of the following statements is most accurately supported by the data described?

options.text: Increasing weekly exercise would lower the cholesterol level of any individual in the study.
Exercise hours and cholesterol levels are negatively associated in this group, but the data do not show that exercise causes lower cholesterol.
Because the points form a cloud rather than a line, there is no relationship between exercise hours and cholesterol levels.
People with lower cholesterol levels in this group generally exercised fewer hours per week.

items.explanation_ko: 점들이 오른쪽 아래로 흩어져 있으므로 운동 시간과 콜레스테롤 사이에는 음의 연관성이 있지만, 관찰 자료이므로 운동이 콜레스테롤을 낮춘다는 인과는 확정할 수 없다. 오답: A는 상관을 개인 수준의 인과로 확대했고, C는 흩어져 있어도 경향은 존재하므로 틀리며, D는 음의 관계와 반대 방향이다.

items.stimulus:
A clinical trial of a cardiovascular drug reports the following five-year heart attack rates:
- Placebo group: 8%
- Treatment group: 6%

Both Absolute Risk Reduction (ARR) and Relative Risk Reduction (RRR) can be calculated from these data.

Relative Risk Reduction is the absolute risk reduction expressed as a proportion of the placebo group's risk.
items.question: What is the Relative Risk Reduction (RRR) of the treatment compared to placebo?

options.text: 2 percentage points

items.explanation_ko: 절대위험감소는 8% − 6% = 2%p이고, 상대위험감소는 2 ÷ 8 = 25%이다. 오답: A(2%p)는 절대위험감소, B(8%)는 위약군 위험률, D(33%)는 2를 6으로 나눈 값이다.

items.stimulus:
A community health screening event has the following cost structure:
- Fixed cost: $300 (venue, equipment setup)
- Variable cost: $50 per patient screened

The total budget for the event is $1,500.
items.question: What is the maximum number of patients that can be screened within the budget?

options.text: 20 patients
22 patients
24 patients
26 patients

items.stimulus:
Hospital admissions for influenza-related illness in four selected months of one year:

| Month | Admissions |
|-------|------------|
| Jan   | 80         |
| Apr   | 30         |
| Jul   | 15         |
| Oct   | 40         |
items.question: Which statement is best supported by the data?

options.text: Admissions stayed roughly constant across the months shown.
Of the months shown, admissions were highest in January and lowest in July.
Admissions rose from April to October, so October is the peak month of the year.
Admissions fell by the same amount between each pair of consecutive months shown.

items.explanation_ko: 제시된 네 달 중 입원은 1월(80)이 가장 많고 7월(15)이 가장 적다. 오답: A는 15–80으로 크게 변하므로 틀리고, C는 10월(40)이 1월(80)보다 적어 연중 최고일 수 없으며, D는 감소폭이 50, 15로 다르고 10월에는 오히려 증가하므로 틀리다.

items.stimulus:
A cylindrical IV fluid bag has internal dimensions: radius 4 cm, height 20 cm. (Use π ≈ 3.14)

Volume of cylinder formula: V = π × r² × h
items.question: What is the approximate volume of fluid the bag can hold (in cm³ or mL, since 1 cm³ = 1 mL)?

options.text: About 1,000 mL
About 500 mL
About 250 mL
About 1,500 mL

items.explanation_ko: V = 3.14 × 4² × 20 = 3.14 × 320 = 1,004.8 cm³, 약 1,000 mL이다. 오답: B(500)는 반지름을 제곱하지 않거나 반으로 계산한 값, C(250)는 지름과 반지름 혼동, D(1,500)는 계산 오류이다.

items.stimulus:
A diagnostic test for a particular cancer has the following operating characteristics:

- Sensitivity: 85% (correctly identifies 85% of patients who have the disease)
- Specificity: 92% (correctly identifies 92% of patients who do NOT have the disease)
- Disease prevalence in screened population: 4%
items.question: What is the Positive Predictive Value (PPV) — the probability that a person who tests positive actually has the disease?

options.text: About 17%
About 85%
About 65%
About 31%

items.explanation_ko: 10,000명 중 환자 400명, 비환자 9,600명이다. 진양성 400 × 0.85 = 340명, 위양성 9,600 × 0.08 = 768명이므로 PPV = 340 ÷ 1,108 ≈ 30.7%, 약 31%이다. 오답: B(85%)는 민감도를 그대로 쓴 것, C(65%)와 A(17%)는 위양성이나 유병률을 잘못 반영한 값이다.

items.stimulus: Three medical specialty teams handle the on-call hospital workload. Specialty A takes 50% of all incoming calls, Specialty B takes 30%, and Specialty C takes 20%. The proportion of calls that are cardiac emergencies varies by specialty: 10% of A's calls, 25% of B's calls, and 5% of C's calls.
items.question: If a randomly selected call is a cardiac emergency, what is the probability it was handled by Specialty B?

options.text: About 25%
About 56%
About 47%
About 75%

items.explanation_ko: 응급 콜 전체 비율은 0.50 × 0.10 + 0.30 × 0.25 + 0.20 × 0.05 = 0.05 + 0.075 + 0.01 = 0.135이다. 그 중 Specialty B 몫은 0.075 ÷ 0.135 ≈ 55.6%, 약 56%이다. 오답: A(25%)는 B의 응급 비율 P(응급|B)를 그대로 쓴 것, D(75%)와 C(47%)는 분자·분모를 잘못 잡은 계산 오류이다.

items.stimulus:
Two anti-anxiety treatment trials report identical mean symptom improvements of 8 points (on a 50-point scale) with identical standard deviations of 4 points—but different sample sizes:

- Study A: n = 50, mean improvement = 8 (SD = 4)
- Study B: n = 500, mean improvement = 8 (SD = 4)

The standard error of the mean is calculated as SE = SD / √n.
items.question: Which statement most accurately compares the two studies?

options.text: Study B's standard error is about 3.16 times smaller than Study A's, so Study B gives a more precise estimate of the mean improvement.
Study B's standard error is 10 times smaller than Study A's, so its confidence interval is 10 times narrower.
Because the standard deviations are identical, the two studies have the same standard error.
Study A gives the more precise estimate, because a smaller sample contains less total variation.

items.explanation_ko: SE = SD ÷ √n이므로 A는 4 ÷ √50 ≈ 0.566, B는 4 ÷ √500 ≈ 0.179로, B의 표준오차가 √10 ≈ 3.16배 작아 평균 추정이 더 정밀하다. 오답: B는 표본이 10배일 때 표준오차가 10배가 아니라 √10배 줄어드므로 틀리고, C는 SD가 같아도 n이 다르면 SE가 다르므로 틀리며, D는 작은 표본이 오히려 덜 정밀하므로 틀리다.

items.stimulus:
A clinical trial requires participants who simultaneously meet ALL of these inclusion criteria:
- Age 30-65 years
- BMI 18-30
- No history of cardiovascular disease
- Non-smoker for at least 2 years

From 1,000 randomly screened candidates:
- 80% meet the age criterion
- 70% meet the BMI criterion
- 85% meet the cardiovascular criterion
- 60% meet the smoking criterion

All four criteria are statistically independent in this candidate pool.
items.question: Approximately how many of the 1,000 candidates would qualify for the trial (meet all four criteria)?

options.text: About 100
About 400
About 286
About 600

items.explanation_ko: 독립이므로 0.80 × 0.70 × 0.85 × 0.60 = 0.2856, 1,000명 중 약 286명이다. 오답: D(600)와 B(400)는 가장 엄격한 기준이나 일부 기준만 반영한 값, A(100)는 계산 오류이다.

items.stimulus: A medical conference attended 280 people in total, divided into two registration categories: physicians (paying $200 each) and medical students (paying $80 each). Total registration revenue was $44,000.
items.question: How many physicians attended the conference?

items.stimulus:
Five-year survival rates from a clinical trial of two cancer treatments:

| Year | Treatment A | Treatment B |
|------|-------------|-------------|
| 1    | 90%         | 95%         |
| 2    | 75%         | 85%         |
| 3    | 60%         | 70%         |
| 4    | 50%         | 55%         |
| 5    | 45%         | 45%         |
items.question: Which statement is most accurately supported by these data?

options.text: Treatment B's survival rate was at least as high as Treatment A's in every year, but the advantage had disappeared by year 5.
Treatment A had higher survival than Treatment B in the early years of the trial.
Treatment B had a higher five-year survival rate than Treatment A.
The difference in survival between the treatments was greatest in year 1.

items.explanation_ko: 모든 연도에서 B의 생존율이 A 이상이고(95>90, 85>75, 70>60, 55>50), 5년째에는 45%로 같아 차이가 사라진다. 오답: B는 초기 생존율이 B 쪽이 더 높으므로 틀리고, C는 5년 생존율이 같으므로 틀리며, D는 차이가 2·3년째(10%p)에 가장 크고 1년째(5%p)는 아니므로 틀리다.

items.stimulus: An intravenous (IV) infusion of 1,000 mL of saline solution must be administered over 8 hours. The IV administration set delivers 15 drops per millilitre (drop factor = 15 gtt/mL).
items.question: What is the required drip rate, expressed as drops per minute?

options.text: About 21 drops/min
About 25 drops/min
About 31 drops/min
About 42 drops/min

items.explanation_ko: 1,000 mL ÷ 480분 × 15 방울/mL = 15,000 ÷ 480 ≈ 31.25, 약 31방울/분이다. 오답: A(21)는 시간을 12시간으로 본 값, B(25)·D(42)는 시간 환산이나 드롭 팩터를 잘못 적용한 값이다.

items.stimulus:
A five-year cardiovascular outcomes trial of a new drug versus placebo reports its primary result:

'Hazard Ratio (HR) for cardiovascular death in the drug group versus placebo: HR = 0.70 (95% confidence interval: 0.55 to 0.89, p = 0.003).'

A hazard ratio below 1 means the outcome occurred at a lower rate in the drug group; a 95% confidence interval that does not include 1 indicates a statistically significant difference.
items.question: Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of these results?
