options.text: The drug increases the risk of cardiovascular death by 70% compared with placebo, and this increase is statistically significant (p = 0.003).
70% of patients taking the drug avoided cardiovascular death over five years, compared with a lower proportion of patients on placebo.
The drug reduces the risk of cardiovascular death by about 30%, and the confidence interval is consistent with a true reduction of roughly 11% to 45%.
The reduction is not statistically significant, because the confidence interval spans a range wider than the 30% point estimate.

items.explanation_ko: HR 0.70은 위약 대비 위험이 약 30% 낮다는 뜻이며, 95% 신뢰구간 0.55–0.89는 위험 감소가 약 11%(1 − 0.89)에서 45%(1 − 0.55) 사이임을 뜻한다. 구간이 1을 포함하지 않으므로 통계적으로 유의하다. 오답: A는 HR이 1보다 작은데 증가로 해석했고, B는 HR을 생존 비율로 오해했으며, D는 구간이 1을 포함하지 않으므로 유의하지 않다는 판단이 틀리다.

items.stimulus:
Body Surface Area (BSA) is used to calculate doses for certain medications, particularly chemotherapy. The simplified Mosteller formula is:

BSA (m²) = √(Height in cm × Weight in kg / 3600)

A chemotherapy regimen prescribes 60 mg per square metre of BSA per dose.
items.question: What dose is appropriate for a patient who is 170 cm tall and weighs 72 kg?

options.text: About 90 mg
About 100 mg
About 120 mg
About 110 mg

items.stimulus:
Epidemiologists distinguish two key disease frequency measures:
- Incidence: rate of NEW cases occurring in a given period (e.g., per year)
- Prevalence: total cases existing at a given time (new + ongoing)

For stable conditions (steady-state), these are related by approximately:
Prevalence ≈ Incidence × Average disease duration

In a population of 100,000:
- Currently 5,000 people have a particular chronic condition (current prevalence)
- 800 new cases develop each year (annual incidence)
- Recovered or deceased patients leave the prevalent pool
items.question: Based on the relationship Prevalence ≈ Incidence × Duration, what is the estimated average duration of this disease?

options.text: About 4 years
About 6.25 years
About 5 years
About 10 years

items.explanation_ko: 유병 ≈ 발생 × 유병 기간이므로 기간 = 5,000 ÷ 800 = 6.25년이다. 오답: C(5년)는 5,000 ÷ 1,000으로 어림한 값, A(4년)·D(10년)는 계산 오류이다.

items.stimulus: A medication has a plasma half-life of 4 hours, meaning the concentration of the drug in the patient's blood decreases by 50% every 4 hours through metabolism and excretion. A patient receives a single intravenous dose, achieving an initial peak plasma concentration of 200 mg/L.
items.question: What is the plasma concentration 12 hours after the initial peak?

options.text: 25 mg/L
50 mg/L
100 mg/L

items.explanation_ko: 12시간은 반감기 3번이므로 200 → 100 → 50 → 25 mg/L이다. 오답: D(100)는 1번, C(50)는 2번, A(12.5)는 4번 반감한 값이다.

items.stimulus:
A clinical trial is designed to detect a 5 percentage-point reduction in mortality (from 20% in the placebo group to 15% in the treatment group) with 80% statistical power and α = 0.05. Power calculations indicate that 1,200 patients per group are required.

The research team is considering a redesigned trial with the same statistical assumptions (80% power, α = 0.05) but targeting detection of a smaller, 3 percentage-point reduction (from 20% to 17%) instead.

Assume that the number of patients required per group is inversely proportional to the square of the difference in mortality the trial aims to detect.
items.question: Approximately how many patients per group will the redesigned trial require?

options.text: About 3,300
About 1,200
About 720
About 2,000

items.explanation_ko: 필요 인원은 검출하려는 차이의 제곱에 반비례합니다. 차이가 5%p에서 3%p로 줄면 인원은 (5/3)² = 25/9 ≈ 2.78배가 되어 1,200 × 2.78 ≈ 3,333명, 약 3,300명입니다. 오답: B는 차이가 줄어도 인원이 같다고 본 것입니다. C는 반대로 인원이 줄어든다고 계산한 값(1,200 × 0.6)입니다. D는 제곱을 빼고 단순 반비례(1,200 × 5/3)로 계산한 값입니다.

items.stimulus:
A diagnostic test for an aggressive cancer can be tuned to different threshold levels, producing different combinations of sensitivity and specificity:

| Threshold | Sensitivity | Specificity |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| Low       | 95%         | 60%         |
| Medium    | 85%         | 80%         |
| High      | 70%         | 95%         |

The cancer is highly treatable when caught early but rapidly fatal if missed. A cheap follow-up confirmatory test exists that quickly resolves false positives.
items.question: Which threshold setting is most appropriate for this clinical scenario?

options.text: Low threshold, because missing a cancer is very costly while false positives can be cheaply resolved by follow-up testing.
Medium threshold, because it gives the best balance between sensitivity and specificity.
High threshold, because it produces the fewest false positives and so the least unnecessary anxiety.
High threshold, because a positive result at this setting is the most likely to be a true positive.

items.explanation_ko: 놓치면 치명적이고 위양성은 값싼 확인 검사로 해결되므로 민감도가 가장 높은(95%) 낮은 기준이 적절하다. 오답: B는 민감도·특이도 합이 높은 기준(165)은 중간과 높은 기준 두 개이며, 이 상황에서 균형이 목표가 아니므로 틀리고, C·D는 위양성을 줄이는 대신 환자의 30%를 놓치게 되므로 이 상황에 맞지 않는다.

items.stimulus:
A genetic disorder follows autosomal recessive inheritance, meaning a person develops the disease only if they inherit two copies of the disease allele (one from each parent). Carriers (one disease allele + one normal allele) do not show symptoms but can pass the disease allele to children.

A couple is planning a child. Both parents have been tested and confirmed as carriers (genotype Aa, where A is the normal allele and a is the disease allele).
items.question: What is the probability that their child will be a carrier (Aa or aA, meaning one disease allele but no disease)?
items.explanation_ko: Aa × Aa에서 AA 1/4, Aa 1/2, aa 1/4이므로 보인자일 확률은 50%이다. 오답: A(25%)는 이환(aa) 확률, D(75%)는 증상이 없을 확률, C(33%)는 증상 없는 자녀 중 비보인자 비율을 잘못 쓴 값이다.

items.stimulus: A genomics research team tests 100 different gene variants for association with a rare disease. Each test uses a significance threshold of α = 0.05 (i.e., 5% chance of incorrectly declaring 'significant' when no real association exists, called a Type I error).
items.question: If all 100 null hypotheses are actually true (no real associations exist), approximately how many tests would you expect to falsely reach 'significance' (p < 0.05) by chance alone?

options.text: Approximately 1
Approximately 5
Approximately 25
Approximately 95

items.explanation_ko: 귀무가설이 모두 참이면 각 검정이 우연히 유의할 확률은 5%이므로 100 × 0.05 = 5개가 기대된다. 오답: A(1개)는 계산 오류, C(25개)는 근거 없는 값, D(95개)는 유의하지 않은 검정 수이다.

items.stimulus:
A laboratory pharmacist needs to prepare 500 mL of a 12% antiseptic solution for a clinical procedure. Available materials are:
- A 20% concentrated antiseptic stock solution
- Sterile distilled water (0% antiseptic content)

The two materials must be mixed to produce the desired concentration and final volume.
items.question: How much of each material should be mixed to produce 500 mL of 12% antiseptic solution?

options.text: 200 mL concentrate + 300 mL water
300 mL concentrate + 200 mL water
240 mL concentrate + 260 mL water
350 mL concentrate + 150 mL water

items.explanation_ko: 필요한 원액 성분은 500 × 12% = 60 mL이고, 20% 원액에서 60 mL를 얻으려면 60 ÷ 0.20 = 300 mL가 필요하다. 나머지 200 mL는 물이다. 오답: A는 8%, C는 9.6%, D는 14%가 되어 12%가 아니다.

items.stimulus:
A 10-year cohort study compared two groups for development of a chronic disease:

| Group       | n     | New cases | Total person-years |
|-------------|-------|-----------|-------------------|
| Exposed     | 2,000 | 80        | 18,000            |
| Unexposed   | 5,000 | 100       | 47,000            |

Note: Person-years account for both the number of people and the duration each was followed (some participants left the study early due to loss to follow-up, death from other causes, etc.).
items.question: What is the Incidence Rate Ratio (IRR) of the exposed compared to the unexposed group?

options.text: About 1.6
About 1.9
About 2.1
About 4.0

items.explanation_ko: 노출군 발생률은 80 ÷ 18,000 ≈ 4.44/1,000인년, 비노출군은 100 ÷ 47,000 ≈ 2.13/1,000인년이므로 IRR ≈ 4.44 ÷ 2.13 ≈ 2.09, 약 2.1이다. 오답: D(4.0)는 사례 수 비율 등을 잘못 쓴 값, B(1.9)와 A(1.6)는 인원이나 인년을 섞어 쓴 계산 오류이며, 단순 비율 80/2,000 ÷ 100/5,000 = 2.0은 인년 차이를 반영하지 않은 값이다.

items.stimulus: A medical school admissions committee must select 4 students for prestigious research scholarships from 10 finalists. The committee makes its selection based solely on merit (the order of selection does not matter—4 students are chosen as a group, and only the final group composition matters).
items.question: How many different groups of 4 students can be selected from 10 finalists?

items.stimulus: A new pain management drug has been tested in a randomised trial. Among 1,000 patients receiving the drug, 12% developed a clinically significant gastrointestinal side effect (severe nausea, ulcers, or bleeding requiring intervention). Among 1,000 patients receiving placebo, only 4% developed the same side effect. The drug's pain relief efficacy was demonstrated in a separate analysis. The Number Needed to Harm (NNH) is calculated as 1 divided by the absolute increase in the risk of the side effect.
items.question: What is the Number Needed to Harm (NNH) for this side effect?

options.text: About 8
About 33
About 25
About 13

items.explanation_ko: 절대위험증가는 12% − 4% = 8%p이고, NNH = 1 ÷ 0.08 = 12.5, 약 13명이다. 오답: A(8)는 8%p를 그대로 쓴 값, C(25)는 1 ÷ 0.04, B(33)는 1 ÷ 0.03에 해당하는 값이다.

items.stimulus:
A hospital ward has limited daily resources for two patient types:
- Total nursing capacity: 24 hours per day
- Total bed availability: 10 beds

Patient mix and economics:
- Patient Type A: requires 2 hours of nursing per day, generates $300 in revenue
- Patient Type B: requires 3 hours of nursing per day, generates $500 in revenue

Patient counts must be non-negative integers.
items.question: What is the maximum daily revenue achievable from optimal patient mix?
items.explanation_ko: 제약은 2A + 3B ≤ 24, A + B ≤ 10이다. 간호 시간당 수익은 B($166.7)가 A($150)보다 높으므로 시간을 B에 모두 쓰면 B = 8, 수익 $4,000이며 침대는 2개 남는다. 다른 조합은 A = 3, B = 6이 $3,900, A = 6, B = 4가 $3,800, A = 10이 $3,000으로 모두 작다. 오답: A·B·D는 각각 A만 채운 경우, 두 제약을 모두 꽉 채운 경우, 실행 불가능한 값이다.

meta.formatNotes: UCAT ANZ는 2025년 시험부터 Abstract Reasoning(추상추론)이 폐지되어 현재 4개 하위시험으로 구성됩니다. 언어추론(VR) 44문항/22분(지문 11개 × 각 4문항, True/False/Can't Tell 3지선다와 4지선다 혼합, 문항당 약 30초), 의사결정(DM) 35문항/37분(문항당 약 63초; 유형은 논리 퍼즐, 삼단논법, 정보 해석, 가정 인식(가장 강한 논거), 벤 다이어그램, 확률적 추론. 삼단논법·정보 해석은 다섯 진술마다 Yes/No를 끌어다 놓는 방식이며 0~2점 부분점수, 나머지는 4지선다), 수리추론(QR) 36문항/26분(지시문 2분, 화면 계산기 사용 가능, 표·그래프 자료 세트당 여러 문항, 문항당 약 43초), 상황판단(SJT) 69문항/26분(시나리오당 최대 6문항, 적절성 4단계·중요도 4단계 척도, 정답에 가까우면 부분점수; 문항당 약 23초). VR·DM·SJT 지시문은 각 1분 30초. 인지 영역(VR+DM+QR)은 각 300~900점, 합산 900~2700점이며 SJT는 인지 영역 합산과 별도로 300~900점 척도점수로 보고됩니다(밴드 1~4는 영국 UCAT 방식). 가장 적절/가장 부적절 고르기(3개 보기) 유형은 대비 자료에 소개되나 현재 ANZ 시험에서의 출제 여부는 공식적으로 확인하지 못해 이 은행에는 넣지 않았습니다. 이 은행의 DM 삼단논법·정보 해석 문항은 사이트 단일정답 구조에 맞춰 '따라 나오는 결론 조합'을 고르는 4지선다로 바꾸었고, 원래 형식의 진술별 정답은 yesNoKey 필드에 함께 담았습니다. timeSec은 공식 시간 배분(문항당 평균)을 기준으로 난이도에 따라 조정한 권장 시간입니다. 모든 지문·자료·시나리오는 자체 창작이며 공식·기출·업체 문항을 사용하지 않았습니다. 출처: https://ucat.edu.au/ucat-anz/test-format , https://www.medentry.edu.au/blog/ucat-2025-frequently-asked-questions , https://www.medentry.edu.au/resources/ucat-guide/decision-making , https://www.medentry.edu.au/resources/ucat-guide/situational-judgement (열람일 2026-10-26)

items.stimulus:
Cities are frequently warmer than the countryside around them, a pattern known as the urban heat island effect. The difference is usually most pronounced at night. During the day, asphalt, concrete and brick absorb solar energy; after sunset they release it slowly, so that the air above a dense city centre may remain several degrees warmer than surrounding farmland until the early morning. Waste heat from vehicles, air-conditioning units and industry adds to the effect, while the scarcity of vegetation removes one of nature's most effective cooling mechanisms: the evaporation of water from leaves.

Because of this, many municipal governments have adopted targets for increasing tree canopy cover. Trees cool streets in two ways. Their shade prevents sunlight from reaching surfaces that would otherwise store heat, and transpiration draws heat from the surrounding air. Measurements taken on summer afternoons have shown that pavement beneath a mature canopy can be substantially cooler than nearby pavement in full sun, although the reduction in air temperature is considerably smaller than the reduction in surface temperature.

Planting programmes are not without difficulties. Young trees need regular watering for their first few years, and in drought-prone regions this demand may compete with other uses of water. Roots can damage footpaths and underground pipes if species are poorly chosen. Moreover, canopy benefits accrue slowly: a sapling planted today may take two decades to provide meaningful shade. Some planners therefore argue that canopy targets should be pursued alongside faster measures, such as reflective roofing materials, which can lower roof temperatures within a single season.

Critics also point out that canopy is unevenly distributed. In several cities that have been studied, wealthier suburbs have markedly more tree cover than lower-income neighbourhoods, meaning that the residents least able to afford air-conditioning often experience the greatest heat exposure.
items.question:
Based on the passage, is the following statement true, false, or can't you tell?

The urban heat island effect is typically greatest during daylight hours.

options.text: True
False
Can't Tell

items.explanation_ko: 1) 진술의 핵심어는 '낮 시간에 가장 크다'입니다. 2) 지문 1문단 둘째 문장에 'The difference is usually most pronounced at night'라고 나옵니다. 3) 지문은 차이가 보통 '밤에' 가장 뚜렷하다고 하므로 진술과 정면으로 어긋납니다. 따라서 False입니다.

items.question: Which of the following statements is best supported by the passage?

Air-conditioning units help to reduce the urban heat island effect.

items.stimulus:
Before the nineteenth century, most towns kept their own local time, setting their clocks so that noon fell when the sun stood highest in the sky. Because the sun's apparent position shifts as one travels east or west, two towns only a short distance apart could disagree by several minutes. For communities whose pace of life was set by walking and horse-drawn carriages, such discrepancies hardly mattered.

The spread of railways changed this. A timetable that listed departures in the local time of every station along a route was confusing for passengers and dangerous for operators, since two trains sharing a single track might be working from clocks that did not agree. Railway companies responded by adopting a single reference time for their entire network, often the time kept at the company's headquarters or at a major observatory. The telegraph made this practicable, allowing time signals to be transmitted almost instantly over long distances.

For a period, many towns operated with two times at once: "railway time" displayed at the station and local solar time used for everyday civic affairs. Some public clocks were even built with two minute hands. Gradually, however, the convenience of a shared standard won out, and local solar time was abandoned in most places.

Extending the idea internationally required agreement on a prime meridian from which time zones could be measured. A conference held in the 1880s recommended a meridian passing through Greenwich, England, although adoption by individual countries proceeded unevenly over the following decades. Even today, zone boundaries often follow political borders rather than strict lines of longitude, and a few countries use offsets of half an hour or even forty-five minutes from their neighbours.
items.question:

items.stimulus:
Before the nineteenth century, most towns kept their own local time, setting their clocks so that noon fell when the sun stood highest in the sky. Because the sun's apparent position shifts as one travels east or west, two towns only a short distance apart could disagree by several minutes. For communities whose pace of life was set by walking and horse-drawn carriages, such discrepancies hardly mattered.

The spread of railways changed this. A timetable that listed departures in the local time of every station along a route was confusing for passengers and dangerous for operators, since two trains sharing a single track might be working from clocks that did not agree. Railway companies responded by adopting a single reference time for their entire network, often the time kept at the company's headquarters or at a major observatory. The telegraph made this practicable, allowing time signals to be transmitted almost instantly over long distances.

For a period, many towns operated with two times at once: "railway time" displayed at the station and local solar time used for everyday civic affairs. Some public clocks were even built with two minute hands. Gradually, however, the convenience of a shared standard won out, and local solar time was abandoned in most places.

Extending the idea internationally required agreement on a prime meridian from which time zones could be measured. A conference held in the 1880s recommended a meridian passing through Greenwich, England, although adoption by individual countries proceeded unevenly over the following decades. Even today, zone boundaries often follow political borders rather than strict lines of longitude, and a few countries use offsets of half an hour or even forty-five minutes from their neighbours.

items.stimulus:
Over the past two decades, a growing number of governments have introduced taxes on sugar-sweetened beverages. The reasoning is straightforward: if a product contributes to dental decay, obesity and type 2 diabetes, raising its price should discourage consumption, while the revenue can be directed towards health programmes. Yet the design of such taxes varies considerably, and the details influence their effects.

The simplest approach is a flat levy per litre, applied regardless of how much sugar a drink contains. This is easy to administer but gives manufacturers no reason to change their recipes. A tiered approach, by contrast, charges more for drinks above certain sugar thresholds and nothing for those below. Where tiered levies have been announced well in advance of taking effect, manufacturers have frequently reformulated popular products to fall beneath the thresholds, reducing the sugar supplied to consumers even before any tax has been collected. Supporters regard this as the policy's greatest success; sceptics note that it also means less revenue than originally forecast.

Evaluating health outcomes is more difficult. Purchases of taxed drinks typically fall after a tax is introduced, but consumers may substitute other sugary foods or buy drinks across a nearby border where no tax applies. Changes in obesity rates take years to emerge and are influenced by many other factors, making it hard to attribute any trend to a single measure. Dental outcomes in children, which respond more quickly to changes in sugar intake, have been proposed as an earlier indicator.

Opponents argue that such taxes are regressive, because lower-income households spend a larger share of their budget on food and drink. Advocates reply that these same households also bear a disproportionate share of diet-related disease, and so stand to gain the most if consumption falls.

items.stimulus:
Hanji, the traditional handmade paper of Korea, is produced from the inner bark of the paper mulberry tree. The bark is soaked, boiled with an alkaline solution traditionally derived from plant ash, rinsed and beaten by hand until the fibres separate. The pulp is then suspended in water together with a viscous substance extracted from the roots of a plant in the hibiscus family, which slows drainage and keeps the long fibres evenly dispersed. Sheets are formed by repeatedly dipping a bamboo screen into the vat and swaying it in several directions, so that the fibres settle in crossing layers rather than in a single orientation.

This crossing structure is often credited with giving hanji its notable strength and flexibility. Because the fibres are long and the alkaline processing leaves relatively little acid in the sheet, well-made hanji resists the yellowing and brittleness that afflict many machine-made papers. Some documents written on similar paper centuries ago remain legible today.

Such qualities have attracted interest beyond Korea. Conservators in several countries have experimented with hanji for repairing damaged books and works on paper, where a strong, thin and chemically stable material is required. In some projects it has been used alongside, or in place of, Japanese papers that have long served a similar role in conservation studios.

Despite this recognition, the craft faces pressures at home. Hand production is slow and labour-intensive, and the number of skilled makers has declined over recent decades. Locally grown mulberry bark is more expensive than imported supplies, and some workshops have turned to imported material to remain viable, a choice that purists argue compromises quality. Government and regional initiatives have sought to support the craft through the designation of master artisans, training programmes and the promotion of hanji in contemporary design, from lighting to fashion.

Despite this recognition, the craft faces pressures at home. Hand production is slow and labour-intensive, and the number of skilled makers has declined over recent decades. Locally grown mulberry bark is more expensive than imported supplies, and some workshops have turned to imported material to remain viable, a choice that purists argue compromises quality. Government and regional initiatives have sought to support the craft through the designation of master artisans, training programmes and the promotion of hanji in contemporary design, from lighting to fashion.

items.stimulus:
Hanji, the traditional handmade paper of Korea, is produced from the inner bark of the paper mulberry tree. The bark is soaked, boiled with an alkaline solution traditionally derived from plant ash, rinsed and beaten by hand until the fibres separate. The pulp is then suspended in water together with a viscous substance extracted from the roots of a plant in the hibiscus family, which slows drainage and keeps the long fibres evenly dispersed. Sheets are formed by repeatedly dipping a bamboo screen into the vat and swaying it in several directions, so that the fibres settle in crossing layers rather than in a single orientation.

This crossing structure is often credited with giving hanji its notable strength and flexibility. Because the fibres are long and the alkaline processing leaves relatively little acid in the sheet, well-made hanji resists the yellowing and brittleness that afflict many machine-made papers. Some documents written on similar paper centuries ago remain legible today.

Such qualities have attracted interest beyond Korea. Conservators in several countries have experimented with hanji for repairing damaged books and works on paper, where a strong, thin and chemically stable material is required. In some projects it has been used alongside, or in place of, Japanese papers that have long served a similar role in conservation studios.

Despite this recognition, the craft faces pressures at home. Hand production is slow and labour-intensive, and the number of skilled makers has declined over recent decades. Locally grown mulberry bark is more expensive than imported supplies, and some workshops have turned to imported material to remain viable, a choice that purists argue compromises quality. Government and regional initiatives have sought to support the craft through the designation of master artisans, training programmes and the promotion of hanji in contemporary design, from lighting to fashion.

items.explanation_ko: 1) 1,000명으로 생각하면 쉽습니다. 질환자 2% = 20명, 비질환자 980명. 2) 질환자 중 양성 = 20 × 0.9 = 18명. 3) 비질환자 중 위양성 = 980 × 0.05 = 49명. 4) 양성 총 67명 중 실제 질환자 18명 → 18/67 ≈ 0.269 ≈ 27%. 5) 민감도 90%를 그대로 답(보기 D)으로 고르는 것이 대표적인 '기저율 무시' 오류입니다. 정답 B.

meta.formatNotes: 공식 형식 요약(ACER GAMSAT Information Booklet 기준, 2022년판 및 2025년 이후 시행 방식 보충). Section 1(인문·사회과학 추론)은 객관식 62문항, 100분(읽기 8분 + 풀이 92분)이며, 모든 객관식은 보기 4개(A–D)입니다. 지문은 주로 글(개인적·상상적·설명적·논증적 글)이고 일부 시각 자료와 표가 나오며, 사회·문화, 개인, 대인 관계 주제가 중심입니다. 시와 만화도 출제됩니다. Section 2(작문)는 과제 2개, 65분(읽기 5분 + 작성 60분, 과제당 약 30분)입니다. 각 과제는 하나의 주제를 공유하는 짧은 진술문 4개로 구성되며, 첫 번째 과제(Task A)는 사회·문화적 쟁점, 두 번째 과제(Task B)는 보다 개인적·사회적 쟁점을 다룹니다. 채점은 사고의 질(thinking and content)과 언어 구사(organisation and expression)를 기준으로 독립 채점자 3명이 합니다. 2025년 3월 시험부터 Section 2는 시험장 응시일 약 2주 전 자택 원격 감독 방식으로 따로 치르고, Section 1과 3은 시험장에서 컴퓨터로 응시합니다. Section 3(생물·물리과학 추론)는 객관식 75문항, 150분(읽기 8분 + 풀이 142분)입니다. 과목 비율은 화학 40%, 생물 40%, 물리 20%이며 세 과목이 섞여 출제됩니다. 수준은 생물과 화학은 대학 1학년, 물리는 고교 졸업(A-level/Year 12) 수준입니다. 암기보다 자료 해석과 문제 해결 능력을 측정하며, 대부분 지문·표·그래프를 바탕으로 한 세트형 문항입니다. 이 문제은행의 비율: S1 20문항(지문 7세트), S2 주제 10개(Task A 5개, Task B 5개, 각 4–5개 진술문), S3 30문항(화학 12, 생물 12, 물리 6 = 40/40/20). 문항당 권장 시간은 실제 시험 평균(S1 약 90초, S3 약 115초)을 기준으로 난이도에 맞춰 조정했습니다. 출처: ACER GAMSAT Information Booklet 2022 https://gamsat.acer.org/files/GAMSAT_Info_booklet_2022.pdf ; 2025년 이후 시행 방식(Section 2 원격 분리 응시) 보충: https://www.frasersmedical.com/blogs/what-will-the-september-2024-gamsat-look-like , https://medify.co/resources/gamsat-faq ; 일반 개요: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduate_Medical_School_Admissions_Test (모두 2026-10-26 열람). 모든 지문, 시, 대화, 만화 설명, 자료, 과학 지문과 진술문은 이 문제은행을 위해 새로 작성한 창작물이며, ACER 또는 학원 문항을 복제하거나 변형하지 않았습니다. 일부 과학 표(SN1/SN2 상대 속도, N₂O₄ 평형 상수)는 교육용으로 단순화한 예시 값이며 실측값이 아님을 표 제목에 밝혔습니다.

items.stimulus:
The shop had been closed for eleven weeks when Mara finally turned the key. Dust had settled on the glass counter in a fine, even layer, as if the room had been holding its breath. On the workbench lay a pocket watch, its back removed, its tiny gears arranged on a square of green felt in the order her father had always used: largest on the left, smallest on the right, a sentence waiting for its last word.

She had come intending to list the stock and ring the auctioneer. Instead she sat on his stool, which was too low for her, and picked up the tweezers. Her hands remembered more than she had expected. They did not remember enough. After an hour the balance wheel still refused its seat, and she laughed aloud at the silence that answered her. He would have said nothing, either. He had never explained; he had only waited, a little behind her shoulder, until she found the mistake herself.

She put the tweezers down, took the auctioneer's card from her pocket, and slid it beneath the felt, under the smallest gear.
items.question: The description of the gears as 'a sentence waiting for its last word' most strongly suggests that

options.text: the watch is too damaged to be repaired.
Mara's father left his careful work unfinished.
Mara's father communicated mainly through written notes.
Mara intends to sell the watch before anything else.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 비유의 대상은 '크기 순으로 정리된 톱니바퀴'이고, '마지막 단어를 기다리는 문장'은 완성 직전에 멈춘 상태를 뜻합니다. 2단계: 가게가 11주 동안 닫혀 있었고 작업대 위에 분해된 시계가 그대로 놓여 있다는 맥락에서, 아버지가 늘 쓰던 정돈된 방식으로 하던 작업이 끝나지 않은 채 남았다는 의미가 됩니다. 3단계: A는 파손을 말한 근거가 없고, C는 '문장'이라는 말을 문자 그대로 읽은 오답이며, D는 이 비유와 무관합니다. 정답 B.

items.stimulus:
Every few years a council discovers that its library is 'underused' and resolves to make it 'vibrant'. Out go the reading tables; in come the maker-space, the café and the toddler music sessions. Each of these is worthy. But the case for them usually rests on a quiet sleight of hand: footfall is counted, and silence is not. A person who spends three hours reading in a corner registers as one visit; forty people passing through a pop-up market register as forty. By this arithmetic the most successful library would be a railway station.

I do not object to noise. I object to the assumption that a public good is measured by how many people it can be seen to serve in an afternoon. Some institutions exist precisely to offer what the rest of the city cannot: a place where nothing is being sold and no one needs you to be anything. Remove that, and you have not modernised the library. You have abolished it and kept the name.
items.question: The writer's main objection is to

options.text: the presence of cafés and children's activities in libraries.
councils spending public money on libraries at all.
a way of measuring success that favours visible activity over the kind of use libraries uniquely provide.

items.stimulus:
Every few years a council discovers that its library is 'underused' and resolves to make it 'vibrant'. Out go the reading tables; in come the maker-space, the café and the toddler music sessions. Each of these is worthy. But the case for them usually rests on a quiet sleight of hand: footfall is counted, and silence is not. A person who spends three hours reading in a corner registers as one visit; forty people passing through a pop-up market register as forty. By this arithmetic the most successful library would be a railway station.

I do not object to noise. I object to the assumption that a public good is measured by how many people it can be seen to serve in an afternoon. Some institutions exist precisely to offer what the rest of the city cannot: a place where nothing is being sold and no one needs you to be anything. Remove that, and you have not modernised the library. You have abolished it and kept the name.
items.question: The sentence 'By this arithmetic the most successful library would be a railway station' functions mainly to

options.text: recommend that libraries be built near transport hubs.
push the footfall measure to an absurd conclusion in order to expose its flaw.
show that railway stations are better funded than libraries.
concede that footfall is the most objective available measure.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 바로 앞 문장은 방문자 수 계산 방식(3시간 독서 1명 = 1회, 시장 통과 40명 = 40회)을 설명합니다. 2단계: 그 기준을 끝까지 적용하면 사람이 가장 많이 지나가는 기차역이 최고의 도서관이 된다는 불합리한 결론이 나옵니다. 이는 귀류법(reductio ad absurdum)으로 기준의 결함을 드러내는 장치입니다. 3단계: A와 C는 문자 그대로 읽은 오답이고, D는 글쓴이의 의도와 반대입니다. 정답 B.

items.stimulus:
Every map is a decision about what to leave out. A map that showed everything would be as large as the territory and, for that reason, useless. Cartographers therefore select, and selection is never neutral: a road atlas records petrol stations and omits the springs a walker would need; a tourist map enlarges the cathedral and shrinks the industrial estate where most residents work.

We tend to notice this bias only when a map fails us, when the shortcut it promised turns out to cross a river. Yet the more serious distortions are the ones that never fail their intended users. A map made for investors can be perfectly accurate about land values and perfectly silent about who lives on the land. Its silence is not an error; it is the purpose of the map, made visible to anyone who thinks to ask what the map is for.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 본문은 'would be as large as the territory and, for that reason, useless'라고 이유를 직접 제시합니다. 2단계: 지도의 가치는 선택과 단순화에 있는데, 모든 것을 담으면 영토 자체와 다를 바가 없어집니다. 3단계: A, B는 본문에 없는 이유이고, D는 선택의 편향에 관한 다른 예시입니다. 정답 C.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: [A⁻]/[HA] = 0.010/0.10 = 0.10. 2단계: pH = 4.76 + log(0.10) = 4.76 − 1.00 = 3.76. 3단계: 비를 거꾸로 넣으면 5.76(D)이 나오는 함정입니다. 2.88은 약산 단독 용액을 근사한 값으로 이 혼합 용액과 맞지 않습니다. 정답 B.

Under Condition II, the solvent itself (water or ethanol) replaces bromide, giving an alcohol or ether. Relative rates are shown in the table. In both conditions, the C–Br bond is broken.

table.title: Illustrative relative rates of reaction of alkyl bromides (ethyl bromide = 1 under each condition)
headers: Condition II: warmed in 80% aqueous ethanol, no added nucleophile

items.question: Which conclusion is most consistent with the data?

options.text: Both conditions proceed by the same mechanism, which is fastest for tertiary substrates.
Condition I proceeds by a mechanism that is hindered by bulky groups around the carbon; Condition II proceeds through a carbocation intermediate.
Condition I proceeds through a carbocation intermediate; Condition II is hindered by bulky groups around the carbon.
Neither condition depends on the structure of the alkyl group.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 조건 I은 메틸 > 1차 > 2차 > 3차 순으로 빨라집니다. 탄소 주변이 붐빌수록 느려지므로, 친핵체가 뒤쪽에서 공격하는 SN2(입체 장애에 민감)와 일치합니다. 2단계: 조건 II는 3차 >> 2차 > 1차 ≈ 메틸 순입니다. 탄소양이온이 안정할수록 빨라지므로 SN1(탄소양이온 중간체)과 일치합니다. 3단계: 강한 친핵체(I⁻)와 극성 비양성자성 용매(아세톤)는 SN2, 약한 친핵체(용매)와 극성 양성자성 용매는 SN1 조건이라는 점도 일치합니다. 정답 B.

items.stimulus: A student compares how four alkyl bromides react under two sets of conditions. Under Condition I, iodide ion replaces bromide. Under Condition II, the solvent itself (water or ethanol) replaces bromide, giving an alcohol or ether. Relative rates are shown in the table. In both conditions, the C–Br bond is broken.

table.title: Illustrative relative rates of reaction of alkyl bromides (ethyl bromide = 1 under each condition)
headers: Condition II: warmed in 80% aqueous ethanol, no added nucleophile

items.question: A pure sample of (S)-2-bromobutane is treated under Condition I. The major organic product is expected to be

options.text: predominantly (R)-2-iodobutane, formed with inversion of configuration.
predominantly (S)-2-iodobutane, formed with retention of configuration.
a racemic mixture of (R)- and (S)-2-iodobutane.
an achiral iodoalkane.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 앞 문항에서 조건 I은 SN2 메커니즘입니다. 2단계: SN2에서는 친핵체가 이탈기 반대쪽에서 공격하므로 입체 중심의 배열이 뒤집힙니다(Walden 반전). 3단계: Br과 I는 모두 우선순위가 가장 높은 치환기이므로, 공간 배열이 뒤집히면 표기도 S에서 R로 바뀝니다. 따라서 (R)-2-iodobutane이 생성됩니다. 라세미 혼합물(C)은 SN1의 특징입니다. 정답 A.

items.stimulus: A student compares how four alkyl bromides react under two sets of conditions. Under Condition I, iodide ion replaces bromide. Under Condition II, the solvent itself (water or ethanol) replaces bromide, giving an alcohol or ether. Relative rates are shown in the table. In both conditions, the C–Br bond is broken.

table.title: Illustrative relative rates of reaction of alkyl bromides (ethyl bromide = 1 under each condition)
headers: Condition II: warmed in 80% aqueous ethanol, no added nucleophile

items.question: A small amount of sodium azide (NaN₃, a good nucleophile) is added to tert-butyl bromide under Condition II. Compared with the reaction without azide, the most likely result is that

options.text: the rate of disappearance of tert-butyl bromide increases in proportion to [N₃⁻], and only the azide product forms.
the rate of disappearance of tert-butyl bromide is largely unchanged, but some azide product forms alongside the alcohol and ether.
the reaction stops, because azide reacts with the solvent.
the rate falls sharply, because azide hinders the tertiary carbon.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 조건 II에서 3차 브로마이드는 SN1으로 반응합니다. SN1의 속도 결정 단계는 C–Br 결합이 끊어져 탄소양이온이 생기는 단계이며, 친핵체는 관여하지 않습니다. 2단계: 따라서 rate = k[(CH₃)₃CBr]이고, 친핵체(N₃⁻)를 더해도 기질이 사라지는 속도는 거의 변하지 않습니다. 3단계: 그러나 생성된 탄소양이온은 물, 에탄올, 아자이드 중 무엇과도 빠르게 결합할 수 있으므로 생성물 분포는 달라져 아자이드 생성물이 일부 섞입니다. 4단계: A는 SN2식 속도 의존을 가정한 오답이고, C와 D는 근거가 없습니다. 정답 B. (이온 세기 증가로 속도가 약간 변할 수는 있지만 [N₃⁻]에 비례하지는 않습니다.)

items.stimulus:
Dinitrogen tetroxide (colourless) and nitrogen dioxide (brown) exist in equilibrium:
N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g)
Kc = [NO₂]² / [N₂O₄]
A student seals a mixture of the two gases in a gas syringe and observes the colour under different conditions. Equilibrium constants are given in the table.
items.question: At constant temperature, the plunger is pushed in quickly so the gas volume is halved. Which observation is expected?

options.text: The colour immediately becomes lighter and then darkens further over time.
The colour does not change, because Kc is constant at constant temperature.
The colour immediately becomes darker and then becomes partly lighter as the system re-establishes equilibrium.
The colour immediately becomes darker and continues to darken until all N₂O₄ has decomposed.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 부피를 절반으로 줄이면 모든 기체의 농도가 순간적으로 2배가 되므로 갈색(NO₂)이 곧바로 진해집니다. 2단계: 압력이 커지면 평형은 기체 몰수가 적은 쪽(N₂O₄, 1 mol 대 2 mol)으로 이동합니다. 따라서 NO₂ 일부가 N₂O₄로 바뀌며 색이 다소 옅어집니다. 3단계: 그래도 새 평형의 [NO₂]는 압축 전보다 높습니다. Kc가 일정해도 농도는 달라질 수 있으므로 B는 틀렸습니다. 정답 C.

items.stimulus:
Dinitrogen tetroxide (colourless) and nitrogen dioxide (brown) exist in equilibrium:
N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g)
Kc = [NO₂]² / [N₂O₄]
A student seals a mixture of the two gases in a gas syringe and observes the colour under different conditions. Equilibrium constants are given in the table.
items.question: At 298 K, an equilibrium mixture has [N₂O₄] = 0.0200 mol L⁻¹. The equilibrium concentration of NO₂ is closest to

options.text: 9.2 × 10⁻⁵ mol L⁻¹
4.8 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹
9.6 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹
3.0 × 10⁻² mol L⁻¹

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: Kc = [NO₂]²/[N₂O₄]이므로 [NO₂]² = Kc × [N₂O₄] = (4.6 × 10⁻³)(0.0200) = 9.2 × 10⁻⁵. 2단계: [NO₂] = √(9.2 × 10⁻⁵) ≈ 9.6 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹(9.6² = 92.16이므로 검산 가능). 3단계: A는 제곱근을 취하지 않은 값입니다. 정답 C.

items.stimulus:
Propane burns completely in excess oxygen:
C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O
Molar masses (g mol⁻¹): C₃H₈ = 44, CO₂ = 44, H₂O = 18.
items.question: What mass of water is produced when 4.4 g of propane burns completely?
items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 프로페인의 몰수 = 4.4 g ÷ 44 g mol⁻¹ = 0.10 mol. 2단계: 반응식에서 C₃H₈ 1 mol당 H₂O 4 mol이 생기므로 H₂O = 0.40 mol. 3단계: 질량 = 0.40 × 18 = 7.2 g. 13.2 g은 CO₂(0.30 mol × 44)의 질량을 구한 함정입니다. 정답 A.

items.stimulus:
Standard reduction potentials at 25 °C:
Ag⁺(aq) + e⁻ → Ag(s)   E° = +0.80 V
Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Cu(s)   E° = +0.34 V
Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Zn(s)   E° = −0.76 V
A galvanic cell is built from a zinc electrode in 1 mol L⁻¹ Zn²⁺(aq) and a silver electrode in 1 mol L⁻¹ Ag⁺(aq), joined by a salt bridge.
items.question: Which statement about this cell under standard conditions is correct?

options.text: E°cell = 1.56 V, and electrons flow through the external wire from zinc to silver.
E°cell = 2.36 V, and electrons flow through the external wire from zinc to silver.
E°cell = 1.56 V, and electrons flow through the external wire from silver to zinc.
E°cell = 0.04 V, and zinc is the cathode.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 환원 전위가 더 큰 Ag⁺/Ag가 환원(환원 전극 cathode, 이 전지의 + 극), 더 작은 Zn²⁺/Zn이 산화(산화 전극 anode, − 극)됩니다. 2단계: E°cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode) = 0.80 − (−0.76) = 1.56 V. 전위는 세기 성질이므로 Ag 반쪽 반응에 2를 곱해도 E°는 2배가 되지 않습니다. 2.36 V(B)는 0.80을 2배 한 함정입니다. 3단계: 전자는 산화가 일어나는 아연에서 외부 도선을 따라 은으로 흐릅니다. 정답 A.

items.stimulus: 2,3-Dibromobutane, CH₃–CHBr–CHBr–CH₃, has two stereocentres (C2 and C3). Each stereocentre carries the same set of four different groups: H, Br, CH₃ and the other CHBr–CH₃ unit.
items.question: How many distinct stereoisomers of 2,3-dibromobutane exist?
items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 입체 중심이 2개이므로 최대 2² = 4가지(RR, SS, RS, SR)를 생각할 수 있습니다. 2단계: 두 입체 중심의 치환기 구성이 동일하므로 분자에 대칭면이 생길 수 있습니다. (2R,3S)와 (2S,3R)은 같은 분자이며, 거울상과 겹쳐지는 비키랄 meso 화합물입니다. 3단계: 따라서 (2R,3R), (2S,3S) 거울상 이성질체 한 쌍과 meso 형 하나, 총 3가지입니다. 정답 B.

items.stimulus: A radioactive tracer used to label a compound decays by first-order kinetics with a half-life of 6.0 hours.
items.question: What percentage of the original tracer remains after 24 hours?

items.stimulus: An enzyme was assayed with and without two different inhibitors, X and Y, each present at a fixed concentration. For an enzyme following Michaelis–Menten kinetics, v = Vmax[S] / (Km + [S]), where Km is the substrate concentration at which the rate is half of Vmax. Assume that in the absence of inhibitor Vmax = 100 µmol min⁻¹.

table.title: Initial reaction rate (µmol min⁻¹) at different substrate concentrations (same enzyme concentration throughout)

items.question: The Km of the enzyme in the absence of inhibitor is closest to

options.text: 0.5 mmol L⁻¹
2.0 mmol L⁻¹
5.0 mmol L⁻¹
50 mmol L⁻¹

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: Km은 속도가 Vmax의 절반이 되는 기질 농도입니다. Vmax = 100이므로 v = 50인 지점을 찾습니다. 2단계: 억제제가 없을 때 [S] = 2.0 mmol L⁻¹에서 v = 50입니다. 따라서 Km ≈ 2.0 mmol L⁻¹. 3단계: D의 50은 '속도 50'과 농도를 혼동한 함정입니다. 정답 B.

items.stimulus: An enzyme was assayed with and without two different inhibitors, X and Y, each present at a fixed concentration. For an enzyme following Michaelis–Menten kinetics, v = Vmax[S] / (Km + [S]), where Km is the substrate concentration at which the rate is half of Vmax. Assume that in the absence of inhibitor Vmax = 100 µmol min⁻¹.

table.title: Initial reaction rate (µmol min⁻¹) at different substrate concentrations (same enzyme concentration throughout)

items.question: Assume that inhibitor X does not change Vmax. In the presence of inhibitor X, the substrate concentration needed to reach a rate of 50 µmol min⁻¹ is closest to

options.text: 2 mmol L⁻¹
4 mmol L⁻¹
10 mmol L⁻¹
This rate cannot be reached in the presence of X.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: Vmax가 100으로 그대로라면 v = 50인 농도가 X 존재 시의 겉보기 Km(Km,app)입니다. 2단계: 아무 데이터 점 하나로 계산합니다. [S] = 2.0에서 v = 33이므로 33 = 100 × 2/(Km,app + 2) → Km,app + 2 = 6.06 → Km,app ≈ 4. 3단계: 검산: [S] = 5.0에서 100 × 5/(4 + 5) = 55.6 ≈ 56으로 표와 일치합니다. 표에서도 50은 2.0(33)과 5.0(56) 사이에 있습니다. 4단계: X는 Vmax를 바꾸지 않고 Km을 2배로 높이므로 경쟁적 억제제의 특징을 보입니다. 정답 B.

items.stimulus: An enzyme was assayed with and without two different inhibitors, X and Y, each present at a fixed concentration. For an enzyme following Michaelis–Menten kinetics, v = Vmax[S] / (Km + [S]), where Km is the substrate concentration at which the rate is half of Vmax. Assume that in the absence of inhibitor Vmax = 100 µmol min⁻¹.

table.title: Initial reaction rate (µmol min⁻¹) at different substrate concentrations (same enzyme concentration throughout)

items.question: Which statement about inhibitors X and Y is best supported by the data?

options.text: Both inhibitors lower Vmax to about half of its uninhibited value.
Inhibitor Y increases Km but leaves Vmax unchanged.
Inhibitor X binds irreversibly to the enzyme.
The effect of X, but not of Y, can be largely overcome by raising the substrate concentration.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: [S] = 100에서 X 존재 시 속도는 96으로 억제제가 없을 때(98)와 거의 같습니다. 기질을 늘리면 X의 효과가 사라지므로 경쟁적 억제입니다. 2단계: Y 존재 시 속도는 기질이 많아도 약 50에서 포화됩니다. Vmax가 절반으로 떨어진 것이고, 기질을 늘려도 회복되지 않습니다(비경쟁적 억제). Y의 경우에도 v = 25(Vmax 50의 절반)가 [S] = 2.0에서 나타나므로 Km은 그대로입니다. 3단계: A는 X에 대해 틀렸고, B는 Y의 특성을 거꾸로 서술했으며, C의 비가역 결합은 기질로 극복되는 X의 결과와 맞지 않습니다. 정답 D.

items.stimulus:
A rare condition is caused by a recessive allele carried on the X chromosome. In one family:
• Generation I: an unaffected woman (I-1) with no family history of the condition and an affected man (I-2) have two children.
• Generation II: an unaffected daughter (II-1) and an unaffected son (II-2).
• II-1 has children with an unaffected man (II-3) who has no family history of the condition.
Assume that no new mutations occur and that the allele is fully penetrant.
items.question: What is the probability that II-1 is a carrier of the allele?
items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 딸은 아버지에게서 반드시 X 염색체를 하나 받습니다. 아버지 I-2는 환자이므로 그의 유일한 X 염색체에 열성 대립유전자가 있습니다. 2단계: 따라서 II-1은 반드시 이 대립유전자를 하나 가지며, 표현형이 정상이므로 보인자입니다. 확률 1. 정답 D.

items.stimulus:
A rare condition is caused by a recessive allele carried on the X chromosome. In one family:
• Generation I: an unaffected woman (I-1) with no family history of the condition and an affected man (I-2) have two children.
• Generation II: an unaffected daughter (II-1) and an unaffected son (II-2).
• II-1 has children with an unaffected man (II-3) who has no family history of the condition.
Assume that no new mutations occur and that the allele is fully penetrant.
items.question: What is the probability that the first child of II-1 and II-3 is an affected son?
items.explanation_ko: 1단계: II-1은 보인자(XᴬXᵃ), II-3은 정상(XᴬY)입니다. 2단계: 아들일 확률 1/2, 아들이 어머니에게서 Xᵃ를 받을 확률 1/2. 3단계: 따라서 '환자인 아들'일 확률 = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4. 1/2(D)은 '아들이라는 조건 아래' 환자일 확률로, 문항이 묻는 값과 다릅니다. 정답 C.

items.stimulus:
A rare condition is caused by a recessive allele carried on the X chromosome. In one family:
• Generation I: an unaffected woman (I-1) with no family history of the condition and an affected man (I-2) have two children.
• Generation II: an unaffected daughter (II-1) and an unaffected son (II-2).
• II-1 has children with an unaffected man (II-3) who has no family history of the condition.
Assume that no new mutations occur and that the allele is fully penetrant.
items.question: In a different, unrelated family, which observation would provide the strongest evidence that this condition is NOT inherited in an X-linked recessive manner?

options.text: Most people with the condition are male.
An affected man and a carrier woman have an affected daughter.
An affected man and a woman shown by genetic testing not to carry the allele have an affected son.
All the daughters of an affected man are unaffected.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: X 연관 열성 유전의 핵심 특징은 아버지가 아들에게 X 염색체를 주지 않는다는 점입니다(아들은 아버지에게서 Y를 받음). 2단계: 어머니가 대립유전자를 가질 가능성이 없는데(가족력 없음, 신규 돌연변이 없음 가정) 환자 아버지에게서 환자 아들이 나왔다면 남성에서 남성으로 전달된 것이므로 X 연관 열성과 모순됩니다. 3단계: A, B, D는 모두 X 연관 열성 유전과 일치하는 관찰입니다(B: 딸은 아버지의 Xᵃ와 어머니의 Xᵃ를 받을 수 있음). 정답 C.

items.stimulus:
Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) is released from the posterior pituitary when plasma osmolality rises. In the principal cells of the renal collecting duct, ADH binds V2 receptors on the basolateral membrane. This raises intracellular cAMP and causes vesicles containing aquaporin-2 water channels to fuse with the apical membrane. Water then moves out of the tubular fluid into the hypertonic medullary interstitium, concentrating the urine. Plasma osmolality is sensed by hypothalamic osmoreceptors, which control ADH release by negative feedback.

In a study, three groups went without water for 12 hours, after which urine osmolality was measured. Each person was then injected with synthetic ADH and urine osmolality was measured again.

table.title: Urine osmolality (mOsm kg⁻¹) in three groups
headers: 1 h after injection of synthetic ADH
rows: 3: normal ADH secretion, non-functional V2 receptors

items.question: A drug that completely blocks the rise in cAMP in collecting-duct principal cells is given to healthy volunteers before the same protocol. Their results would most closely resemble those of

options.text: Group 3, because ADH could bind its receptor but could not trigger aquaporin-2 insertion.
Group 1, because ADH secretion is unaffected.
Group 2, because ADH secretion would stop.
none of the groups, because urine would become more concentrated than in Group 1.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 본문에 따르면 ADH → V2 수용체 → cAMP 상승 → 아쿠아포린-2 삽입 순서로 작용합니다. 2단계: cAMP 상승을 막으면 ADH가 분비되고 수용체에 결합해도 신호가 전달되지 않습니다. 따라서 탈수 후에도, ADH 주사 후에도 소변이 묽게 유지됩니다. 3단계: 이는 수용체 이후 경로가 작동하지 않는 3군(140 → 150)과 같은 양상입니다. 2군은 외부 ADH 주사에 반응하므로 해당하지 않습니다. 정답 A.

items.stimulus:
Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) is released from the posterior pituitary when plasma osmolality rises. In the principal cells of the renal collecting duct, ADH binds V2 receptors on the basolateral membrane. This raises intracellular cAMP and causes vesicles containing aquaporin-2 water channels to fuse with the apical membrane. Water then moves out of the tubular fluid into the hypertonic medullary interstitium, concentrating the urine. Plasma osmolality is sensed by hypothalamic osmoreceptors, which control ADH release by negative feedback.

In a study, three groups went without water for 12 hours, after which urine osmolality was measured. Each person was then injected with synthetic ADH and urine osmolality was measured again.

table.title: Urine osmolality (mOsm kg⁻¹) in three groups
headers: 1 h after injection of synthetic ADH
rows: 3: normal ADH secretion, non-functional V2 receptors

items.question: After 12 hours without water, how would plasma ADH concentration in Group 3 most likely compare with that in Group 1?

options.text: Higher, because continued loss of dilute urine raises plasma osmolality further, stimulating more ADH release.
Lower, because the non-functional receptors send an inhibitory signal to the pituitary.
The same, because both groups have normal ADH secretion.
Zero, because without functional receptors ADH is not released.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 3군은 ADH 분비 기능은 정상이지만 신장이 반응하지 못해 탈수 중에도 묽은 소변(140)으로 물을 계속 잃습니다. 2단계: 그 결과 혈장 삼투압이 1군보다 더 크게 상승하고, 시상하부 삼투수용체가 이를 감지해 ADH를 더 많이 분비합니다. 음성 되먹임의 고리(물 재흡수 → 삼투압 정상화)가 닫히지 않으므로 ADH가 높게 유지됩니다. 3단계: B의 억제 신호는 본문에 없고, C는 분비 '능력'이 같다는 것과 분비 '양'이 같다는 것을 혼동한 오답이며, D는 본문(분비 정상)과 모순됩니다. 정답 A.

items.stimulus: In intestinal epithelial cells, glucose is taken up from the gut lumen by a symporter that moves one glucose molecule together with two Na⁺ ions into the cell. Glucose concentration inside the cell is higher than in the lumen. The low intracellular Na⁺ concentration is maintained by Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pumps on the basolateral membrane. Ouabain is a specific inhibitor of Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase.
items.question: If these cells are treated with ouabain, glucose uptake from the lumen would be expected to

options.text: increase, because more Na⁺ would remain in the lumen to drive the symporter.
stay the same, because the symporter does not hydrolyse ATP itself.
decrease, because the Na⁺ gradient that drives glucose uptake against its concentration gradient would gradually dissipate.
decrease immediately to zero, because ouabain binds directly to the glucose symporter.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 포도당은 농도 기울기를 거슬러 세포 안으로 들어가므로 에너지가 필요합니다. 그 에너지원은 Na⁺의 전기화학적 기울기입니다(2차 능동 수송). 2단계: Na⁺ 기울기는 Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase가 유지합니다. 우아바인으로 펌프를 막으면 세포 내 Na⁺가 점점 쌓여 기울기가 줄어들고, 공동 수송체의 구동력도 줄어듭니다. 3단계: B는 수송체가 ATP를 직접 쓰지 않는다는 점만 보고 간접 의존성을 놓친 오답이고, D는 우아바인이 펌프에 특이적이라는 조건과 모순됩니다. 정답 C.

items.stimulus: A researcher studies a hormone. Its effects appear only after several hours and are blocked by drugs that inhibit transcription. Treating target cells briefly with a protease that removes all proteins from the outer surface of the plasma membrane does not prevent the hormone's effect.
items.question: These observations are most consistent with the hormone being

options.text: a lipid-soluble hormone that acts through an intracellular receptor that regulates gene expression.
a peptide hormone that acts through a G protein-coupled receptor on the cell surface.
a hormone that acts by opening ion channels in the plasma membrane.
a water-soluble hormone that cannot cross the plasma membrane.

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 세포 표면 단백질을 제거해도 효과가 유지되므로 수용체는 세포막 바깥이 아니라 세포 안에 있습니다. 2단계: 효과가 몇 시간 뒤에 나타나고 전사 억제제로 차단되므로 유전자 발현 조절을 통해 작용합니다. 3단계: 세포막을 통과해 세포 내 수용체에 결합하고 전사를 조절하는 것은 스테로이드 같은 지용성 호르몬의 특징입니다. B, C, D는 모두 세포 표면 수용체가 필요합니다. 정답 A.

items.stimulus: In a polymerase chain reaction (PCR), each cycle of denaturation, primer annealing and extension doubles the number of copies of the target DNA sequence, provided reagents are not limiting.
items.question: A reaction starts with 4 copies of a double-stranded target sequence. Assuming perfect efficiency, how many cycles are needed to obtain 4096 copies?
items.explanation_ko: 1단계: n회 후 복사본 수 = 4 × 2ⁿ. 2단계: 4 × 2ⁿ = 4096 → 2ⁿ = 1024 → n = 10. 3단계: 12(C)는 시작 복사본을 1개로 가정해 2¹² = 4096을 푼 함정이고, 1024(D)는 2ⁿ 값 자체를 고른 오답입니다. 정답 B.

items.stimulus: An autosomal recessive condition affects 1 in 400 people in a large, randomly mating population that is in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium.
items.question: What proportion of the population is expected to be heterozygous carriers?

items.stimulus: A 2.0 kg block is released from rest at the top of a frictionless ramp inclined at 30° to the horizontal. The ramp is 5.0 m long (measured along its surface). At the bottom, the block moves without loss of speed onto a horizontal rough surface, where the coefficient of kinetic friction between block and surface is 0.25. Take g = 10 m s⁻², sin 30° = 0.50 and ignore air resistance.
items.question: The speed of the block at the bottom of the ramp is closest to

options.text: 3.5 m s⁻¹
5.0 m s⁻¹
7.1 m s⁻¹
10 m s⁻¹

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 높이 h = 5.0 × sin 30° = 2.5 m. 2단계: 마찰이 없으므로 mgh = ½mv² → v² = 2gh = 2 × 10 × 2.5 = 50. 3단계: v = √50 ≈ 7.1 m s⁻¹. 경사면 길이 5.0 m를 높이로 착각하면 10 m s⁻¹(D)가 나옵니다. 정답 C.

items.stimulus: A 2.0 kg block is released from rest at the top of a frictionless ramp inclined at 30° to the horizontal. The ramp is 5.0 m long (measured along its surface). At the bottom, the block moves without loss of speed onto a horizontal rough surface, where the coefficient of kinetic friction between block and surface is 0.25. Take g = 10 m s⁻², sin 30° = 0.50 and ignore air resistance.
items.question: How far does the block slide along the rough horizontal surface before stopping?
items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 수평면에서 마찰력 f = μmg = 0.25 × 2.0 × 10 = 5.0 N. 2단계: 바닥에서의 운동 에너지 = ½ × 2.0 × 50 = 50 J (또는 mgh = 2.0 × 10 × 2.5 = 50 J). 3단계: 마찰력이 한 일 = 운동 에너지 → 5.0 × d = 50 → d = 10 m. 질량과 무관하게 d = h/μ = 2.5/0.25 = 10 m로도 구할 수 있습니다. 7.1 m는 바닥에서의 속력(7.1 m s⁻¹) 숫자를 거리로 착각한 함정입니다. 정답 D.

items.stimulus: A circuit consists of a 12 V battery of negligible internal resistance connected to resistor R1 = 4.0 Ω in series with a parallel combination of resistors R2 = 6.0 Ω and R3 = 3.0 Ω. Connecting wires have negligible resistance.
items.question: The current through R3 is closest to

items.stimulus: A circuit consists of a 12 V battery of negligible internal resistance connected to resistor R1 = 4.0 Ω in series with a parallel combination of resistors R2 = 6.0 Ω and R3 = 3.0 Ω. Connecting wires have negligible resistance.
items.question: Resistor R3 is now removed, leaving a gap in its branch. The power dissipated in R1 changes from its original value to approximately
items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 원래 회로에서 R1 전류는 2.0 A이므로 P = I²R = 4.0 × 4.0 = 16 W. 2단계: R3를 제거하면 R1과 R2만 직렬로 남아 전체 저항 = 4.0 + 6.0 = 10 Ω, 전류 = 12/10 = 1.2 A. 3단계: R1의 전력 = 1.2² × 4.0 = 1.44 × 4.0 = 5.76 W ≈ 5.8 W. 16 W(C)는 변하기 전 값이고, 36 W(D)는 배터리 전압 전체가 R1에 걸린다고 본 오답입니다. 정답 A.

items.stimulus: A pipe of length 0.85 m is closed at one end and open at the other. The speed of sound in the air inside is 340 m s⁻¹. In a pipe closed at one end, standing waves have a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end (ignore end corrections).
items.question: What are the two lowest resonant frequencies of the pipe?

options.text: 50 Hz and 150 Hz
100 Hz and 200 Hz
100 Hz and 300 Hz
200 Hz and 400 Hz

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 한쪽이 닫힌 관의 기본 진동은 관 길이가 파장의 1/4입니다. λ = 4L = 3.4 m. 2단계: f₁ = v/λ = 340/3.4 = 100 Hz. 3단계: 닫힌 관에서는 홀수 배음만 존재하므로 다음 공명은 3f₁ = 300 Hz입니다. B는 닫힌 관 기본음에 모든 정수 배음(열린 관의 배음 규칙)을 잘못 적용한 값이고, D는 양쪽이 열린 관으로 계산한 값(f₁ = v/2L = 200 Hz, 다음 400 Hz)입니다. 정답 C.

items.stimulus: A rigid, sealed steel container holds an ideal gas at 27 °C and a pressure of 150 kPa. The container is heated until the gas reaches 127 °C. The volume of the container does not change.
items.question: The new pressure of the gas is closest to

options.text: 113 kPa
200 kPa
300 kPa
706 kPa

items.explanation_ko: 1단계: 부피와 몰수가 일정하므로 P/T가 일정합니다(게이뤼삭 법칙). 온도는 반드시 켈빈으로 바꿉니다. T₁ = 300 K, T₂ = 400 K. 2단계: P₂ = 150 × 400/300 = 200 kPa. 3단계: 섭씨를 그대로 쓰면 150 × 127/27 ≈ 706 kPa(D)라는 함정이 나옵니다. 정답 B.

prompts: Every age believes it stands at the summit; every later age finds it halfway up the slope.
Progress is the name we give to change after we have decided we like it.
A society that cannot say what it refuses to give up has no way of knowing whether it is progressing or merely moving.
The road forward is paved with the things someone else was told to leave behind.
We measure advancement by what we can do, and rarely by what we no longer need.
essays.approach_ko: 진보를 무조건 좋은 것으로 전제하지 말고, '누구의 기준으로, 무엇을 대가로 한 진보인가'를 중심 질문으로 잡는 것이 좋습니다. 가능한 각도는 세 가지입니다. 첫째, 진보의 판단이 사후적이고 가치 의존적이라는 점(두 번째 문장), 둘째, 진보의 비용이 특정 집단에 전가된다는 점(네 번째 문장), 셋째, 지킬 가치를 정하지 않으면 변화와 진보를 구별할 수 없다는 점(세 번째 문장)입니다. 구조는 서론에서 하나의 명확한 입장을 밝히고, 본론 두세 단락에서 의료 기술, 도시 개발, 노동 자동화 같은 구체적 사례로 입장을 검증한 뒤, 반론(예: 수명 연장과 빈곤 감소는 측정 가능한 진보다)을 인정하고 재반박하는 단락을 넣는 방식이 안정적입니다. 흔한 실수는 기술 발전의 장단점을 나열만 하고 결론이 '양면이 있다'로 끝나는 것입니다. 채점자는 사고의 깊이와 일관된 논지를 보므로, 결론에서 처음 질문에 대한 자신의 답을 다듬어 제시해야 합니다.
sampleThesis: Progress is real, but it can only be recognised by a society that has first decided what it will not trade away; without that, change is merely motion.
Because the costs of advancement fall unevenly, a claim of progress should be judged by those who paid for it, not only by those who enjoy its benefits.
The surest sign of progress is not new capability but the disappearance of old necessities, such as a disease that no longer needs treating.

prompts: A law that is never questioned soon forgets why it was written.
Fairness is easy to agree on in general and nearly impossible to agree on in particular.
The scales of justice balance only after someone has decided what each side weighs.
Punishment answers the question 'What did you do?'; justice must also ask 'What happens now?'
A court can declare a winner; only a community can make the loser believe it was fair.
essays.approach_ko: 정의를 법 절차와 동일시할지, 더 넓은 사회적 정당성으로 볼지 먼저 정하세요. 각도로는 응보적 정의와 회복적 정의의 대비(네 번째 문장), 정의의 기준 자체가 권력에 의해 설정된다는 비판(세 번째 문장), 판결의 정당성은 공동체의 수용에서 나온다는 관점(다섯 번째 문장)이 있습니다. 사례로는 청소년 범죄 처리, 의료 자원 배분의 공정성, 역사적 불의에 대한 배상 논쟁 등을 활용할 수 있습니다. 실존 사건이나 판례를 쓸 때는 세부 사실을 틀리지 않게 일반화해서 쓰는 것이 안전합니다. 흔한 실수는 '정의는 중요하다' 수준의 당위로 흐르는 것과, 여러 문장을 하나씩 해설하는 데 그치는 것입니다. 한두 문장을 출발점으로 삼아 자신의 주장을 세우면 충분합니다.
sampleThesis: Justice that ends with punishment is incomplete, because a just system must also take responsibility for what the offender, the victim and the community become afterwards.
Laws gain their authority not from being obeyed but from surviving repeated questioning; a legal system that discourages challenge slowly loses its claim to be just.
Agreement on fairness in the abstract is cheap; the real test of a society's commitment to justice is whether it accepts verdicts that go against its own interests.

prompts: Every tool that saves us time also decides how we will spend it.
A convenience becomes a dependency on the day it stops working.
A technology has truly won when people forget there was ever another way to do the task.
We learn to build a machine in a decade and spend a century learning when not to use it.
A device that knows everything about you is a mirror you cannot look away from.
essays.approach_ko: 기술이 중립적 도구인지, 인간의 선택과 습관을 재구성하는 힘인지가 핵심 쟁점입니다. 각도로는 편리함이 의존으로 바뀌는 과정(두 번째 문장), 보이지 않게 된 기술이 가장 큰 영향력을 갖는다는 역설(세 번째 문장), 기술 발전 속도와 사회적 판단 속도의 차이(네 번째 문장), 데이터와 감시가 자기 인식에 미치는 영향(다섯 번째 문장)이 있습니다. 의학 지망생이라면 전자 의무기록, 원격 진료, 웨어러블 기기, 인공지능 진단 보조 같은 의료 사례를 쓰면 자연스럽습니다. 다만 의학 지식을 과시하기보다 논지를 뒷받침하는 데 사례를 써야 합니다. 흔한 실수는 '기술은 양날의 검' 같은 상투적 표현으로 시작하고 끝내는 것입니다.
sampleThesis: The danger of a technology lies less in its failures than in its success at becoming invisible, because what we no longer notice we no longer question.
Time-saving tools do not free our time so much as reassign it, and a society should judge them by what they lead us to do with the hours they save.
Since our judgement about new technologies always lags behind their adoption, the responsible course is to build in ways to reverse them, not to wait for certainty.

prompts: A custom survives not because it is true but because it is shared.
To keep a tradition alive, each generation must be allowed to change it a little.
What one generation calls heritage, the next may call a habit it never chose.
The newest ideas often turn out to be old ones that were waiting for the right moment.
A people without rituals must invent reasons to gather; a people with too many may forget the reasons altogether.
essays.approach_ko: 전통을 보존과 변화 중 하나로 단순화하지 말고, 전통이 살아남는 조건을 묻는 방식이 좋습니다. 각도로는 전통의 정당성이 진리가 아니라 공유에서 나온다는 관점(첫 번째 문장), 전통은 변형을 통해서만 이어진다는 역설(두 번째 문장), 세대 간 동의 없는 계승의 문제(세 번째 문장), 의례의 사회적 기능과 형식화(다섯 번째 문장)가 있습니다. 한국 학생이라면 명절 문화, 제사, 가족 호칭, 직장 위계 문화의 변화 등 자신이 잘 아는 사례를 쓰면 구체성이 살아납니다. 특정 문화를 우월하거나 열등하게 그리는 표현은 피하고, 결론에서 전통과 개인의 자율 사이의 균형점을 자신의 언어로 제시하세요.
sampleThesis: A tradition is best preserved not by freezing it but by allowing each generation to renegotiate it, since a custom that cannot change will eventually be abandoned rather than reformed.
Shared rituals hold communities together, but once their purpose is forgotten they bind people to obligations they never chose; the value of a tradition lies in whether it can still explain itself.
Much of what we call innovation is tradition rediscovered, which suggests that respecting the past and embracing change are less opposed than they appear.

prompts: A country's wealth is best counted at the bus stop, not in the boardroom.
Wealth is most visible where it is newest and least visible where it is oldest.
Every fortune is a story about luck told as a story about effort.
Poverty is not only a lack of money; it is a shortage of second chances.
Generosity costs the wealthy little and the poor a great deal, yet we praise both in the same words.
essays.approach_ko: 부를 개인의 성취로 볼지, 사회 구조와 운의 산물로 볼지가 핵심 축입니다. 각도로는 사회의 부를 평균이 아니라 바닥으로 측정해야 한다는 관점(첫 번째 문장), 성공 서사에서 운과 구조가 지워지는 문제(세 번째 문장), 빈곤을 소득이 아니라 기회와 회복력의 결핍으로 보는 관점(네 번째 문장), 기부와 미덕의 비대칭(다섯 번째 문장)이 있습니다. 보건의료와 연결하면 건강 불평등, 의료 접근성, 질병이 빈곤을 낳는 악순환을 사례로 쓸 수 있습니다. 통계 수치를 쓸 때는 정확히 기억나지 않는 숫자를 지어내지 말고 경향으로 서술하는 것이 안전합니다. 정치적 구호처럼 들리지 않도록 반대 입장(노력과 인센티브의 중요성)을 공정하게 다루면 사고의 성숙도가 드러납니다.
sampleThesis: A society's wealth should be measured from the bottom rather than the top, because prosperity that leaves many without second chances is concentration, not abundance.
Effort matters, but the stories we tell about fortunes systematically erase luck, and policies built on those stories punish people for misfortune they did not choose.
Poverty is best understood not as a shortage of money but as a shortage of room for error, which is why small setbacks such as an illness can have lasting consequences for the poor.

prompts: Failure is a teacher who never repeats the lesson in the same words.
We fear failing in public far more than we fear never trying in private.
Some failures close a door; others reveal that we were standing in the wrong corridor.
A person who has never failed has usually never been measured.
Success forgets its causes quickly; failure remembers every one of them.
essays.approach_ko: Task B는 개인적, 사회적 주제이므로 성찰적이고 개인적인 글이 잘 맞습니다. 다만 개인 일화만 길게 늘어놓으면 깊이가 부족해 보이므로, 경험을 통해 일반적인 통찰로 나아가야 합니다. 각도로는 공개적 실패에 대한 두려움이 시도 자체를 막는다는 점(두 번째 문장), 실패가 방향 전환의 신호가 된다는 점(세 번째 문장), 성공보다 실패가 원인 분석을 더 잘하게 만든다는 점(다섯 번째 문장)이 있습니다. 구조는 짧은 장면이나 일화로 시작해, 그 경험이 드러내는 질문을 제시하고, 그 질문을 더 넓은 맥락(교육, 의료 현장의 오류 보고 문화 등)으로 확장한 뒤, 처음 장면으로 돌아와 마무리하는 원형 구조가 효과적입니다. 흔한 실수는 '실패는 성공의 어머니' 같은 결론으로 끝내는 것입니다. 실패가 항상 배움으로 이어지는 것은 아니라는 단서를 다는 것만으로도 글이 훨씬 성숙해집니다.
sampleThesis: Failure teaches only those willing to examine it, and the greater obstacle to growth is not failing but the fear of being seen to fail.
Not every failure is a lesson in perseverance; some are evidence that the goal itself was wrong, and the harder skill is telling the two apart.
Because success rarely invites scrutiny, a person or a profession that hides its failures loses the most honest record of what actually works.

prompts: Old friends keep the drafts of us that we would rather have thrown away.
Friendships rarely end with an argument; they end with a silence no one thought to break.
We choose our friends, and then, slowly, they choose who we become.
The test of a friendship is not how it survives a crisis but how it survives a dull year.
It is easier to be loyal to a friend than to be honest with one.
essays.approach_ko: 우정을 정의하려 하기보다 우정이 유지되거나 끝나는 방식, 우정이 사람을 바꾸는 방식에 초점을 맞추면 글이 구체적이 됩니다. 각도로는 극적인 위기보다 일상의 무관심이 관계를 끝낸다는 점(두 번째, 네 번째 문장), 친구가 정체성 형성에 미치는 영향(세 번째 문장), 충성과 정직 사이의 긴장(다섯 번째 문장)이 있습니다. 개인 경험을 쓸 때는 실명이나 지나치게 사적인 정보 대신 상황 중심으로 서술하세요. 충성과 정직의 긴장은 의료인의 동료 관계(동료의 실수를 지적해야 하는 상황)로 확장할 수도 있습니다. 흔한 실수는 친구의 장점을 나열하는 수필이 되는 것입니다.
sampleThesis: Most friendships do not break; they fade, which means that the real work of friendship lies in the unremarkable effort of staying in touch.
Loyalty that never risks honesty is a comfortable imitation of friendship, because a true friend is willing to be unwelcome for a moment in order to be useful for a lifetime.
We tend to think of friends as reflections of who we are, but over time they shape who we become, so choosing friends is quietly choosing a future self.

prompts: Solitude is the room in which we discover what we actually think.
The same empty room can feel like a refuge on Sunday and a sentence on Monday.
Those who cannot bear their own company make demanding companions for others.
A crowded life can be the loneliest place of all.
Quiet is where the questions we postpone come to wait for us.
essays.approach_ko: 고독(solitude)과 외로움(loneliness)을 구별하는 것이 출발점입니다. 두 번째 문장이 이 구분을 제시하므로, 서론에서 두 개념을 자신의 말로 정리하면 글의 축이 선명해집니다. 각도로는 혼자 있는 시간이 사고와 자기 이해에 필요하다는 관점(첫 번째 문장), 혼자 있지 못하는 사람이 관계에 과도하게 기대게 된다는 관점(세 번째 문장), 늘 연결된 디지털 환경에서의 외로움(네 번째 문장)이 있습니다. 반대 측면, 예를 들어 사회적 고립이 건강에 해롭다는 점도 함께 다루면 균형 잡힌 글이 됩니다. 연구 결과를 언급할 때는 구체적 수치를 지어내지 말고 일반적 경향으로 서술하세요.
sampleThesis: Solitude and loneliness are often confused, yet one is a chosen withdrawal that sharpens thought while the other is an unwanted absence that dulls it; a healthy life needs the first in order to avoid the second.
Constant connection has not cured loneliness but disguised it, because being surrounded by others is no substitute for being known by them.
The capacity to be alone is not a retreat from relationships but a condition for good ones, since people who are comfortable with themselves ask less of others and offer more.

prompts: Ambition is a fire: it warms the house or burns it down, depending on where it is lit.
A modest goal fully reached may teach more than a great one half-attempted.
Ambition without patience is only impatience in better clothes.
We admire ambition in those who succeed and call it vanity in those who do not.
Much of what we call ambition is borrowed from expectations we never examined.
essays.approach_ko: 의대 지원자가 자주 받는 주제 유형이므로 자기 동기에 대한 정직한 성찰이 강점이 됩니다. 각도로는 야망이 건설적일지 파괴적일지는 방향에 달려 있다는 관점(첫 번째 문장), 결과에 따라 같은 야망이 다르게 평가되는 이중 잣대(네 번째 문장), 부모나 사회의 기대를 자신의 야망으로 착각하는 문제(다섯 번째 문장)가 있습니다. 다섯 번째 문장은 의대 진학 동기와 연결해 '내 목표는 정말 나의 것인가'를 성찰하는 글로 쓰기 좋습니다. 다만 자기소개서처럼 의사가 되고 싶은 이유를 늘어놓는 글이 되지 않도록 주의하세요. 채점자는 지원 동기가 아니라 주제에 대한 사고의 질을 봅니다.
sampleThesis: Ambition is worth having only once we have examined where it came from, because a goal borrowed from others' expectations can drive us hard in a direction we never chose.
Our judgement of ambition is distorted by outcomes: we call it vision when it succeeds and vanity when it fails, though the drive behind both may be identical.
The most durable ambition is patient, preferring goals that can be fully achieved and built upon over grand plans that are abandoned halfway.

prompts: To forgive is to stop asking the past to pay a debt it has no means to settle.
An apology offered too quickly can be a way of ending the conversation.
We forgive strangers more readily than those we love, because we expected less of them.
Some wrongs are forgiven only after the person who forgives has changed.
A grudge is a ledger that only the injured party keeps open.
essays.approach_ko: 용서를 상대를 위한 행위로 볼지, 용서하는 사람 자신을 위한 행위로 볼지가 중요한 축입니다. 각도로는 용서가 과거가 아니라 그 무게를 누가 지느냐를 바꾼다는 관점(첫 번째 문장), 성급한 사과가 책임을 회피하는 수단이 될 수 있다는 점(두 번째 문장), 가까운 사람일수록 용서가 어려운 이유(세 번째 문장), 용서에 시간이 필요하다는 점(네 번째 문장)이 있습니다. 용서를 강요하는 것이 피해자에게 또 다른 부담이 될 수 있다는 반대 측면도 다루면 깊이가 생깁니다. 의료 현장의 사과와 오류 공개 문화로 확장하는 것도 가능합니다. 지나치게 감상적인 어조나 종교적 설교처럼 들리는 결론은 피하세요.
sampleThesis: Forgiveness cannot rewrite the past, but it can release the injured person from carrying it, which is why it should be offered when the forgiver is ready rather than when the offender asks.
A quick apology often serves the person who gives it more than the person who receives it; genuine reconciliation requires the wrongdoer to stay in the uncomfortable conversation.
We find it hardest to forgive those closest to us precisely because we expected the most of them, so forgiveness within close relationships is less about the act than about revising what we expect.
